title: v1.60.2.0 fix(developer-profile): exclude mode:resources entries from SESSION_COUNT, TIER, and NUDGE_ELIGIBLE
body:
## Summary

Reopens the fix from #1821 (closed for staleness), now **rebased onto current main (v1.57.10.0) → v1.57.11.0** as requested:

> "Closing — this targets v1.55.1.0, which is behind main (now v1.57.0.0), and has merge conflicts. If the developer-profile fix is still relevant, please rebase on current main and reopen. Thanks!"

The fix is still relevant: upstream never touched `bin/gstack-developer-profile` or its test, so both defects are still live on main today. The only conflicts on rebase were version bookkeeping (VERSION/CHANGELOG/package.json), now resolved.

## The bug (deterministic, on the normal /office-hours path)

Every `/office-hours` session writes two profile rows, not one: the real session, plus a `mode:"resources"` bookkeeping row that Phase 6 unconditionally appends (`office-hours/sections/design-and-handoff.md:510`) to dedupe which founder-resource links you've already seen. At the start of the next session the profile is read back (`design-and-handoff.md:278`) to pick the greeting tier and decide whether to fire the builder→founder nudge.

`do_read()` counted those bookkeeping rows as real sessions:

- **`SESSION_COUNT` / `TIER` inflation.** `const count = sessions.length` counted resources rows, so after one real session `SESSION_COUNT` read 2 and tier thresholds (intro=1, welcome_back=2-3, regular=4-7, inner_circle=8+) crossed ~2x too fast. A brand-new user gets greeted as a returning "regular."
- **`NUDGE_ELIGIBLE` armed off bookkeeping.** The predicate `sessions.filter(e => e.mode !== 'startup')` was doubly wrong: it counted resources rows *as builder sessions* and excluded real startup sessions. The builder→founder nudge could fire at someone who never actually came back to build.

This is not undefined behavior or malformed input — gstack's own Phase 6 writes the row every session, and the inflation compounds with each run.

## The fix (`bin/gstack-developer-profile`, `do_read()`)

- Hoist the existing `realSessions = sessions.filter(e => e.mode !== 'resources')` filter above `count`, so `SESSION_COUNT` / `TIER` use it (LAST_*/CROSS_PROJECT/DESIGN_COUNT already did).
- Scope the nudge to `realSessions.filter(e => e.mode === 'builder')` — the nudge is about someone who keeps returning to *build*, so `builder` is the correct predicate. `nudgeEligible = builderSessions >= 3 && totalSignals >= 5` is unchanged.

## Tests (`test/gstack-developer-profile.test.ts`)

- Resources rows don't inflate `SESSION_COUNT` / `TIER` / `NUDGE_ELIGIBLE`.
- Gate boundaries on both `>=` thresholds: 2 builder = false, 3 builder = true, 3 builder / <5 signals = false, 4 real = regular.
- Upper-tier boundary: 7 real = regular, 8 = inner_circle, with resources rows present.
- `CROSS_PROJECT` ignores a trailing resources row on a different project.

42 pass, 0 fail. Full free `bun test` suite is green.

## Adversarial review

An adversarial pass tried to break the fix and could not: verified the bug is reachable on the happy path, confirmed no other field in `do_read()` still double-counts resources rows (signals come from the `signals_accumulated` aggregate; resources rows carry empty `signals`/`topics`/`design_doc`), confirmed the only `mode` values that exist are `startup`/`builder`/`resources` so the predicate change introduces no under-count, confirmed the boundary tests genuinely fail under the old buggy code, and confirmed an all-resources degenerate profile is safe (no throw). Verdict: sound.

## CI note

This is a fork PR, so the eval/E2E jobs that need base-repo secrets will fail with empty-env auth — expected, not a code issue. The change is code-only (no on-disk state format change, so no upgrade migration needed). The free `bun test` gate is the meaningful one here and it's green.

Closes #1821.

title: update_check: false gates the binary but not the preamble instruction text — upgrade-handling prose ships unconditionally
body:
## Summary

`update_check: false` correctly silences the `gstack-update-check` binary (it exits early and emits nothing), but the **instruction text** that tells the agent how to interpret update-check output still ships in every generated `SKILL.md` preamble. The runtime layer honors the opt-out; the instruction layer does not.

This is the same bug *class* as #1150 (preamble content not gated by a config opt-out), for a different flag (`update_check`) and different content (upgrade-handling prose).

## Why it's a real opt-out, not a misconfig

`update_check` is a first-class config key:
- `bin/gstack-config:41` — documented: `# update_check: true   # false = suppress version check notifications`
- `bin/gstack-config:120` — registered default `true`
- Present in the active-values / known-keys lists (`bin/gstack-config:347,363`)

## The layer disagreement

**Binary (honors the flag):** `bin/gstack-update-check:32-34` reads `update_check`, and on `false` exits 0 with no output before any version logic.

**Instruction text (ignores the flag):** `scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-upgrade-check.ts:8,10` unconditionally emit:

```
If output shows `UPGRADE_AVAILABLE <old> <new>`: read .../gstack-upgrade/SKILL.md and follow the "Inline upgrade flow" ...
If output shows `JUST_UPGRADED <from> <to>`: print "Running gstack v{to} (just updated!)" ...
```

These render into every skill's preamble regardless of the flag.

## Inconsistency with every other config flag

Every other runtime flag follows an **echo-then-gate** convention — `generate-preamble-bash.ts` echoes the value (`PROACTIVE:`, `SKILL_PREFIX:`, `EXPLAIN_LEVEL:`, `QUESTION_TUNING:`) and the instruction layer gates on it. `update_check` is the only flag with **no echoed signal and no instruction-layer gate**.

## Impact

Functionally the upgrade check *is* suppressed — the binary emits nothing, so the conditional is vacuously false and the agent takes no upgrade action. The residual cost is:

- ~13 lines of dead upgrade-handling instructions in every preamble for users who opted out.
- The model still reads and visibly "considers" upgrade state, which reads to the user as the check still firing.
- Convention drift: opt-out should mean opt-out at both layers (the principle #1150 is built on).

## Suggested fix (surgical — ~4 lines)

`generateUpgradeCheck()` is misnamed: it bundles four concerns (PROACTIVE, SKILL_PREFIX, upgrade-availability/just-upgraded, feature discovery), so gating the whole function would wrongly disable the proactive/skill-prefix prose. Instead:

1. Echo `UPDATE_CHECK: $_UPDATE_CHECK` in `generate-preamble-bash.ts` alongside the other flags.
2. Gate **only lines 8 and 10** of `generate-upgrade-check.ts` on `UPDATE_CHECK == "true"`.
3. Regenerate via `bun run gen:skill-docs`.

## Secondary note

`update_check: false` also suppresses the post-upgrade `JUST_UPGRADED` "just updated!" confirmation (the binary exits before `:119`). That arguably differs from a "version check notification" — maintainer may want to scope whether the just-upgraded message should survive the opt-out.

body:

Two bodies of work land here, plus the eval-infra plumbing that made the first one provable.

**Hermetic local E2E (the headline).** Every E2E runner that spawns an agent child — `claude -p` (`session-runner`), the real-PTY plan-mode runner (`claude-pty-runner`), the Agent SDK runner, and the `codex`/`gemini` runners — now builds the child's environment through a new `test/helpers/hermetic-env.ts`: an allowlist scrub (process basics + network/proxy + named `ANTHROPIC_*` auth + per-runner `extraAllow`), a fresh seeded `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, a temp `GSTACK_HOME`, and `--strict-mcp-config`. **Eval infra.** `gstack-detach` + `eval:bg*` scripts run long eval jobs in a SIGTERM-proof, `caffeinate`-wrapped session with a machine-wide lock, run-scoped logs, and a guaranteed `EXIT=` sentinel.

title: question-preference-hook returns permissionDecision: "defer" on pass-through paths, interrupting AskUserQuestion cards
body:
## Summary

The `question-preference-hook` currently uses a helper named `defer()` for normal pass-through cases, but that helper returns:

```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
    "permissionDecision": "defer"
  }
}
```

That is not equivalent to "no decision." In Claude Code's current hook contract, `defer` has a specific meaning: pause the tool call so an external caller can resume it later. Claude's docs describe it as intended for `claude -p` / SDK-style integrations, and say it is only honored in non-interactive mode.

For this hook's ordinary no-op paths, gstack should abstain instead: omit `permissionDecision` and optionally include `additionalContext`.

Relevant docs page: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks

## Affected local version

- gstack version: `1.56.0.0`
- gstack commit: `cab774c` (`v1.56.0.0 Token-reduction Phase B + AUQ paranoid safety net (#1849)`)
- Branch: `main`
- Claude Code version observed locally: `2.1.177`
- Hook file: `hosts/claude/hooks/question-preference-hook.ts`
- Hook wiring: `~/.claude/settings.json`, `hooks.PreToolUse`, matcher `(AskUserQuestion|mcp__.*__AskUserQuestion)`

## User-visible symptom

Every `AskUserQuestion` card rendered and then failed with:

> Tool execution was interrupted

It happened regardless of model or conversation context.

The local patch changed only the pass-through helper so it no longer emits `permissionDecision: "defer"`. After that, a real `AskUserQuestion` card rendered and accepted a click successfully.

## Why this has broad impact

This hook is wired to all `AskUserQuestion` calls:

```json
{
  "matcher": "(AskUserQuestion|mcp__.*__AskUserQuestion)",
  "command": "~/.claude/skills/gstack/hosts/claude/hooks/question-preference-hook"
}
```

The helper is used for many normal cases, including:

- empty stdin
- JSON parse failure
- non-`AskUserQuestion` tool names
- questions with no marker
- no saved preference
- `always-ask` preference
- one-way safety override
- ambiguous recommendation parsing
- catch-all error handling

That means users can hit this even with zero saved `/plan-tune` preferences.

## Root cause

In `hosts/claude/hooks/question-preference-hook.ts`, the pass-through helper used to be:

```ts
function defer(additionalContext?: string): void {
  const out: Record<string, unknown> = {
    hookEventName: 'PreToolUse',
    permissionDecision: 'defer',
  };
  if (additionalContext) out.additionalContext = additionalContext;
  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ hookSpecificOutput: out }));
  process.exit(0);
}
```

That code appears to intend "no enforcement, let the question proceed." But `permissionDecision: "defer"` means "pause this tool call for later resume," not "let it proceed normally."

Claude Code docs say:

- PreToolUse supports `allow`, `deny`, `ask`, and `defer`.
- `defer` means the tool call exits with `stop_reason: "tool_deferred"` so an external caller can collect input and resume later.
- `defer` is only honored in non-interactive mode with `claude -p`.
- For no-decision behavior, hooks should omit a decision or return no output.

## Minimal proposed fix

Change the pass-through helper so it emits no `permissionDecision`:

```ts
function defer(additionalContext?: string): void {
  const out: Record<string, unknown> = {
    hookEventName: 'PreToolUse',
  };
  if (additionalContext) out.additionalContext = additionalContext;
  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ hookSpecificOutput: out }));
  process.exit(0);
}
```

The `deny()` helper should stay as-is, because `permissionDecision: "deny"` is valid and is the hook's intended enforcement path.

## Cleaner proposed fix

Rename the helper from `defer()` to something like `passThrough()` or `abstain()` to avoid confusing the hook's "no enforcement" path with Claude Code's real `permissionDecision: "defer"` behavior.

## Tests and docs that likely need updating

Search results in the installed gstack repo show no other live hook implementation still returning `permissionDecision: "defer"` after the local patch, but tests and one design note still expect/document it:

- `test/question-preference-hook.test.ts`
- `test/memory-cache-injection.test.ts`
- `test/skill-e2e-plan-tune-cathedral.test.ts`
- `docs/spikes/claude-code-hook-mutation.md`

Examples:

```ts
expect(r.parsed?.hookSpecificOutput?.permissionDecision).toBe('defer');
```

Those expectations should become one of:

```ts
expect(r.parsed?.hookSpecificOutput?.permissionDecision).toBeUndefined();
```

or, if the helper is changed to exit silently on paths without `additionalContext`, assert empty stdout for pure pass-through cases and assert `additionalContext` only where needed.

## Verification from local incident

Confirmed locally:

- The hook was installed and wired to `AskUserQuestion` in `~/.claude/settings.json`.
- gstack was at `1.56.0.0`, commit `cab774c`.
- Claude Code was `2.1.177`.
- The old helper returned `permissionDecision: "defer"` for normal no-op paths.
- The user had no saved preferences, so the enforcement path was not involved.
- The hook error log was empty, so this was not a hook crash.
- After changing the helper to omit `permissionDecision`, a real `AskUserQuestion` card rendered and accepted a click.

## Suggested labels

- bug
- hooks
- AskUserQuestion
- plan-tune

title: fix(gstack-slug): resolve slug from git remote, not a stale cache
body:
## Problem
`bin/gstack-slug` resolves a project's slug **cache-first** (`~/.gstack/slug-cache/<encoded-path>`) and never re-validates it against the git remote once cached. If the slug is first computed while a repo's `origin` is temporarily wrong — most commonly a project scaffolded by copying another repo before its remote is repointed — the wrong slug gets cached and then **shadows the corrected remote forever**. Every consumer (ship metrics, `/retro`, artifacts, project state) then files under the wrong project slug indefinitely.

## Root cause
Lines 16-19 trust a present cache file verbatim, and the remote is only consulted on a cache miss (line 23). There is no invalidation path, so a stale entry is permanent.

## Fix
Flip resolution to **remote-first**:
1. Derive the slug from `git remote get-url origin` on every run.
2. Fall back to the cached slug (then basename) only when there is no remote.
3. Always refresh the cache to match the resolved slug.

A stale or poisoned cache now self-heals on the next run. For a remote-less repo or a non-repo dir, behavior is unchanged: the cache still provides cross-session stability and is still sanitized on read.

Invariants preserved: `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]` sanitization on every path, atomic cache write via `mktemp` + `mv`, and `pipefail`-safe remote read.

## Verification
- `bash -n` clean.
- Correct resolution for repos with a remote, no-remote dirs (basename fallback), and a repo whose slug had previously been mis-cached.
- **Self-heal:** writing a wrong value into the cache file, then running once, returns and re-caches the correct remote-derived slug.
- **Injection safety:** a malicious cached value (only reachable on a no-remote dir) is sanitized to `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]`, not executed.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(retro): count polyglot test files and exclude vendored dirs
body:
## Problem

`/retro` Step 1 command 10 counts repository test files with a JS/TS-only glob and excludes only `node_modules`:

```bash
find . -name '*.test.*' -o -name '*.spec.*' -o -name '*_test.*' -o -name '*_spec.*' 2>/dev/null | grep -v node_modules | wc -l
```

Python's dominant convention is `test_*.py`, which none of those patterns match, so on a Python repo the `test_health.total_test_files` metric never reflects the real count. Step 13 persists it and Step 12 trends it, so the test-health trend line tracks noise. As #1999 notes, a naive widening over-corrects, because virtualenv / vendored dependency trees (`.venv`, `venv`, `site-packages`, `vendor`) carry their own test suites and only `node_modules` was pruned.

## Fix

- Add the common non-JS conventions: `test_*.py` and `*Test.java`. The existing `*_test.*` / `*_spec.*` already cover Go (`*_test.go`), Ruby (`*_test.rb` / `*_spec.rb`), and Python's `*_test.py`, so the genuine gaps are Python's `test_` prefix and Java's separator-less `FooTest.java`.
- Prune vendored and virtualenv directories (`node_modules`, `.venv`, `venv`, `site-packages`, `vendor`, `.git`) inside `find` instead of post-filtering only `node_modules`, so dependency test suites no longer inflate the count.

## Verification

On a polyglot fixture (5 real project test files across ts/js/go/py/java, plus dependency test files under `.venv/` and `node_modules/`):

| glob | count |
|------|-------|
| old (JS-only, node_modules filter) | 4 (misses `test_*.py` + `*Test.java`, counts a `.venv` test) |
| new | 5 (exact project count) |

`bun test test/gen-skill-docs.test.ts test/skill-validation.test.ts` — 734 pass, 0 fail. SKILL.md regenerated from the template.

The same glob shape also lives in the shared `scripts/resolvers/testing.ts` (the `/ship` before/after counts); left out of scope here to keep this focused on the `/retro` trend metric in #1999.

Closes #1999

title: /autoplan aggregator silently returns 0 tasks: jq scope bug in commit filter
body:
## Summary

`/autoplan`'s Phase 4 Implementation Tasks aggregator returns zero tasks for every invocation because of a jq scope bug. The error is swallowed by `2>/dev/null`, so users see an empty aggregated list with no diagnostic, even when the per-phase `tasks-<phase>-*.jsonl` files contain valid records on the current branch/commit.

Repro'd against `v1.58.1.0` (also affects `v1.52.2.0`).

## Location

`autoplan/SKILL.md:1641` (current `main`):

```jq
select(.branch == $branch and ($commits | split("|") | index(.commit) != null))
```

## Root cause

Inside `index(.commit)`, `.commit` is evaluated against jq's **current input**, which at that point is the array produced by `$commits | split("|")` — NOT the outer record. jq tries to "index the split array by the string `commit`" and errors out:

```
jq: error (at <stdin>:1): Cannot index array with string "commit"
```

The error is suppressed by `2>/dev/null` on the surrounding `jq ... >> "$ALL_JSONL"` invocation, so the aggregator silently drops every record and the user sees:

> _No actionable tasks emitted from any phase._

…even when the JSONL files clearly contain matching records on the current branch and recent commits.

## Repro

```bash
echo '{"branch":"dev","commit":"abc123","phase":"ceo-review"}' | \
  jq --arg branch "dev" --arg commits "abc123|def456" \
  'select(.branch == $branch and ($commits | split("|") | index(.commit) != null))'
# jq: error (at <stdin>:1): Cannot index array with string "commit"
```

Triggered today against `MHVFCU/mhv-member-manager` with two valid JSONL files (12 CEO tasks + 20 Eng tasks, both on `dev`, both with `commit` values present in the last-5-commits filter set). Aggregator output: 0 tasks. After applying the fix below: 32 tasks rendered correctly.

## Fix

Bind the record before the inner pipeline so `.commit` resolves to the record's field, not the split array:

```jq
. as $r | select($r.branch == $branch and ($commits | split("|") | index($r.commit) != null))
```

Equivalent alternative using `IN/1`:

```jq
select(.branch == $branch and (.commit | IN($commits | split("|") | .[])))
```

Both verified working against the same input.

## Suggested patch

Diff against `autoplan/SKILL.md:1641`:

```diff
-      'select(.branch == $branch and ($commits | split("|") | index(.commit) != null))' \
+      '. as $r | select($r.branch == $branch and ($commits | split("|") | index($r.commit) != null))' \
```

## Why this matters

Every `/autoplan` run is currently shipping an empty `### Implementation Tasks (aggregated across phases)` section at the Final Approval Gate. Users either:
1. Don't notice (and lose the aggregated checklist value that /autoplan promises), or
2. Notice and have to re-aggregate by hand.

The `2>/dev/null` masks the actual jq error from anyone running with verbose shells, which makes this near-impossible to diagnose without dropping the redirect.

## Related: defensive improvement

While you're in there, consider dropping the `2>/dev/null` on the per-file `jq` invocation OR teeing stderr to a debug file. The current silent-error pattern hides not just this bug but any future malformed-JSONL case.

Repro environment: macOS 15.5, jq 1.7.1, bash 5.x, zsh 5.x. Bug is jq-version-independent (it's a scope/parsing issue, not a version-specific behavior change).

title: Orphan terminal-agent.ts bun processes + visible conhost windows accumulate on Windows
body:
### Summary

On Windows, every gstack session that spawns a `terminal-agent.ts` daemon leaves behind a visible `conhost.exe` window. When a Claude Code / gstack session ends abruptly (window closed via X, crash, force-kill), the `bun.exe` daemon and its `conhost.exe` survive and accumulate over time. After a few days of daily use I had 3 orphan processes from old sessions, each with a visible terminal window.

### Repro

1. Windows 11, Claude Code with gstack installed.
2. Run any `/browse` command — gstack spawns `bun run terminal-agent.ts` via `terminal-agent-control.ts:71` (`Bun.spawn(['bun', 'run', script], { stdio: ['ignore', 'ignore', 'ignore'] })` with `proc.unref()`).
3. A visible `conhost.exe` window opens (Windows default for console subprocesses).
4. Close the Claude Code window without `/exit` (or let it crash).
5. `Get-Process bun` shows the agent still running; the conhost window is still visible.
6. Repeat over several sessions → orphans pile up.

In my install:

```
> Get-Content ~/.gstack/terminal-agent-pid
{"pid":27492,"gen":"...","startedAt":1780844984663}   # tracked agent (8 days old, long dead)

> Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='bun.exe'"
PID 31700, 37116, 37272   # all running terminal-agent.ts, none tracked
```

Three live daemons, none in the pid-record. The current spawn site only kills the one PID recorded in `terminal-agent-pid` (via `killAgentByRecord` in `terminal-agent-control.ts:65-68`), so orphans from prior crashed sessions are never reaped.

### Two issues, two fixes

**1. Orphan accumulation.** `spawnTerminalAgent` reads the pid-record and kills only that one PID. Anything from a prior session that wasn't cleanly torn down survives. Suggested fix: at boot, after killing the recorded PID, scan for additional bun processes running `terminal-agent.ts` whose owner matches (current uid / SID) and whose parent process is dead, and reap those too. Identity-based (the v1.44 design) is preserved — we'd still never touch a sibling gstack session whose parent is alive.

**2. Visible conhost windows on Windows.** `Bun.spawn` accepts a `windowsHide: true` option (Bun >= 1.0.x on Windows) that suppresses the conhost window for console subprocesses. The `terminal-agent` is fully headless (`stdio: ['ignore', 'ignore', 'ignore']`), so hiding its window has no UX downside. Adding `windowsHide: true` to the `Bun.spawn` call in `terminal-agent-control.ts:71` (and any other detached-daemon spawn sites) would eliminate the window-popup symptom entirely.

### Workaround I'm using locally

A SessionStart hook that runs the following PowerShell:

```powershell
$tracked = (Get-Content ~/.gstack/terminal-agent-pid -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).pid
Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='bun.exe'" |
  Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like '*terminal-agent.ts*' -and $_.ProcessId -ne $tracked } |
  ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force }
```

This catches the orphan-accumulation issue but doesn't help with the initial conhost popup.

### Why upstream and not just local

The local hook is a band-aid. The right fix is identity-aware orphan reaping at agent-boot (so it works for every Windows gstack user out of the box) plus `windowsHide: true` so the conhost windows never appear in the first place. Happy to send a PR if you'd like — wanted to file the issue first to confirm the approach.

### Env

- OS: Windows 11 Pro 26200
- gstack: v1.57.7.0 (commit 1626d48)
- Bun: 1.3.14
- Claude Code: Opus 4.7

title: one-way-doors: revoke/reset credential patterns miss nouns rotate has — 'reset my secret' leaks through as two-way
body:
## Observed problem

`scripts/one-way-doors.ts` is the secondary keyword safety net for AskUserQuestion calls that fire without a registry id. Its three credential patterns are meant to be parallel across `revoke`/`reset`/`rotate` (the inline comment says they "allow filler words between verb and noun", and the test header for #1839 states "the credential-rotation patterns must be parallel across revoke/reset/rotate").

They are not. The noun alternations differ:

```
/\brevoke\s+[\w\s]*\b(api key|token|credential|access key|password)\b/i,        // missing: secret
/\breset\s+[\w\s]*\b(api key|token|password|credential)\b/i,                     // missing: secret, access key
/\brotate\s+[\w\s]*\b(api key|token|secret|credential|access key|password)\b/i, // complete
```

So a destructive credential operation phrased with the "wrong" verb/noun pair classifies as **two-way** (auto-decidable) instead of one-way (always ask). This is a false-negative in a safety net — the exact failure class #1839 fixed for `rotate ... password`.

## Current behavior on upstream `main` (c7ae6320, v1.58.1.0)

```
$ bun -e 'import {classifyQuestion} from "./scripts/one-way-doors.ts"; ...'
two-way   revoke my secret      <- should be one-way
two-way   reset my secret       <- should be one-way
two-way   reset my access key   <- should be one-way
ONE-WAY   rotate my secret
```

## Expected behavior

`revoke`/`reset`/`rotate` should share an identical credential noun list, so every `<verb> my <noun>` combination across {api key, token, secret, credential, access key, password} classifies as one-way.

## Duplicate searches performed

- open PRs and issues touching `one-way-doors` / "one-way door" — none cover this (only #1839/#1911 fixed `rotate ... password`, which is already on main)
- searched open PRs for "revoke reset rotate" and the credential-noun subsystem — no collision
- confirmed the existing `test/one-way-doors.test.ts` only checks the non-password nouns against `rotate`, never against `revoke`/`reset`

## Candidate fix shape

Unify the noun alternation across all three verbs (add `secret` to `revoke`; add `secret` and `access key` to `reset`), and extend the regression test to assert every verb × noun pair is one-way.

title: fix(one-way-doors): unify credential noun list across revoke/reset/rotate
body:
## Problem

`scripts/one-way-doors.ts` is the secondary keyword safety net for AskUserQuestion calls that fire without a registry id. A false negative here auto-approves a destructive op (the question is treated as two-way / preference-suppressible instead of one-way / always-ask).

Its three credential patterns are meant to be parallel across `revoke`/`reset`/`rotate` (the inline comment says they "allow filler words between verb and noun"; the `#1839` test header states the patterns "must be parallel across revoke/reset/rotate"). They were not:

```
revoke: api key | token |          credential | access key | password   (missing: secret)
reset:  api key | token |          credential |              password   (missing: secret, access key)
rotate: api key | token | secret | credential | access key | password   (complete)
```

## Root cause

`secret` lived only in the `rotate` alternation, and `access key` was absent from `reset`. So these phrasings slipped through as two-way on `main` (c7ae6320, v1.58.1.0):

```
two-way   revoke my secret      <- should be one-way
two-way   reset my secret       <- should be one-way
two-way   reset my access key   <- should be one-way
ONE-WAY   rotate my secret
```

This is the same false-negative class `#1839` fixed for `rotate ... password`; that fix unified one verb's nouns but left `revoke`/`reset` short.

## Fix

Give all three verbs an identical credential noun alternation (`api key | token | secret | credential | access key | password`). Pure widening of an over-narrow safety net: no previously-caught phrasing stops matching, and the additions are conservative (a credential verb + credential noun is exactly what this net is for).

## Testing

`bun test test/one-way-doors.test.ts` — 4 pass, 28 assertions. Added a regression test asserting every `<verb> my <noun>` pair across all three verbs and all six nouns classifies one-way; it fails on `main` for the three cases above and passes with this change.

Fixes #2024

title: design variants: --count silently generates zero variants on NaN/0/negative input
body:
### Observed problem

`design variants --count <bad value>` silently produces **zero** variants and emits a confusing JSON result instead of failing or clamping to a sane value.

The CLI parses the flag with `parseInt` and no validation (`design/src/cli.ts:200`):

```ts
count: flags.count ? parseInt(flags.count as string) : 3,
```

`variants()` then only clamps the **upper** bound (`design/src/variants.ts:156`):

```ts
const count = Math.min(options.count, 7); // Cap at 7 style variations
```

There is no lower-bound or NaN guard, so non-numeric / zero / negative counts flow straight through.

### Current behavior on `main` (c7ae6320)

Reproduced against the real clamp + JSON-emit path:

| `--count` | parsed | clamped | variants generated | JSON `count` field |
|-----------|--------|---------|--------------------|--------------------|
| `abc`     | `NaN`  | `NaN`   | 0                  | `null`             |
| `0`       | `0`    | `0`     | 0                  | `0`                |
| `-2`      | `-2`   | `-2`    | 0                  | `-2`               |
| `3`       | `3`    | `3`     | 3                  | `3`                |
| `10`      | `10`   | `7`     | 7                  | `7`                |

A typo like `--count e` (NaN) makes the command exit "successfully" having created nothing, and the structured stdout reports `"count": null` — actively misleading for any caller parsing that JSON.

### Expected behavior

A bad `--count` should resolve to a valid number in the supported range, never a silent no-op:
- non-finite (`NaN`) -> fall back to the default of 3
- numeric but out of range -> clamp to `[1, 7]`

So `--count abc` -> 3, `--count 0`/`-2` -> 1, `--count 10` -> 7 (unchanged).

### Duplicate search performed

- Open PRs touching `design/`: #1774 (timeout label only), #1638 (timeout 240s bump), #1528 (`--api-timeout` flag + `parseApiTimeoutMs` guard — validates the *timeout* flag, not `--count`), #1737 (variant preservation). None guard `--count`.
- `gh pr list --search "design count"` -> no matches; `--search "variants"` -> only the timeout PRs above.
- No open/closed issue covers the `--count` validation gap.

### Candidate fix shape

Normalize the count in `variants.ts` via a small exported, unit-testable helper (mirrors the `parseApiTimeoutMs` helper pattern proposed in #1528):

```ts
export function normalizeVariantCount(count: number): number {
  if (!Number.isFinite(count)) return 3;        // unparseable -> default
  return Math.max(1, Math.min(Math.trunc(count), 7)); // clamp to [1, 7]
}
```

Use it where `Math.min(options.count, 7)` is today. Add a regression test asserting the table above.

title: AskUserQuestion silently broken: PreToolUse hook emits permissionDecision:'defer' → 'Tool result missing due to internal error'
/careful fails open on chained rm: 'rm -rf /; rm -rf node_modules' is silently allowed
body:
### Summary

The `/careful` PreToolUse hook (`careful/bin/check-careful.sh`) fails open on chained `rm -r` commands: a destructive recursive delete is silently allowed when the command is chained with a second `rm` that targets a build-artifact directory.

### Observed problem

The "safe exception" block (lines 28-48) whitelists `rm -rf` of build artifacts (`node_modules`, `dist`, `.next`, etc.). It extracts the rm targets with a single greedy expression:

```sh
RM_ARGS=$(printf '%s' "$CMD" | sed -E 's/.*rm[[:space:]]+(-[a-zA-Z]+[[:space:]]+)*//;s/--recursive[[:space:]]*//')
```

`.*rm` matches greedily, so for a chained command it only ever inspects the targets of the **last** `rm` in the string. If that final rm targets a safe directory, the whole command is whitelisted and the hook returns `{}` (allow) without warning, even though an earlier rm in the chain is destructive.

### Current behavior on upstream `main` (c7ae6320)

```
$ printf '{"tool_input":{"command":"rm -rf /; rm -rf node_modules"}}' | bash careful/bin/check-careful.sh
{}
```

No warning. The `rm -rf /` is waved through because the greedy extraction only sees the trailing `node_modules`.

Reversing the order (safe rm first, dangerous rm last) correctly warns, which confirms the asymmetry is caused by the last-rm-only extraction:

```
$ printf '{"tool_input":{"command":"rm -rf node_modules; rm -rf /home/user/data"}}' | bash careful/bin/check-careful.sh
{"permissionDecision":"ask","message":"[careful] Destructive: recursive delete (rm -r). This permanently removes files."}
```

### Expected behavior

Any chained command containing a destructive recursive `rm` should warn (`permissionDecision: "ask"`), regardless of where the safe rm sits in the chain. Single-command artifact cleanups (`rm -rf node_modules`, `rm -rf .next dist`) should still be allowed.

### Candidate fix shape

The target-extraction shortcut is only reliable for a single `rm` invocation. Gate the safe-exception so it applies only when the command has no shell separator (`;`, `|`, `&`, newline). When a separator is present, fall through to the existing destructive-pattern check, which already warns on any `rm -r`. This is the fail-safe direction for a guard and preserves the single-command artifact-cleanup convenience.

### Duplicate searches performed

- Open PRs touching `careful/bin/check-careful.sh`: #1110 (text-output false positives — over-warning, the opposite direction; it splits on `&&`/`||` but turns `;` into a space and re-feeds the same greedy safe-exception, so it does not fix this) and #1509 (hook activation gate + `hookSpecificOutput` shape — does not touch the detection logic).
- Open issues: #1060 (false positives in commit messages — over-warning), #1091 (broad proposal to add structured execution judgment). Neither covers this fail-open.
- Verified the bug reproduces on current `main` (c7ae6320).

title: fix(careful): warn on chained rm even when the last target is safe
body:
Fixes #2039

## Problem

The `/careful` PreToolUse hook fails open on chained `rm -r` commands. Its "safe exception" block (whitelisting `rm -rf` of build artifacts like `node_modules`, `dist`, `.next`) extracts the rm targets with a single greedy match:

```sh
RM_ARGS=$(printf '%s' "$CMD" | sed -E 's/.*rm[[:space:]]+(-[a-zA-Z]+[[:space:]]+)*//;...')
```

`.*rm` is greedy, so it only inspects the **last** `rm` in the command. A chain whose final rm targets a safe directory gets the whole command whitelisted, so a destructive earlier rm is silently allowed:

```
$ printf '{"tool_input":{"command":"rm -rf /; rm -rf node_modules"}}' | bash careful/bin/check-careful.sh
{}        # no warning — rm -rf / waved through
```

Reversing the order correctly warns, confirming the cause is the last-rm-only extraction.

## Root cause

The target-extraction shortcut is only reliable for a single `rm` invocation. With a chained command, the greedy match collapses to the final rm's arguments and ignores everything before it.

## Fix

Gate the safe-exception so it only applies to a single rm command. When any shell separator is present (`;`, `|`, `&`, real newline, or the JSON-escaped `\n`/`\r` that survives the grep extraction path as a literal two-char sequence), skip the shortcut and fall through to the existing destructive-pattern check, which already warns on any `rm -r`. This is the fail-safe direction for a safety guard, and single-command artifact cleanups (`rm -rf node_modules`, `rm -rf .next dist`) still allow.

## Testing

`bun test test/hook-scripts.test.ts` — 35 pass, 0 fail (3 new regression tests for semicolon and `&&` chains in both orders; existing safe-exception and mixed-target tests unchanged).

Verified before/after:

| command | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `rm -rf /; rm -rf node_modules` | `{}` (allowed) | `ask` |
| `rm -rf /etc/data && rm -rf dist` | `{}` (allowed) | `ask` |
| `rm -rf node_modules` (single safe) | `{}` | `{}` |
| `rm -rf .next dist` (single safe) | `{}` | `{}` |
| `rm -rf /var/data` (single dangerous) | `ask` | `ask` |

## Not a duplicate

Distinct from the other open `check-careful.sh` PRs: #1110 targets text-output false positives (over-warning, opposite direction — it turns `;` into a space and re-feeds the same greedy safe-exception, so it does not address this), and #1509 changes hook activation + output shape, not the detection logic.

## Notes

External-fork CI: the eval/E2E and report jobs may fail on missing secrets for a fork PR; the changed test (`test/hook-scripts.test.ts`) is a free deterministic gate-tier test and passes locally.

title: fix(redact): detect GitLab, Hugging Face, npm, DigitalOcean, GCP, and Bearer tokens (#1946)
body:
## What changed and why

`lib/redact-patterns.ts` missed several common credential token types, so the redaction guard would let them slip past `gstack-redact` (and the pre-push hook) without warning. This adds detection for:

| id | tier | shape |
|----|------|-------|
| `gitlab.pat` | HIGH | `glpat-` / `glptt-` / `gldt-` (PAT, pipeline-trigger, deploy) |
| `huggingface.token` | HIGH | `hf_…` |
| `npm.token` | HIGH | `npm_…` (36 chars) |
| `digitalocean.token` | HIGH | `dop_v1_…` (64 hex) |
| `gcp.service_account_key` | HIGH | JSON-escaped `"private_key": "-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----"` (the `\n`-escaped form the existing `pem.private_key` block misses) |
| `http.bearer` | MEDIUM | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |

Calibration follows the existing taxonomy philosophy: distinctive, low-false-positive prefixes go HIGH (block); `Bearer` is intentionally MEDIUM because bare `Bearer <token>` appears constantly in API docs and example curl commands. It carries a validator (length + Shannon entropy ≥ 3.5 + non-placeholder, reusing the existing `isPlaceholderSpan` / `shannonEntropy` helpers) so example headers and `Bearer ${VAR}` placeholders don't fire.

This is the **detection-coverage** slice of #1946 only. The separate pre-push-guard-install concern in that issue is intentionally out of scope here (it's a different surface, already being handled in another PR).

Fixes #1946 (token-detection portion).

## How to test

```bash
bun test test/redact-engine.test.ts
```

All new patterns have a positive-match assertion; `http.bearer` additionally asserts placeholder/low-entropy rejection. 64 pass / 0 fail.

## Duplicate check

No open or merged PR adds these token patterns to `lib/redact-patterns.ts` (the only other redact PR in flight, #1962, covers pre-push-hook installation, a disjoint surface).

## Notes / scope

- No regex is vulnerable to ReDoS (anchored, linear); `test/redact-pattern-lint` stays green.
- `bun run gen:skill-docs` produces no SKILL.md changes — the taxonomy doc table is tier/category-level, not per-pattern.

title: fix(resolvers): correct design/browse/make-pdf fallback path on env-var hosts (#1159)
body:
## What changed and why

On env-var hosts (codex, hermes — `usesEnvVars: true`), the design/browse/make-pdf setup blocks computed their global fallback path as `"$HOME${dir.replace(/^~/, '')}"`. That only strips a leading `~`. For these hosts the dir is already an exported absolute root (`$GSTACK_DESIGN` / `$GSTACK_BROWSE` / `$GSTACK_MAKE_PDF`), so the `~`-strip was a no-op and `$HOME` got prepended anyway, emitting an invalid path like `$HOME$GSTACK_DESIGN/design`. That never resolves, so the binaries were reported `DESIGN_NOT_AVAILABLE` even when installed.

This extracts a single `runtimeFallbackPath(dir, bin)` helper in `scripts/resolvers/types.ts` that uses `$`-rooted dirs verbatim and only substitutes `$HOME` for a leading `~`. All five fallback sites (design x2, browse, make-pdf) route through it.

- codex/hermes before: `D="$HOME$GSTACK_DESIGN/design"` (broken)
- codex/hermes after: `D="$GSTACK_DESIGN/design"` (correct)
- claude before/after: `D="$HOME/.claude/skills/gstack/design/dist/design"` (byte-identical, unaffected)

Fixes #1159.

## How to test

```bash
bun test test/runtime-fallback-path.test.ts
```

32 pass / 0 fail. Covers the helper directly plus the generated design/browse/make-pdf setup blocks for every env-var host (asserts no `$HOME$GSTACK_*` shape) and a Claude-unaffected guard.

## Duplicate check

No open or merged PR touches the design/browse/make-pdf fallback path resolution.

## Notes / scope

- Committed docs (Claude host) are unchanged, so `bun run gen:skill-docs` yields no SKILL.md diff (codex/hermes docs are generated at install time).
- Kept tight to the confirmed root cause. A commenter suggested also adding `design/dist`/`make-pdf/dist` to hermes `globalSymlinks`; that is not the cause here (`$GSTACK_DESIGN` already points at the real on-disk location, and the working Claude host omits those symlinks too), so it's intentionally left out.

title: fix(setup-deploy): presence-check Render key instead of printing key bytes (#1078)
body:
## What changed and why

The setup-deploy skill instructed `echo $RENDER_API_KEY | head -c 4` to check whether the key was set. Even though the intent was "presence only," it still writes the first 4 bytes of a live secret into terminal scrollback, screen recordings, and screenshots — and skill instructions tend to get copied downstream once they ship.

This replaces it with a presence check that writes zero key bytes:

```bash
if [ -n "${RENDER_API_KEY:-}" ]; then echo "RENDER_API_KEY: set"; else echo "RENDER_API_KEY: not set"; fi
```

Edited in `setup-deploy/SKILL.md.tmpl` (the source of truth) and regenerated `setup-deploy/SKILL.md`. This was the only partial-secret-print instance in the skill.

Fixes #1078.

## How to test

```bash
bun test test/skill-validation.test.ts
```

Adds a static guard asserting that setup-deploy (template + generated) never pipes a provider `API_KEY` into `head`/`cut` or slices it via `${KEY:N:M}`. Verified the guard fails red if the old `head -c 4` pattern is reintroduced. 334 pass / 0 fail.

## Duplicate check

No open or merged PR touches setup-deploy or the Render key check.

title: v1.58.3.0 feat: gbrowser anti-detection Layer C stealth
body:
## Summary

Ships always-on "Layer C" anti-detection stealth for GBrowser, replacing the prior webdriver-only default. (Also merges `origin/main` up to v1.58.1.0; the VERSION/CHANGELOG/docs commits are bookkeeping.)

**Stealth engine (`browse/src/stealth.ts`)**
- `buildStealthScript`: always-on Layer C init script — webdriver mask, `window.chrome.{runtime,app,csi,loadTimes}` shape, `Notification.permission` alignment, per-install `hardwareConcurrency`/`deviceMemory`, a `Function.prototype.toString` proxy that holds up under the depth-3 `[native code]` check, and a static sweep of Selenium/Phantom/Nightmare/Playwright globals.
- `buildGStackLaunchArgs`: per-install `--gstack-*` cmdline switches (GPU vendor/renderer, UA-CH platform/model, hw concurrency/memory) for gbrowser's Pack 1 C++ patches, emitted only when the matching `GSTACK_*` env is set (no-op on stock Chromium).
- `applyStealth` blends Layer C (always) + a shared `cdc_`/Permissions cleanup shim + opt-in `GSTACK_STEALTH=extended` (WebGL spoof, faked plugins, mediaDevices) layered on top. `--gstack-suppress-prepare-stack-trace` is opt-in via `GSTACK_CDP_STEALTH=on`.

**Launch integration (`browse/src/browser-manager.ts`)**
- Stealth applies on all four context-creation paths: `launch`, `launchHeaded`, `handoff`, and `recreateContext` (the `useragent` / `viewport --scale` rebuild). The shared `STEALTH_LAUNCH_ARGS` / `STEALTH_IGNORE_DEFAULT_ARGS` constants are spread into each path.

**Tests**
- 80 stealth tests (static shape + real-Chromium runtime): webdriver, chrome.* shape, Notification/Permissions pairing, toString depth-3, per-install hardware, extended-mode blend, `readHostProfile` clamp, plus static tripwires asserting every context path applies stealth.

## Test Coverage

AI-assessed coverage: **89%** (gate: 80% target — PASS). Dedicated stealth suite: **80 tests passing** (real Chromium for the runtime checks). Full free suite green (browse/test + test + make-pdf/test, 0 failures).

4 documented gaps, none blocking: 2 are live-only (the `--gstack-*` C++ patch consumers, verified out-of-repo in gbrowser's `anti-bot.test.sh`; in-repo only asserts the switches are built), 1 is a defensive CSP catch branch, 1 is the inline UA-string assembly. Everything in the JS stealth path has runtime coverage.

## Pre-Landing Review

Specialist army (testing, maintainability, security, performance) + cross-model adversarial (Claude + Codex):
- **Security: no findings.** The script-injection boundary was verified safe — env values pass through `Number()` + `isFinite` + `>0` clamp before page-world interpolation (only bare numeric literals survive), and cmdline values reach Chromium via an argv array (no shell). A "trusted-source only" comment now documents the load-bearing assumption.
- **Performance: no findings.** The `toString` proxy is an accepted O(1)-per-call tradeoff; no quadratic or sync-I/O patterns.
- **Testing (6) + Maintainability (4): all informational, all addressed** — added `readHostProfile` clamp, toString depth-3, and `chrome.csi()`/`loadTimes()` invocation tests; dropped a dead `HostProfile.platform` field; corrected stale comments; documented the extended-mode coexistence limitations.
- **Adversarial (Codex) caught a HIGH the other passes missed:** `recreateContext()` — reached by routine `useragent` / `viewport --scale` commands — rebuilt the context without re-applying stealth, silently un-masking every restored page. Fixed in both the main and fallback paths, and the launch-path tripwire now asserts all four context-creation paths apply stealth so the regression class can't recur.

## Design Review

No frontend files changed — design review skipped.

## Eval Results

No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped.

## Scope Drift

Scope Check: CLEAN. Stated intent (anti-detection stealth) matches the delivered diff; no creep, no missing requirements.

## Plan Completion

No plan file detected for this branch.

## Verification Results

No localhost dev server (this is a browser library). Live anti-bot verification lives in gbrowser's out-of-repo `anti-bot.test.sh`; runtime behavior is covered by the real-Chromium tests in this PR.

## TODOS

No TODO items completed in this PR. The "Anti-bot stealth: Playwright CDP patches" TODO had a stale premise ("masks `navigator.webdriver` only") that was corrected to reflect Layer C; the CDP-protocol-layer work itself remains open.

## Documentation

Synced browser anti-detection docs to the shipped "Layer C" stealth (v1.58.3.0).

- **BROWSER.md**: Rewrote the "Stealth scope" section (was "masks `navigator.webdriver` only") to describe always-on Layer C across all four context-creation paths: webdriver mask, `window.chrome.*` shape, `Notification.permission`/Permissions alignment, per-install `hardwareConcurrency`/`deviceMemory`, the `Function.prototype.toString` proxy, and the automation-global sweep. Documented `GSTACK_STEALTH=extended` (also `1`/`true`), the Pack 1 `--gstack-*` switches, the Pack 2/B11 `GSTACK_CDP_STEALTH=on` → `--gstack-suppress-prepare-stack-trace`, and `ignoreDefaultArgs` stripping. Corrected "What GStack Browser means" to note the stock-Chrome UA (no `GStackBrowser` suffix, itself a tell) and that CDP-layer detection can still trigger captchas. title: gstack misclassifies a gbrain thin-client (remote-HTTP MCP, no local engine) as broken-config, suppressing brain-aware planning blocks
body:
## Summary

On a machine where gbrain runs as a **thin-client** — the engine lives on a remote host and the agent talks to it purely over a remote-HTTP MCP server, with no local Postgres/PGLite engine — `./setup` prints:

```
gbrain not detected — brain-aware blocks suppressed in planning-skill SKILL.md files.
```

and `gstack-config gbrain-refresh` reports `local-status: broken-config`. The brain is fully functional over MCP (reads/writes work in-session), but gstack decides it's absent and strips the brain-aware blocks from the planning skills (office-hours, plan-ceo-review, etc.).

## Root cause

Two independent assumptions in the detector both assume a **local** engine and a **hardcoded MCP name**:

**1. `detectMcpMode()` in `bin/gstack-gbrain-detect` hardcodes the MCP server name `gbrain`.**
All three tiers look up a server literally named `gbrain`:
- `claude mcp get gbrain --json`
- grep for `^gbrain:` in `claude mcp list`
- `mcpServers.gbrain` in `~/.claude.json`

A thin-client whose MCP server is registered under any other name returns `gbrain_mcp_mode: "none"`, even though a perfectly good remote-HTTP gbrain MCP is connected.

**2. `freshClassify()` in `lib/gbrain-local-status.ts` only probes a local engine.**
It runs `gbrain sources list --json` against a local DB. On a thin-client there is no local `database_url`, so the probe fails and the function hits its defensive default:

```ts
// Defensive default per codex #8: unrecognized failures classify as
// broken-config so the user sees the raw stderr surfaced upstream.
return "broken-config";
```

There is no state representing "no local engine, but a healthy remote brain over MCP."

Combined, a legitimate thin-client lands on `mcp_mode: none` + `local_status: broken-config` → "gbrain not detected" → brain-aware blocks suppressed, despite the brain being live.

## Impact

Thin-client / remote-engine setups (a documented gbrain topology) silently lose brain-aware planning in gstack, with a misleading "broken-config" signal that suggests the user's gbrain install is broken when it isn't.

## Suggested fix

- `detectMcpMode()`: don't hardcode the server name `gbrain`. Detect any MCP server whose endpoint/command resolves to gbrain, or allow the server name to be configured.
- `freshClassify()`: add a state for a healthy remote/thin-client brain (e.g. `remote-ok`). When a remote-HTTP gbrain MCP is present (or the config points at a remote endpoint with no local engine), treat the brain as available and keep the brain-aware blocks, instead of falling through to `broken-config`.

## Environment

- gstack v1.58.3.0
- gbrain v0.42.51.0 (thin-client; remote engine, remote-HTTP MCP)
- macOS

title: /context-restore can load the wrong worktree checkpoint (shared origin-derived slug + newest-across-all-branches restore)
body:
## Summary
With multiple git worktrees of the same repo, `/context-restore` in one worktree
can load a checkpoint saved by a *different* worktree. Two design choices combine.

## Root cause
1. `bin/gstack-slug` derives the slug from `git remote get-url origin`. All
   worktrees of a repo share one origin → same slug → same
   `~/.gstack/projects/<slug>/checkpoints/` dir. (The per-cwd slug cache just
   stores that same shared value under each worktree's path key.)
2. `/context-restore` by default "loads the most recent saved context across ALL
   branches" and explicitly "does NOT filter the candidate set by current branch"
   (per `context-restore` SKILL.md — intentional, for Conductor handoff).

Together: each worktree's `/context-save` writes into the same shared dir, and
`/context-restore` picks the newest file across all branches — which may be
another worktree's.

## Repro
1. Repo with `origin` set; `git worktree add ../repo-b feature-b`.
2. Worktree B: `/context-save` (checkpoint B).
3. Worktree A (older/no checkpoint for its branch): `/context-restore`.
4. A restores B's checkpoint.

## Impact
Cross-worktree context contamination — the agent resumes from the wrong
worktree's state. Most visible in concurrent multi-session/multi-worktree usage.

## Proposed fix (options)
- Default `/context-restore` to branch-scoped selection (filter candidates by
  frontmatter `branch:` == current branch), with an explicit `--all-branches`
  opt-in to keep the cross-branch handoff use case. Checkpoints already record
  `branch:` in frontmatter.
- And/or make the slug worktree-aware so each worktree gets its own checkpoints dir.
- A `--branch <name>` / explicit-path selector for deterministic pinning.

## Related
#1125 (slug derivation), #1191 (concurrent same-repo state), #1161 (repo-local artifacts)

Environment: gstack 1.48.0.0

title: fix(context-restore): prefer the current branch's own checkpoint (#2052)
body:
## Problem

All worktrees of a repo share one `origin`-derived slug (`bin/gstack-slug` keys off `git remote get-url origin`), so they all resolve to the same `~/.gstack/projects/<slug>/checkpoints/` directory. `/context-restore` Step 1 then loaded the **newest checkpoint across the whole directory, regardless of branch**:

```bash
FILES=$(find "$CHECKPOINT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name "*.md" -type f | sort -r | head -20)
```

With multiple live worktrees, that means `/context-restore` in worktree A could silently restore a checkpoint saved by worktree B — cross-worktree context contamination (issue #2052).

## Fix

Step 1 now orders candidates **current-branch-first**, reading each file's `branch:` frontmatter, and keeps other-branch checkpoints as a *fallback* rather than dropping them. A git branch is checked out in at most one worktree, so preferring the current branch's own checkpoint cleanly separates worktrees.

Crucially this **preserves the documented Conductor cross-branch handoff**: when the current branch has no checkpoint of its own, the full newest-first set across all branches is still used — exactly the old behavior. The change only stops a *newer sibling-worktree save* from shadowing a branch that does have its own checkpoint.

Details:
- scan the 200 newest before partitioning, so a current-branch checkpoint sitting below a burst of sibling saves is still found; the result is still capped at 20
- non-git / detached-HEAD / branchless legacy saves fall back to the old newest-first behavior (back-compat), and no checkpoint is ever dropped from the candidate set

This implements the issue's first proposed option (branch-scoped default + cross-branch fallback) without flipping the default to a hard branch filter, so the Conductor handoff use case keeps working with no new flag.

## Testing

`bun test test/context-save-hardening.test.ts` → **26 pass** (21 existing + 5 new).

New regression tests in the existing `context-restore: ...` harness (they exercise the exact Step-1 shell pipeline):
- the bug: a current-branch save is **not** shadowed by a newer sibling-worktree save (fails on the old pipeline)
- fallback: current branch has no checkpoint → newest across all branches (Conductor handoff)
- back-compat: empty/non-git current branch → newest across all
- branchless legacy saves still rank as fallback, never lost
- within the current branch, ordering stays newest-first

Regenerated `context-restore/SKILL.md` and `scripts/proactive-suggestions.json` via `bun run gen:skill-docs` (all three hosts); generated docs are fresh.

Branched from `main` at `a861c00c`.

Fixes #2052

title: Non-Claude hosts: binary-resolver fallback doubles $HOME ($HOME$GSTACK_BROWSE), browse/design/make-pdf never resolve
body:
## Summary

For every non-Claude host that uses `$GSTACK_*` env-var paths (codex, factory, cursor, opencode, slate, kiro, hermes, gbrain), the **binary-resolver fallback** in the generated `SKILL.md` files prepends `$HOME` to a path that is *already* absolute, producing a doubled-home path that never resolves.

Example from `~/.codex/skills/gstack-qa/SKILL.md`:

```bash
GSTACK_ROOT="$HOME/.codex/skills/gstack"
GSTACK_BROWSE="$GSTACK_ROOT/browse/dist"
...
[ -z "$B" ] && B="$HOME$GSTACK_BROWSE/browse"     # ← $HOME doubled
```

`$HOME$GSTACK_BROWSE` expands to `/Users/me/Users/me/.codex/skills/gstack/browse/dist`, so the fallback `[ -x "$B" ]` check fails and the skill reports `NEEDS_SETUP` / `BROWSE_NOT_AVAILABLE` even though the binary is present at the correct path.

## Impact

- Affects the global-install fallback branch only (the repo-local `.agents/skills/...` branch on the line above resolves first), so it bites plain global Codex/Factory/etc. installs, not repo-vendored ones.
- 18 generated skills across the `browse`, `design`, and `make-pdf` setup blocks. Three doubled patterns:
  - `B="$HOME$GSTACK_BROWSE/browse"`
  - `D="$HOME$GSTACK_DESIGN/design"`
  - `P="$HOME$GSTACK_MAKE_PDF/pdf"`

## Root cause

`scripts/resolvers/{browse,design,make-pdf}.ts` build the fallback as:

```ts
B="$HOME${ctx.paths.browseDir.replace(/^~/, '')}/browse"
```

This assumes `browseDir` is `~`-rooted (true for Claude: `~/.claude/skills/gstack/browse/dist`). For env-var hosts `ctx.paths.browseDir` is `"$GSTACK_BROWSE"` (see `scripts/resolvers/types.ts` `buildHostPaths()` → `usesEnvVars` branch), so `.replace(/^~/, '')` is a no-op and `$HOME` gets prepended to an already-absolute value.

## Proposed fix

Add a small helper in `scripts/resolvers/types.ts` and use it at all 6 call sites:

```ts
export function toShellPath(dir: string): string {
  return dir.startsWith('~') ? `$HOME${dir.slice(1)}` : dir;
}
```

Call sites become e.g. `B="${toShellPath(ctx.paths.browseDir)}/browse"`.

- Claude: `~/.claude/.../browse/dist` → `$HOME/.claude/.../browse/dist` (byte-identical to today)
- Env-var hosts: `$GSTACK_BROWSE` passes through untouched → `$GSTACK_BROWSE/browse`

Verified locally: `tsc --noEmit` clean, resolver + make-pdf tests (201) and host-config/golden tests (73) pass, regenerated Codex output now resolves to an existing binary, Claude output unchanged. Golden fixtures unaffected (the `ship` skill has no binary-resolver block).

Affected call sites: `scripts/resolvers/browse.ts:109`, `scripts/resolvers/design.ts:795,803,840`, `scripts/resolvers/make-pdf.ts:22`.

Env: gstack v1.58.3.0, macOS, `./setup --host codex`.

title: gstack-developer-profile --read double-counts mode:"resources" rows into SESSION_COUNT, TIER, and NUDGE_ELIGIBLE
body:
## `gstack-developer-profile --read` double-counts `mode:"resources"` bookkeeping rows into SESSION_COUNT, TIER, and NUDGE_ELIGIBLE

`bin/gstack-developer-profile` derives a builder's `SESSION_COUNT`, `TIER`, and `NUDGE_ELIGIBLE` from the `sessions[]` array in `~/.gstack/developer-profile.json`. But `/office-hours` appends **two** rows per run: the real session row (`mode: "startup"` or `"builder"`), and a separate `mode: "resources"` bookkeeping row recorded after resources are surfaced (`office-hours/SKILL.md:1620`, written via `--log-session`). The read path counts both.

This was masked while #1677 was live (the writer wrote to the legacy `builder-profile.jsonl` the reader never re-read, so `SESSION_COUNT` was stuck at 0). Now that the profile is unified onto `developer-profile.json` and sessions actually persist, the resources rows are read — so the bug is live: counts read roughly **2x** real sessions.

## Root cause (`bin/gstack-developer-profile`, current `main`)

The file already knows resources rows aren't sessions. Lines 236-238 filter them for `LAST_*`/`CROSS_PROJECT`, with a comment naming them "the Phase 6 auto-append":

```
const realSessions = sessions.filter(e => e.mode !== 'resources');
```

But that filter is applied to only 2 of the 4 consumers. The other two still read raw `sessions`:

- **Line 228:** `const count = sessions.length;` → `SESSION_COUNT` and `TIER` (thresholds `>=8` inner_circle, `>=4` regular, `>=1` welcome_back) are inflated.
- **Line 255:** `const builderSessions = sessions.filter(e => e.mode !== 'startup').length;` → doubly wrong: it **counts** `resources` rows (they're `!== 'startup'`) and **excludes** real `startup` sessions. Feeds `NUDGE_ELIGIBLE` (line 256: `builderSessions >= 3 && totalSignals >= 5`), so the builder→founder nudge can arm off bookkeeping alone.

## Repro

Fresh `$HOME`. Run `/office-hours` to completion 4 times as real design sessions.

- Each run appends 1 session row + 1 `mode:"resources"` row → `sessions.length == 8`.
- `gstack-developer-profile --read` reports `SESSION_COUNT: 8` / `TIER: inner_circle`.
- Truth: 4 real sessions, which should be `TIER: regular`.

Two real sessions already report `SESSION_COUNT: 4` / `regular` when the user is actually at `welcome_back`. The founder nudge can fire after as few as 3 runs on bookkeeping rows rather than 3 real `builder` sessions.

## Impact

Low-severity (greeting tier and the builder→founder nudge are personalization/tone, not crash or data loss), but it fires on the **default happy path** for every `/office-hours` user now that sessions persist: wrong-tier greeting and a premature "have you thought about whether this could be a company?" nudge.

## Fix

Hoist the existing `realSessions` filter above `count`, and make the nudge count real `mode:"builder"` sessions:

- `count = realSessions.length` → SESSION_COUNT / TIER / CROSS_PROJECT / designs all key off real sessions.
- `builderSessions = realSessions.filter(e => e.mode === 'builder').length` → nudge measures repeat *builders*, which is what it was meant to measure.

Write path untouched; this is a read-only aggregation change. A PR with this fix plus regression tests (count, tier both-sides-of-gate boundaries, cross-project, and nudge in the presence of resources rows) is up at #1991.

## Relationship to #1677

Distinct bug, sequential. #1677 was a write-path split-brain (`SESSION_COUNT` always 0 because writes went to a file the reader never read). Unifying the profile fixed that and **exposed** this one: now that rows persist and get read, the `mode:"resources"` rows get over-counted. #1677 = sessions don't persist; this = persisted sessions are over-counted.

title: fix(learnings-log): bun -e import fails on Windows Git Bash (MSYS path mangling)
body:
## Problem

On **Windows Git Bash (MSYS)**, `bin/gstack-learnings-log` exits 1 with no output, so `/learn` cannot append learnings — they have to be hand-appended to `learnings.jsonl`.

## Root cause

bun is a **native Windows binary**. The script runs:
```bash
bun -e "import { hasInjection } from '$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/jsonl-store.ts'; ..."
```
MSYS unreliably mangles the absolute `/c/Users/...` import path embedded inside the `bun -e` script string, so the static import fails with `Cannot find module ... from 'C:\...\[eval]'` → empty stdout → `exit 1`, no write. (Confirmed via `bash -x` trace + isolating the snippet.)

It is **not** the bun-shim PATH issue — the shim resolves fine.

## Fix

Resolve the lib to a `file://` URL (`cygpath -m` on MSYS, plain absolute path on POSIX), pass it via env var `GSTACK_LIB_URL` (env values are **not** path-mangled), and `await import()` it dynamically (the script already uses top-level await). One-file change in `bin/gstack-learnings-log`.

POSIX/macOS/Linux are unaffected (no `cygpath`; `file://` + absolute path resolves correctly).

## Verification (Windows Git Bash)

- Probe entry logged → `exit=0`, written to `learnings.jsonl` with auto-injected `ts` and `trusted:false`.
- Reject paths intact: invalid `type` and invalid `key` both exit 1 and write nothing.
- `gstack-learnings-search` reads the file cleanly.

Only `gstack-learnings-log` used this inline-absolute-path-in-`-e`-string pattern; other bin scripts use relative imports (`from "../lib/..."`) which bun resolves from the module location regardless of MSYS.

title: v1.58.4.0 fix: high-priority community bug wave + PTY plan-mode smoke gate
body:
## Summary

Two things ship in v1.58.4.0.

**High-priority community bug-fix wave**
- **gbrain writes work on transaction-mode poolers** — removed the forced `GBRAIN_PREPARE=true` that deterministically broke 100% of writes on port-6543 poolers (#1965).
- **gbrain probe timeout is its own status** — a slow-but-healthy engine classifies as `timeout` (15s default, `GSTACK_GBRAIN_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`-overridable) and sync proceeds with a warning instead of silently suppressing brain features (#1964).
- **Dashboards never report fake zeros** — security + community dashboards surface "unknown — backend error" (or 503) on failure instead of `0`; success responses carry a `status:"ok"` marker (#1947).
- **Telemetry redaction** — `error_message` runs through the redaction engine at log time, fails closed to null on redactor failure (#1947).
- **Six new credential patterns** — GitLab, HuggingFace, npm, DigitalOcean, `Bearer` (entropy-gated), GCP service-account JSON (#1946).
- **Pre-push guard fails closed** on an un-computable diff, with a `GSTACK_REDACT_PREPUSH=skip` escape valve; `/ship` owns the per-repo install (#1946).
- **Windows git-bash bins** — `gstack-learnings-log` / `gstack-question-log` cygpath-normalize `$SCRIPT_DIR`; question-log dedupes its injection-pattern list via `lib/jsonl-store.ts` (#1950, #1934).

title: [Windows] `browse` fails to start: Chromium disconnects on launch, then `resolveDisconnectCause` crashes with `browser?.process is not a function`
body:
## Environment
- gstack: 1.58.4.0 (also reproduced on 1.58.1.0)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200), running via git-bash
- Node: v24.15.0, Bun: 1.3.14
- Playwright Chromium installed: chromium-1208 + chromium_headless_shell-1208

## Symptom
Every `browse` command (`goto`, `--version`, `--help`, `status`, …) prints:

[browse] Starting server...
[browse] Server failed to start within 15s


and exits 0. The headless browser never becomes usable, so `/qa` and `/qa-only`
cannot run on this machine.

## Root cause
The 15s timeout is misleading — the server DOES start and bind a port, then the
daemon crashes immediately. Running the server directly surfaces the real error:

$ node dist/server-node.mjs
[browse] Server running on http://127.0.0.1:27493/ (PID: 15352)
[browse] Tab closed (id=1, remaining=0)
[browse] FATAL unhandled rejection: browser?.process is not a function



Two layered problems:

1. **Primary (the real blocker):** On Windows the Chromium instance disconnects
   immediately at startup — the initial tab closes right after launch
   ("Tab closed (id=1, remaining=0)"). Likely the known Bun→Node→Chromium
   sandbox issue referenced in `src/browser-manager.ts` (#276).

2. **Secondary (masks the cause + kills the daemon):** the disconnect handler
   `resolveDisconnectCause()` at `src/browser-manager.ts:94` calls
   `browser?.process()`. Playwright's `Browser` has no `.process()` method, so
   this throws an unhandled rejection that crashes the whole server. A recoverable
   disconnect becomes a fatal startup failure, and the launcher only reports the
   generic "failed to start within 15s".

## Not a browser-binary issue
Reproduced identically with three different Chromium binaries:
- bundled Playwright `chromium-1208`
- bundled `chromium_headless_shell-1208`
- system Google Chrome via `GSTACK_CHROMIUM_PATH="C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe"`

Same `Tab closed → browser?.process is not a function` crash every time.

## Suggested fix
- Guard the `.process()` call so a disconnect during startup produces a clear,
  diagnosable error instead of an unhandled rejection, e.g.:
  ```ts
  const proc = typeof browser?.process === 'function' ? browser.process() : null;
(Won't restore browsing on its own, but stops the daemon from dying silently
and surfaces the real Windows-launch failure.)

Investigate the immediate Chromium disconnect on Windows/git-bash (#276) — this is the underlying blocker.
Repro
Windows 11 + git-bash, gstack 1.58.4.0
~/.claude/skills/gstack/browse/dist/browse goto https://example.com
Observe "Server failed to start within 15s"
node ~/.claude/skills/gstack/browse/dist/server-node.mjs to see the real crash

title: Cursor adapter: mapping gstack skills to .cursor/rules/ for Cursor users
body:
gstack is built around Claude Code's skill system. Cursor works differently: it uses `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` files instead of skills, and it can't structurally restrict delegated agent tool access the way Claude Code can.

A number of gstack users are also Cursor users and the mapping isn't obvious. I built [operating-kit](https://github.com/Sharrmavishal/operating-kit) partly to solve this — it's a portable operating method for both Claude Code and Cursor that ships a documented adapter.

The adapter covers:
- What ports cleanly (persona, operating principles, vigilance protocol, field notes, incident response — ~90%)
- What degrades: tool restriction for subagents (becomes an instruction rather than a wall), memory recall (becomes a `.mdc` rule rather than auto-recall)
- How the `.mdc` rules map to gstack's always-on skills: `operating-method.mdc` (alwaysApply: true) covers the persona + gates, `code-change.mdc` auto-attaches on code globs, `ship-and-recover.mdc` is pulled in for deploys/incidents

The full mapping is in [docs/cursor-adapter.md](https://github.com/Sharrmavishal/operating-kit/blob/main/docs/cursor-adapter.md).

Sharing in case it's useful to document a Cursor path in gstack's docs, or for Cursor users asking how to get equivalent behavior. Not a PR proposal — just flagging the mapping exists if it's useful.

title: /codex temp-file creation fails on macOS (BSD mktemp): .txt suffix after XXXXXX + trailing-slash TMP_ROOT
body:
### Summary
On macOS, `/codex` (all three modes) fails before Codex ever runs: the `mktemp`
calls that create the stderr/prompt/response temp files error out, the bash block
exits 1, and the user sees no review. Two compounding bugs, both in gstack.

### Environment
- gstack: 1.58.4.0
- macOS: 26.5.1 (Apple silicon)
- mktemp: /usr/bin/mktemp (BSD)
- $TMPDIR: /var/folders/.../T/  (note the trailing slash — macOS default)

### Symptom
mktemp: mkstemp failed on /var/folders/.../T//codex-err-XXXXXX.txt: File exists
mktemp: mkstemp failed on /var/folders/.../T//codex-prompt-XXXXXX.txt: File exists
/opt/homebrew/bin/bash: line 13: : No such file or directory
=== CODEX_EXIT=1 ===
(The empty `TMPERR`/`_PROMPT_FILE` vars then cascade into "No such file or directory"
for every later `"$TMPERR"` / `cat "$_PROMPT_FILE"`.)

### Root cause
1. **Suffix after the placeholder.** `skills/codex/SKILL.md` uses templates like
   `mktemp "$TMP_ROOT/codex-err-XXXXXX.txt"` (also `codex-prompt-XXXXXX.txt`,
   `codex-resp-XXXXXX.txt`). GNU `mktemp` tolerates a suffix after `XXXXXX`; **BSD
   `mktemp` (macOS) requires the placeholder at the END of the template** and
   mishandles the `.txt` suffix.
2. **Trailing slash in `TMP_ROOT`.** `bin/gstack-paths` emits `TMP_ROOT` straight
   from `$TMPDIR`, which on macOS ends in `/`. The template then expands to a
   double-slash path (`…/T//codex-err-…`), compounding the failure.

### Affected code
- `skills/codex/SKILL.md` (and `SKILL.md.tmpl`) — Steps 2A / 2B / 2C, every
  `mktemp "$TMP_ROOT/codex-*-XXXXXX.txt"`.
- `bin/gstack-paths` — `TMP_ROOT` carries `$TMPDIR`'s trailing slash.

### Suggested fix
Drop the `.txt` suffix (X's at the end) and strip the trailing slash:
```bash
TR="${TMP_ROOT%/}"
TMPERR=$(mktemp "$TR/codex-err-XXXXXX")
_PROMPT_FILE=$(mktemp "$TR/codex-prompt-XXXXXX")
Either fix alone helps; both together is the robust portable form. Optionally have
gstack-paths normalize TMP_ROOT (_tmp_root="${_tmp_root%/}") so every skill
that consumes it benefits, not just /codex.

Repro

macOS, default $TMPDIR: run /codex review in any git repo. The first mktemp
in Step 2A fails.

title: feat(autoplan): unattended-mode gates + confidence-gated escalation
body:
## What & why

`/autoplan` is built to run unattended — spawned by OpenClaw, batched across parallel sprints, or in a host that disables interactive prompts (Conductor runs `--disallowedTools AskUserQuestion`). But its two *never-auto-decided* gates — **premise confirmation** (Phase 1) and **User Challenges** — silently collapsed to their default whenever `AskUserQuestion` was unavailable, because `SPAWNED_SESSION` mode says "auto-choose the recommended option." That auto-accepts exactly the high-stakes judgment the skill otherwise refuses to automate. (The CHANGELOG already documents the symptom: the autoplan E2E bails at the premise gate under `--disallowedTools AskUserQuestion`, and the gates were "broken in any Conductor session.")

This PR closes that gap with two small, composable changes.

### 1. Unattended Mode (G1 + G2)

A new **autoplan-local** override — deliberately scoped to this skill, *not* the shared `{{PREAMBLE}}`, to keep the blast radius to one skill. When unattended (`SPAWNED_SESSION: true`, no AUQ variant callable, or `autoplan_unattended` config), the two hard gates are **parked, not silently accepted**:

- **Park** each premise / User-Challenge to a durable `*-autoplan-pending-*.jsonl` queue (one row per gate, full context).
- **Keep the user's original direction** as the default (`PENDING_PREMISE_REVIEW` / `PENDING_CHALLENGE`). Two models agreeing doesn't let them silently overrule an absent human.
- **HALT** on a security/feasibility-flagged challenge (`BLOCKED — …`). One sanctioned stop, never a silent proceed.
- **Notify** an optional `notify_webhook` (no-op if unset).
- **Resume** with `/autoplan --resume`, which replays each parked row as a real `AskUserQuestion`.

Interactive runs are unchanged — when AUQ is available, the gates behave exactly as before.

### 2. Decision Confidence (G7)

Every auto-decision now carries a 1–10 score (reusing the existing `confidence.ts` rubric). A **Taste** decision scored **below a configurable threshold** (`autoplan_escalate_below`, default 6) is escalated to the gate — or to the pending queue when unattended — instead of silently auto-decided. A near-coin-flip shouldn't be a call the 6 principles make alone. Mechanical decisions and clear taste calls auto-decide as before; User Challenges and the two hard gates are never downgraded. Adds a `Confidence` column to the Decision Audit Trail.

## Implementation

- `scripts/resolvers/autoplan-unattended.ts` — new `{{AUTOPLAN_UNATTENDED}}` resolver
- `scripts/resolvers/confidence.ts` — new `generateDecisionConfidence` (`{{DECISION_CONFIDENCE}}`)
- `scripts/resolvers/index.ts` — register both tokens
- `autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl` — wire both blocks + gate pointers + audit column + Important Rules
- `autoplan/SKILL.md` — regenerated (`bun run gen:skill-docs`)
- `test/resolver-autoplan-unattended.test.ts` — 10 gate-tier assertions

New config keys (free-form, default-on-absent): `autoplan_unattended`, `notify_webhook`, `autoplan_escalate_below`.

## Testing

- New test: **10/10 pass**
- `gen:skill-docs --host all --dry-run`: **0 stale**
- Guards green: idempotency, gen-skill-docs, spec-template-sync, template-context-parity, resolver-entry, touchfiles, skill-validation, budget-regression, collision-sentinel, llms-txt-shape, docs-config-keys, version, parity, coverage-floor (~1170 assertions, 0 failures)

## Notes

- **Backward-compatible:** interactive behavior is unchanged; the new behavior only fires when AUQ is unavailable or config opts in.
- Left `VERSION` / `CHANGELOG` to your release flow to avoid conflicts — happy to add a bump if you prefer.
- Origin: a focused audit of `/autoplan` against its unattended/parallel ICP. Two further gaps from that audit — risk-aware principles keyed on `REPO_MODE`, and a post-implementation `/autoreview` sibling — are intentionally out of scope here.

## Summary

The PreToolUse `question-preference-hook` was emitting

  - exits 0 silently when there is no `additionalContext` to inject
  - emits a payload with only `additionalContext` (no

title: feat(benchmark): add Antigravity (`agy`) provider adapter
body:
## Add Antigravity (`agy`) provider adapter

Google retired the standalone **Gemini CLI** for individual accounts — the `gemini` binary now fails at startup with `IneligibleTierError` ("This client is no longer supported for Gemini Code Assist for individuals… migrate to the Antigravity suite"). It's replaced by the **Antigravity CLI** (`agy`). This breaks the `gemini` provider leg of multi-provider benchmarks and the outside-voice second-opinion flow.

This PR adds a first-class **`antigravity`** provider that wraps `agy`, leaving the legacy `gemini` adapter intact for anyone still on the old CLI.

### Headless contract (verified against `agy` 1.0.11)
```
agy --print "<prompt>" --dangerously-skip-permissions [--model "<name>"] --print-timeout <dur>
```
- `-p` / `--print` / `--prompt` → run one prompt non-interactively, print response.
- `--dangerously-skip-permissions` → auto-approve tool use (the `--yolo` equivalent).
- `--model "<display name>"` → e.g. `"Gemini 3.1 Pro (High)"` (values from `agy models`).
- `--print-timeout <Go-duration>` → print-mode wait (kept in step with our wall-clock budget).

**Key difference from `gemini`:** `agy --print` emits **plain text** — there is **no `--output-format stream-json`**. So the adapter:
- treats stdout as the response,
- reports `tokens: {input:0, output:0}` and `toolCalls: 0` (the CLI exposes no telemetry in print mode),
- checks only that the binary is on PATH in `available()` (auth is configured at install / first TUI launch — no login flag, no API-key env var).

Tool surface is richer than the old Gemini CLI: `agy --print` runs a full agentic session (Read/Write/Edit/Bash/Glob/Grep/WebSearch/WebFetch).

### Changes
