title: fix(codex): BSD-safe temp-file creation on macOS (mktemp suffix + trailing-slash TMP_ROOT)
body:
Fixes #2091.

On macOS, `/codex` (all three modes) fails *before* Codex ever runs: the `mktemp`
calls that create the stderr/prompt/response temp files error out, the bash block
exits 1, and the user gets no review. Two compounding **but independent** bugs,
both in gstack. Diagnosis credit to **Scott Hardin (@scotthardin)** in #2091 —
this PR implements his suggested fix.

## Root causes

**1. Suffix after the `mktemp` placeholder (BSD vs GNU).**
The codex skill used templates like `mktemp "$TMP_ROOT/codex-err-XXXXXX.txt"`
(also `codex-prompt-XXXXXX.txt`, `codex-resp-XXXXXX.txt`). GNU `mktemp` tolerates
a suffix after the `XXXXXX` run; **BSD `mktemp` (macOS) requires the placeholder
at the end of the template and does not substitute the X's at all when a suffix
follows.** So call #1 creates a *literal fixed-name* file `codex-err-XXXXXX.txt`
and exits 0, and a later call — a second `/codex` run, a stale leftover, or a
concurrent worktree — fails with `mkstemp failed: File exists`, exits 1, and the
empty `TMPERR`/`_PROMPT_FILE` vars cascade into "No such file or directory". This
is why the failure is **state-dependent**, and why some macOS users think
`/codex` "works."

**2. Trailing slash in `TMP_ROOT`.**
`bin/gstack-paths` emitted `TMP_ROOT` straight from `$TMPDIR`, which on macOS ends
in `/` (e.g. `/var/folders/.../T/`), so `"$TMP_ROOT/codex-err-…"` expands to a
double-slash path (`…/T//codex-err-…`), compounding the failure.

## The fix

- **`bin/gstack-paths`**: strip the trailing slash from `TMP_ROOT` at the source
  (`_tmp_root="${_tmp_root%/}"`), so **every** consumer benefits, not just
  `/codex`. A bare `/` is preserved (not collapsed to empty).
- **`codex/SKILL.md.tmpl`** (+ regenerated `codex/SKILL.md`): move the placeholder
  to the end of every codex `mktemp` template (drop the `.txt` suffix), at all
  five sites (`codex-err` ×3, `codex-prompt` ×1, `codex-resp` ×1).

Both changes are needed — the suffix bug is independent of the slash bug.

## Verified repro (macOS 26.x, Apple Silicon, gstack 1.58.4.0, `/usr/bin/mktemp` = BSD, `$TMPDIR` ends in `/`)

Before (old template, BSD mktemp):
```
call#1 -> rc=0 path=…/T/codex-err-XXXXXX.txt      # literal name, X's NOT substituted
call#2 -> rc=1 mktemp: mkstemp failed on …/T//codex-err-XXXXXX.txt: File exists
files created:  codex-err-XXXXXX.txt
```
After (new template + slash-normalized root):
```
TMP_ROOT = …/T                                    # no trailing slash, no double slash
call#1 -> rc=0 path=…/T/codex-err-YNRdRX          # real randomized name
call#2 -> rc=0 path=…/T/codex-err-QfpaqE          # survives — no "File exists"
```

## Tests

`test/regression-issue2091-codex-bsd-mktemp.test.ts` pins both bugs:
- **bug 1** — static invariant: no codex `mktemp` template carries a non-`X`
  suffix after `XXXXXX`, asserted across **both** `codex/SKILL.md.tmpl` and the
  generated `codex/SKILL.md` so regen drift (or editing one but not the other)
  can't reopen it.
- **bug 2** — runtime: `gstack-paths` strips a trailing slash from `TMPDIR`/`TMP`,
  leaves a clean path unchanged, and never collapses `/` to empty.

```
bun test test/regression-issue2091-codex-bsd-mktemp.test.ts test/gstack-paths.test.ts \
         test/codex-hardening.test.ts test/gen-skill-docs.test.ts test/skill-validation.test.ts
# 778 pass, 0 fail
```
`codex/SKILL.md` was regenerated via `bun run gen:skill-docs --host all`, so the
`skill-docs` dry-run CI check stays green.

## Same-class occurrences found — left out of scope (follow-ups)

Grepping `mktemp .*XXXXXX\.(txt|json|md)` repo-wide surfaced the same
suffix-after-placeholder antipattern elsewhere. These are **not** on the `/codex`
path (#2091) and use hardcoded `/tmp` rather than `$TMP_ROOT`, so I kept this PR
focused and reviewable rather than silently expanding it:

- `claude/SKILL.md.tmpl:98-99` — `mktemp /tmp/gstack-claude-response-XXXXXX.json`
  and `mktemp /tmp/gstack-claude-error-XXXXXX.txt`.
- `scripts/resolvers/review.ts:354` — `mktemp /tmp/gstack-codex-oh-XXXXXXXX.txt`
  (this is the source that generates `office-hours/SKILL.md:1303`).

Happy to fold these into this PR or send a follow-up — your call.

title: memory-ingest renders all Codex rollout sessions as empty bodies (parser expects payload.message; current format is payload.type=='message' + payload.content)
body:
## Summary
`gstack-memory-ingest` renders **every Codex rollout session with an empty body** (`message_count: 0`, zero-length content). All Codex transcripts import as empty shells.

## Root cause
`parseTranscriptJsonl` (bin/gstack-memory-ingest.ts) detects Codex correctly (`first.type === 'session_meta'`) but its message loop extracts content via:
```js
} else if (isCodex && rec?.payload?.message) { const msg = rec.payload.message; ... }
```
Current Codex rollout JSONL has no `payload.message`. Records are shaped:
```
{ type: 'response_item', payload: { type: 'message', role: 'user'|'assistant'|'developer', content: [...] } }
```
So the branch never fires → 0 messages → empty page body for every Codex session.

## Repro
Ingest any `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl`; the resulting `transcripts/codex/...` page has `message_count: 0` and an empty body. Confirmed across 243/243 Codex sessions on this machine.

## Suggested fix
Handle the `response_item` / `payload.type === 'message'` shape: read `payload.role` and flatten `payload.content` (array of `{type, text}` items) into the body, mirroring the Claude Code branch.

## Env
gstack 1.58.4.0, Codex CLI rollout format (June 2026), Windows 10.

title: feat(context-save): persist plan file before saving checkpoint when in plan mode
body:
When GSTACK_PLAN_MODE=active and CLAUDE_PLAN_FILE exists, /context-save now
persists the plan to .claude/plans/ before writing the checkpoint. This
prevents plan loss when the user saves and exits without approving the plan
(via ExitPlanMode) — common on unstable hardware or when the user needs to
rest.

The plan is saved with a timestamp and also copied to active-plan.md as a
stable symlink target for /context-restore.

Fixes: checkpoint referencing a plan path that does not exist on disk.

title: feat(context-restore): cross-session stall detection for buried tasks
body:
/context-restore only shows the latest checkpoint's Remaining Work, but tasks
that persist across 3+ sessions without progress get buried — the user never
sees them on restore. This adds Step 2a: after loading the latest checkpoint,
scan the last 15 checkpoints for Remaining Work items that appear in 3+
sessions. These are flagged as STALLED and presented before the next-steps
question, preventing task湮灭 (G010 gotcha pattern).

Design:
- Bash-based extraction: awk finds Remaining Work sections, grep pulls
  numbered bold items, sort+uniq counts cross-checkpoint frequency
- Threshold: 3+ occurrences triggers the warning
- Silent skip when no stalls found (zero cost for clean projects)
- Suggests creating a master task inventory file for long-lived projects

See-also: mindivy docs/assets/20260620-gotchas-and-patterns.md #G010

title: v1.59.2.0 fix(make-pdf): stop smartypants URL carve from swallowing the next placeholder (#2084)
body: Closes #2084. `make-pdf generate` mangled any bare/autolinked `http(s)://` URL into a literal `SMARTPANTS_PRESERVED_` token and left an unclosed `` that bled link-blue into every following block to the end of the document. ## Root cause `make-pdf/src/smartypants.ts` carves code/tags/URLs into U+0000-delimited placeholder tokens, transforms the remaining text, then restores the tokens. The URL pattern was `/\bhttps?:\/\/\S+/g`. `\S` matches non-whitespace, and the placeholder delimiter U+0000 is non-whitespace, so for an autolinked URL (`URL`) the link-text URL match greedily swallowed the trailing `` placeholder. The nested placeholder never restored (the restore is a single left-to-right pass), so `SMARTPANTS_PRESERVED_` leaked into the text and the `` was dropped. ## Fix Exclude U+0000 from the URL character class (`[^\s]+`) so the URL match stops at the placeholder boundary. Real URLs never contain U+0000, so the match is identical to `\S+` except that it no longer crosses a carve boundary. Before / after on the issue's repro (via the real `smartypants()`): - before: `https://example.com SMARTPANTS_PRESERVED_2 here.` (leak, no ``) - after: `https://example.com here.` ## Test Added a regression test in `make-pdf/test/render.test.ts` (the existing `smartypants` block): an autolinked URL keeps its `...` intact and leaks no placeholder. Verified it fails on the old `\S+` regex and passes on the fix. Full `render.test.ts`: 67 pass. Quotes, em dashes, ellipses, code/pre zones, and href-only URLs are unaffected.

title: Would you be open to a "decomposition ladder" (roadmap → epics → stories → sprints) as a contribution?
body:
## What I'm proposing

First — thank you for gstack. I've been running it daily and the two ends of the lifecycle are excellent: the thinking side (`/office-hours` + the CEO/Eng/Design/QA review personas) and the execution side (the sprint / goal-loop conductors taking a spec to a PR).

The spot I keep filling in myself is the **middle** — turning a raw idea into a *structured backlog* the execution end can run autonomously. I've built an explicit **decomposition ladder** for that and have been using it in anger:

```
/office-hours (first principles)
   → roadmap (sequenced outcomes/milestones)
      → epics (shippable chunks of value)
         → stories (one-PR-sized, with acceptance criteria)
            → sprints (executable batches)
               → gstack sprint/goal-loop executes each story
```

The one-PR-per-story sizing is what makes the autonomous execution reliable — each unit maps to something the build loop can objectively verify it finished.

## The build/review split (the execution leg)

The principle that makes the autonomous side trustworthy: **the model that builds is never the model that reviews.** Cheap open-weight models (US-hosted via Fireworks) do the building; frontier models gate them adversarially.

| Side | Role | Model | When it runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Build** | Default builder | MiniMax M3 | Most lanes — cheapest, teardown-resilient |
| **Build** | Orchestrator | GLM-5.2 | Hardest lanes (mission stack) |
| **Build** | Worker | Kimi K2.7 Code | Hardest lanes (mission stack) |
| **Build** | Validator | DeepSeek V4 Pro | Hardest lanes (mission stack) |
| **Review** | Adversarial gate | Codex + Grok + Claude | Every lane — non-negotiable on security-sensitive lanes |

*(Model names are a mid-2026 snapshot; the roles are the durable part. This whole leg is the dependency-heavy part that I'd keep in a separate repo — see below.)*

## The ask

I'd rather match your direction than guess at it, so before I send anything: **would you want the gstack-native parts of this upstream, or would you prefer I keep it as a linked satellite repo?**

I ask because the *ladder itself* is pure gstack (no new dependencies) and could live upstream cleanly. But the way I run the **execution leg** adds two *other* projects — [ponytail](https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail) as a code-quality gate inside the build, and an autonomous build agent ([Factory Droid](https://factory.ai), chosen for its native mission structure and because it serves open-weight models through [Fireworks AI](https://fireworks.ai) — US-based inference, not the vendors' own APIs) running open-weight builders (MiniMax M3, or a GLM-5.2 / Kimi K2.7 Code / DeepSeek V4 Pro mission stack) gated by frontier adversarial reviewers (Codex / Grok / Claude) on the **builder ≠ reviewer** principle. I would not want to push a hard dependency on someone else's project into your core, so I'm assuming that execution-wiring part stays in a separate repo regardless, and only the dependency-free decomposition ladder is an upstream candidate.

## What I can send

- A PR adding the decomposition-ladder skills/flow in gstack's existing style (the dependency-free part).
- A standalone writeup of the full loop + the hard-won gotchas (Windows copy-not-symlink, the Chromium extraction deadlock, the embedding-provider-default trap, the OpenCode persistent-backend gotcha, etc.) that you're welcome to link from the README, or that I'll just host myself.

Happy to do as much or as little of that as fits gstack. If "keep it as a satellite and I'll link it" is the answer, that's totally fine — just let me know which you'd prefer before I open a PR.

title: `./setup` hangs on "Installing Playwright Chromium" (macOS arm64); re-running spawns multiple stuck processes
body:
**Environment**
- gstack: v1.58.5.0 (commit 11de390)
- macOS 15 (Darwin 25.5.0), Apple Silicon (arm64)
- bun 1.3.14, node v24.16.0
- Fresh install via the documented one-liner

**What happens**
`./setup` reaches `Installing Playwright Chromium...` and never returns. The browser binary (`browse/dist/browse`) builds fine and Chromium downloads to 100% on the first run, but the step does not complete, so the script never reaches the Claude skill-linking block (`link_claude_skill_dirs`, setup line ~983). Result: only the `gstack` router skill is registered — none of the flat-name skills (`/qa`, `/ship`, `/review`, …) get linked into `~/.claude/skills/`.

Re-running `./setup` to retry makes it worse: each invocation launches another `bash ./setup` + `node .../playwright install chromium` + `oopDownloadBrowserMain.js` that also hangs, so several stuck process trees accumulate:

```
node .../node_modules/.bin/playwright install chromium
bash ./setup --host claude --no-prefix
node .../playwright-core/lib/server/registry/oopDownloadBrowserMain.js
```

**Likely root cause**
`ensure_playwright_browser()` (setup line 252) verifies Chromium on macOS with a bun-based launch:

```sh
bun --eval 'import { chromium } from "playwright"; const browser = await chromium.launch(); await browser.close();'
```

This appears to fail/hang on macOS arm64 (similar to the Bun pipe bug oven-sh/bun#4253 that the code already works around with Node on Windows). Because the check returns non-zero, setup believes Chromium is missing on every run and re-enters `bunx playwright install chromium` (line 483), which itself hangs — an effectively permanent reinstall loop. Chromium is in fact already present under `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/`.

**Workaround that fixed it**
Kill the stuck processes, then link skills directly without touching the Chromium step:

```sh
pkill -f "gstack/setup"; pkill -f "playwright install chromium"; pkill -f oopDownloadBrowserMain
~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-relink   # "Relinked 53 skills as flat names"
```

After this, all skills (`/qa`, etc.) register correctly.

**Suggested fixes**
1. Use the Node-based launch check on macOS too (not only Windows), or add a timeout around the bun `chromium.launch()` probe so a hung probe can't force a reinstall.
2. Guard the install step against re-entry / wrap `bunx playwright install chromium` in a timeout, and detect an already-downloaded Chromium in `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/` before reinstalling.
3. Consider running `link_claude_skill_dirs` before the Chromium step (or in a `trap`/`finally`) so a browser-download failure doesn't leave skills unregistered.

title: headed mode: Chromium window closes immediately on macOS 26 (Sequoia)
body:
## Bug report

**gstack version:** 1.34.1.0 (upgrade to 1.58.5.0 available but not yet applied)
**OS:** macOS Darwin 25.5.0 (macOS 26 / Sequoia)
**Running inside:** Claude Code VSCode extension

---

### What happens

Using `$B connect` (headed mode / `connect-chrome` skill), gstack reports a successful connection, but the visible Chromium window disappears within seconds of opening. There is no time to interact with it.

### Reproduction steps

1. Run `$B connect` inside Claude Code (VSCode extension).
2. gstack prints "Connected to real Chrome", shows a PID, reports status healthy.
3. A Chromium window appears briefly on screen.
4. The window closes on its own within a few seconds (no user interaction).
5. On the next `$B disconnect` attempt, gstack reports "server was unresponsive — force cleaned".

### What works

- `$B connect` returns success (PID shown, status healthy).
- `$B goto <url>` navigates successfully (returns HTTP 200).
- `$B focus` returns "Browser window activated".
- Everything works at the API level; only the visible window disappears.

### Additional context: Chrome profile mismatch

Regular Google Chrome is installed with multiple profiles, but none of them is the `Default` profile. The existing profiles are numbered: Profile 4, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13.

gstack appears to look for `Default/Cookies` (or similar), which does not exist. This may be contributing to the crash or early exit if gstack cannot find or load the expected profile directory and then abandons the process silently.

### Expected behavior

The Chromium window should stay open and remain interactive for the duration of the session, consistent with the behavior documented for headed / `connect-chrome` mode.

### Attempted workarounds

Reproduced multiple times with identical results. The window never stays open long enough to interact with.

---

Happy to provide any additional diagnostic output (e.g., gstack server logs, Chromium crash logs from `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/`) if that would help narrow this down.

title: fix: Chrome numbered-profile cookie discovery + headed window stability on macOS 26
body:
## Summary

Fixes two bugs reported in issue #2138, both affecting macOS 26 (Sequoia).

### Bug 1 — Headed Chromium window closes immediately on macOS 26

**Root cause (two interacting issues):**

1. macOS 26 tightened window activation policy. Chromium windows spawned by a
   non-app process (the Bun server) are subject to a new OS-level window-hiding
   behavior that causes them to close within seconds unless properly registered
   via `NSApplicationActivateIgnoringOtherApps`.

2. `raiseHeadedWindowMacOS()` in `cli.ts` tried to activate "Google Chrome for
   Testing" via osascript, but `launchHeaded()` patches the Info.plist to rename
   the app to "GStack Browser". The activation silently failed, leaving the window
   unraised and subject to the OS hiding it.

**Fixes in `browse/src/browser-manager.ts` and `browse/src/cli.ts`:**

- Add `--disable-features=MacControlledWindowBehavior` to headed launch args on
  darwin. This flag suppresses the new OS-level window-hiding behavior introduced
  in macOS 26 while Playwright's NSApp startup sequence handles activation. No-op
  on macOS < 26 and all non-macOS platforms.
- Fix `raiseHeadedWindowMacOS()` to try "GStack Browser" first (post-patch name)
  with fallback to "Google Chrome for Testing" (pre-patch / patch skipped).

### Bug 2 — `cookie-import-browser` fails when no Default profile exists

**Root cause:** Chrome on macOS 26 and some multi-profile installations never
create a `Default` directory. Every account lands in a numbered profile (`Profile
4`, `Profile 12`, etc.). `cookie-import-browser.ts` only looked for
`Default/Cookies`, throwing "Chrome is not installed" even when cookies existed.

**Fix in `browse/src/cookie-import-browser.ts`:**

- When `getBrowserMatch()` can't find `Default`, call new
  `findFirstNumberedProfile()` which scans for `Profile N` directories, sorts by
  number (lowest first so the primary account wins), and returns the first one
  with a Cookies file.
- Same fallback logic applies on macOS, Linux, and Windows.
- Explicit non-default profile names (e.g. `importCookies('chrome', [...], 'Profile 4')`)
  still fail fast as before — the fallback only fires for the default `'Default'` case.

## Test plan

- [ ] `$B connect` on macOS 26: headed Chromium window stays open and
  `$B screenshot` succeeds (no "Cannot take screenshot with 0 width")
- [ ] `$B disconnect` on macOS 26 reports clean shutdown, not "server was
  unresponsive — force cleaned"
- [ ] `cookie-import-browser chrome` on a Mac with only numbered profiles (no
  `Default` directory): succeeds and imports cookies from the lowest-numbered
  profile
- [ ] `cookie-import-browser chrome` on a standard install with `Default`
  profile: still works (no regression)
- [ ] New unit tests pass: `bun test browse/test/cookie-import-browser.test.ts`

## Files changed

- `browse/src/cookie-import-browser.ts` — `getBrowserMatch` + new `findFirstNumberedProfile`
- `browse/src/browser-manager.ts` — macOS 26 `--disable-features` flag in `launchHeaded` and `handoff`
- `browse/src/cli.ts` — fix `raiseHeadedWindowMacOS` to try both app names
- `browse/test/cookie-import-browser.test.ts` — 3 new tests for numbered-profile fallback

Closes #2138

---

## Local test evidence (macOS 26 / Darwin 25.5.0)

**Environment:** macOS 26 Sequoia (Darwin 25.5.0), running inside Claude Code VSCode extension.

**Test session:** After applying the `--disable-features=MacControlledWindowBehavior` fix, launched
a headed Chromium window via `$B connect` and left it running for 10+ minutes. The window
remained open and interactive for the entire session. 23 Google Search Console indexing requests
were submitted successfully through the headed window with no crashes or premature closures.

**Before this fix:** The window closed within seconds of opening every time.

---

## Second problem found: `handoff()` path missing the macOS 26 flag

After the main fix was verified working, a code audit found that `handoff()` in
`browser-manager.ts` (the headless-to-headed re-launch path, lines ~1560-1600) builds
its own `launchArgs` array independently from `launchHeaded()` and was NOT including
`--disable-features=MacControlledWindowBehavior`.

A user who triggers a handoff (e.g., via the gstack extension "hand off to user" UI flow)
on macOS 26 would have seen the same immediate window-close bug, even after the
`launchHeaded()` fix.

**Fix applied in commit `5c7058bb`:** Added the same `if (process.platform === 'darwin')` guard to
the `handoff()` launchArgs block, immediately after the initial `launchArgs` array is built:

```typescript
// macOS 26: same window-hiding suppression as launchHeaded(). The handoff
// path launches a fresh headed Chromium and is subject to the same
// MacControlledWindowBehavior that causes the window to close immediately
// on Sequoia. No-op on macOS < 26 and on non-macOS platforms.
if (process.platform === 'darwin') {
  launchArgs.push('--disable-features=MacControlledWindowBehavior');
}
```

Build verified: `bun run build` passes cleanly after the change.

Note: the fix commit `5c7058bb` is local only — push access to `garrytan/gstack` was denied
(403). The fix is in the local worktree at `/tmp/gstack-pr/browse/src/browser-manager.ts`
and needs to be pushed by a repo collaborator.

title: gstack-memory-ingest silently ingests 0 pages on gbrain ≥0.42 (git-ignore fast path vs ignore-all ~/.gstack staging)
body:
## Summary

`gstack-memory-ingest` (bulk + incremental) silently ingests **0** transcript pages into a local PGLite brain when running against **gbrain ≥ 0.42**. The run reports success (`written: 86`) but `gbrain import` reports `0 imported, 0 unchanged, 0 failed`, so nothing ever reaches the index. Semantic search over transcripts/artifacts is silently empty.

Discovered during a fresh `/setup-gbrain` (PGLite local, Voyage embeddings) on macOS.

## Root cause (two-repo interaction)

1. `gstack-memory-ingest.ts → makeStagingDir()` stages pages at `~/.gstack/.staging-ingest-<pid>-<ts>/` — a **direct child of `$GSTACK_HOME`**. This is required by `lib/staging-guard.ts` (`checkOwnedStagingDir` enforces `dirname(canon) === home`) so the recursive-delete cleanup is safe.
2. `$GSTACK_HOME` (`~/.gstack`) is the **artifacts git repo**, whose `.gitignore` is `*` (ignore-everything; explicit allowlist via `git add -f`).
3. gbrain 0.42.x (#1159 `--respect-gitignore`) added a git-aware fast path in `collectSyncableFiles` (`src/commands/import.ts`): when the import dir is inside a git work tree it enumerates via `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`, which **honors `.gitignore`**.
4. Because the staging dir lives inside the ignore-all `~/.gstack` tree, `git ls-files --exclude-standard` returns **nothing** → `Found 0 markdown files` → `0 imported`.

### Reproduction
```
# inside ~/.gstack (gitignore = '*')
mkdir -p ~/.gstack/staging-proof && echo hi > ~/.gstack/staging-proof/x.md
git -C ~/.gstack ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard -- ~/.gstack/staging-proof   # -> empty
gbrain import ~/.gstack/staging-proof --no-embed --json                                      # -> Found 0 markdown files
# same dir OUTSIDE any git tree imports fine
mkdir -p ~/staging-proof && echo hi > ~/staging-proof/x.md
gbrain import ~/staging-proof --no-embed --json                                              # -> imported 1
```

## Impact
- Any gstack user on gbrain ≥ 0.42 with `artifacts_sync_mode != off` (so `~/.gstack` is a git repo) gets **silent 0-page transcript ingest**. Code + artifacts-source search still work; only the memory-ingest staging→import path is broken.
- Failure is silent: the run summary says `written: N` and exit 0.

## Proposed fix (keeps both safety invariants intact)

**gbrain** (`garrytan/gbrain`): add an opt-out for the gitignore fast path on `gbrain import`, e.g. `--no-respect-gitignore` (or `GBRAIN_IMPORT_NO_GITIGNORE=1`). When set, `collectSyncableFiles` skips `gitListSyncableFiles` and uses the FS walk. Default stays gitignore-honoring (protects the vendor/build-tree case from #1159).

**gstack** (`garrytan/gstack`): `gstack-memory-ingest.ts` passes that flag on its import call (`spawnGbrainAsync(["import", stagingDir, "--no-embed", "--json", "--no-respect-gitignore"])`), since it deliberately stages inside an ignore-all repo — the ambient `.gitignore` should not apply to an explicitly-targeted staging dir.

The FS walker's `pruneDir` skips hidden *children*, not the passed root, so the `.staging-ingest-*` root name is fine once the fast path is bypassed.

## Environment
- gstack `1.58.5.0`
- gbrain `0.42.53.0`, engine `pglite`, embeddings `voyage:voyage-code-3`
- macOS (darwin 25.5.0)

Happy to open PRs on both repos if the maintainers agree on the flag name/shape.

title: gstack-upgrade: stop the browse daemon after upgrading
body:
## Problem

After a gstack upgrade, a still-running `browse` daemon is on the *pre-upgrade* version. Until it's recycled, every subsequent `browse` call detects the version mismatch and kills + relaunches the daemon. Each relaunch:

- resets the viewport to the default, and
- wipes the browser context — logged-in sessions drop and tabs land on `about:blank`.

In practice this reads as *"browse suddenly can't hold a viewport / keeps logging me out / lands on about:blank"* for a stretch right after an upgrade, until the daemon happens to settle on the new version. It's easy to misdiagnose as a browse bug or a flaky site. Observed the daemon PID change 3× across one session during the churn window (viewport reset + auth-cookie loss each time); it stabilized once it settled on the new version.

## Fix

Add **Step 5.5: Settle the browse daemon** to the inline upgrade flow (right after the version marker is written). If a daemon is running, `browse stop` it so the next `browse` call relaunches exactly once, cleanly, on the new version:

```bash
BROWSE_BIN="$INSTALL_DIR/browse/dist/browse"
if [ -x "$BROWSE_BIN" ] && "$BROWSE_BIN" status 2>/dev/null | grep -qi '^PID:'; then
  "$BROWSE_BIN" stop 2>/dev/null || true
fi
```

Uses only `browse stop` — never `pkill`/pattern-kill, which can take down the user's real browser windows.

## Notes

- Edited `SKILL.md.tmpl` (source) and `SKILL.md` together with the identical block; regenerate `SKILL.md` from the template if that's preferred in CI.
- Scoped to the inline upgrade flow; guarded so it's a no-op when no daemon is running.

title: harden(worktree): symlink-plant defense in pruneStale
make-pdf: cwd-dependent browse resolution picks the ~/.claude/skills/browse alias directory as the binary (generate exits 4 with empty stderr)
body:
## Environment

- gstack v1.58.5.0, fresh install on 2026-07-03 (`git clone` + `./setup`, host: claude)
- macOS arm64 (Darwin 25.5.0), bun 1.2.22
- browse daemon healthy (`$B status` → `Status: healthy`)

## What happens

`pdf generate` fails with exit 4 and an empty-stderr error, even though the browse daemon is up and `browse newtab --json` works fine when run by hand from the same shell:

```
$ cd ~/.claude/skills/gstack
$ make-pdf/dist/pdf generate guide.md out.pdf
Reading markdown... Rendering HTML... Rendering 1 diagram(s)...
[make-pdf] warning: diagram-render tab unavailable: browse newtab exited 1:
Inlining images... Opening tab...
$P: browse newtab exited 1:
(exit 4)
```

`pdf setup` shows why — step 1 "finds" the browse binary at a path that is not a binary:

```
$ cd ~/.claude/skills/gstack && make-pdf/dist/pdf setup
  [1/5] Checking browse binary... OK (/Users/<user>/.claude/skills/browse)   ← this is a DIRECTORY
  [2/5] Launching Chromium... FAIL
```

`~/.claude/skills/browse` is the skill-alias directory that `./setup` creates (it contains only `SKILL.md -> gstack/browse/SKILL.md`). `execFileSync` on a directory fails with EACCES and no stderr, which surfaces as the unhelpful `browse newtab exited 1:` above.

## Root cause (two compounding bugs in `make-pdf/src/browseClient.ts`)

1. **Directories pass the executable probe.** `isExecutable()` uses `fs.accessSync(p, X_OK)`, which succeeds for directories (they carry the traversal x-bit). `findExecutable()` therefore happily returns a directory. A `statSync(p).isFile()` check would close this.

2. **Sibling resolution is cwd-dependent.** `resolveBrowseBin()` builds sibling candidates from `path.dirname(process.argv[0])`. In the bun-compiled binary this evaluates to `.` (argv[0] is bare), so the candidates resolve against the **cwd**, not the binary's location. With cwd = `~/.claude/skills/gstack`, the third candidate `resolve(selfDir, "../browse")` becomes `~/.claude/skills/browse` — the alias directory from bug 1. Resolving from `process.execPath` instead of `argv[0]` would pin it to the real install.

Proof of cwd-dependence (same binary, same machine, only cwd differs):

```
$ cd ~ && ~/.claude/skills/gstack/make-pdf/dist/pdf setup
  [1/5] Checking browse binary... OK (/Users/<user>/.claude/skills/gstack/browse/dist/browse)   ← correct

$ cd ~/.claude/skills/gstack && make-pdf/dist/pdf setup
  [1/5] Checking browse binary... OK (/Users/<user>/.claude/skills/browse)                       ← directory
```

The failing cwd is not exotic: it's the directory the README install one-liner leaves you in (`cd ~/.claude/skills/gstack && ./setup`), so a first-time user's very first `/make-pdf` run in that session hits this.

## Workaround

```
export GSTACK_BROWSE_BIN="$HOME/.claude/skills/gstack/browse/dist/browse"
```

With the override set, `generate` works end-to-end (cover, TOC, mermaid diagram all render).

## Suggested fix

- `findExecutable()`: require `fs.statSync(p).isFile()` before returning a candidate.
- `resolveBrowseBin()`: derive `selfDir` from `process.execPath` (falls back to argv[0] only if unset).

## Related finding: `pdf setup` step 2/5 always fails

While verifying the above I noticed `pdf setup` fails at `[2/5] Launching Chromium... FAIL` **even when the correct binary is resolved** (see the cwd=$HOME run above). `make-pdf/src/setup.ts:39` calls `browseClient.newtab("about:blank")`, but browse's URL allowlist rejects it:

```
$ browse newtab about:blank
Blocked: scheme "about:" is not allowed. Only http:, https:, and file: URLs are permitted.
(exit 1)
```

So the diagnostic tool reports a broken install on a working one (`generate` itself is fine — it calls `newtab()` with no URL). Bare `newtab` or a `file:` URL in the smoke test would fix it. Happy to split this into a separate issue if you prefer.

title: fix(browse): wait for web fonts before screenshots
body:
## Problem

Every screenshot capture path fires `page.screenshot()` immediately with no wait for web fonts. On any page using `@font-face` / Google Fonts, the shot lands mid-FOIT (flash of invisible/fallback text) — the fonts haven't downloaded yet, so text renders in a system fallback or blank. This shows up as "bad images" from `/qa`, `/design-review`, and `responsive` captures, especially on the first capture after navigation.

The `screenshot-size-guard` work already touched these same callsites; this is the timing gap right before them.

## Fix

New shared helper `browse/src/screenshot-utils.ts`:

```ts
export async function waitForFonts(page, timeoutMs = 3000) {
  // await document.fonts.ready, raced against a cap so lazy/streaming
  // fonts can't hang the capture; best-effort, never throws
}
```

Called before every full-page screenshot:

| File | Path |
|---|---|
| `meta-commands.ts` | `screenshot` (disk / `--base64` / `--clip` / `--selector`) |
| `meta-commands.ts` | `responsive` (per viewport — a resize can re-trigger font loads) |
| `write-commands.ts` | `prettyscreenshot` |
| `snapshot.ts` | annotated (`-a`) + heatmap |

It's best-effort and capped at 3s via `Promise.race`, so a page whose fonts never settle can't hang a capture, and a font-wait failure (navigation/context teardown race) never aborts the screenshot.

## Testing

- `browse/test/screenshot-utils.test.ts` — verifies the helper passes a numeric cap, defaults to a finite timeout, and never throws when `evaluate` rejects; plus a static invariant pinning that all three full-page callsites wire `waitForFonts` (mirrors the `screenshot-size-guard` test pattern).
- `bun test browse/test/screenshot-utils.test.ts` → 4 pass.
- `bash browse/scripts/build-node-server.sh` bundles cleanly.

title: benchmark-models: GeminiAdapter.parseStreamJson reads obj.text but current gemini CLI emits obj.content — empty runs row as $0 success
body:
## Symptom
`gstack-model-benchmark --models gemini` returns `output: "", tokens 0/0, costUsd 0` with NO error field — the row looks like a successful $0 run, silently mis-ranking gemini in any comparison table.

## Root cause
`test/helpers/providers/gemini.ts` `parseStreamJson` reads assistant text via:
```ts
if (obj.type === 'message' && typeof obj.text === 'string') { output += obj.text; }
```
but current gemini CLI `--output-format stream-json` emits `content` (with `role`), not `text`:
```json
{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":"PONG","delta":true}
{"type":"result","status":"success","stats":{"input_tokens":19920,"output_tokens":32,...}}
```
Tokens are likewise under `result.stats` (`input_tokens`/`output_tokens`), not `result.usage.input_token_count`; the model name arrives on the `init` event.

Note `test/helpers/gemini-session-runner.ts` was already updated to read `event.content` (with the `role === 'assistant'` guard) — the benchmark provider adapter was missed.

## Repro
`gstack-model-benchmark --prompt 'Reply with exactly the word: PONG' --models gemini --output json` on gemini CLI ≥ 0.x current (emits content-shape events). Verified on v1.58.5.0.

## Suggested fix (verified locally)
Additive fallbacks in `parseStreamJson`: accept `obj.content` when `obj.role === 'assistant'` (the role guard matters — the CLI echoes the user prompt as a `role:'user'` message event, which would otherwise concat into output); `obj.usage ?? obj.stats` with `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` fallbacks; read `modelUsed` from `init`. With that patch the same probe returns `output: 'PONG', tokens 24946/32`.

## Hardening ask
Independent of the field fix: an adapter run that produces EMPTY output with exit 0 should surface as an error row (or a loud flag), never a $0-success row — empty-success is indistinguishable from a healthy cheap run in the table.

title: Windows: playwright-core processLauncher launches chrome-headless-shell without windowsHide — console window per browser launch on the node path (follow-up to #2151, node_modules twin of #1989)
body:
## TL;DR

Follow-up to #2151 / PR #2153. With every gstack-owned spawn site fixed (polyfill `windowsHide`, signal-0 probe), Windows browse sessions **still** flash console windows — now titled `…\ms-playwright\chromium_headless_shell-1208\…\chrome-headless-shell.exe`. The remaining spawn surface is **playwright-core's own `processLauncher.js`**, which gstack does not control: it launches the browser without `windowsHide`, and its force-kill path shells out to `taskkill` (a `cmd.exe` window — the same class as the vendored-copy finding in #1989, but on the node/`node_modules` path).

## Root cause

Verified live: a browse daemon (`node …\browse\dist\server-node.mjs`) had `chrome-headless-shell.exe` as a direct child; the launch goes through `node_modules/playwright-core/lib/server/utils/processLauncher.js`:

```js
const spawnOptions = {
  detached: process.platform !== "win32",
  env: options.env,
  cwd: options.cwd,
  shell: options.shell,
  stdio
};                                      // ← no windowsHide
const spawnedProcess = childProcess.spawn(options.command, options.args || [], spawnOptions);
```

`chrome-headless-shell` is a console-subsystem executable. The browse daemon is console-less on Windows (detached node process), so without `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` the child allocates a **new visible console window** on every browser launch. Same file, force-kill path:

```js
const taskkillProcess = childProcess.spawnSync(`taskkill /pid ${spawnedProcess.pid} /T /F`, { shell: true });  // ← cmd.exe window per kill
```

Upstream playwright doesn't set `windowsHide` here, and there's no config/env knob to make it do so — so this can't be fixed from gstack's call sites the way #2153 fixed the polyfill.

## Relationship to open issues

- #1835 reports chrome-headless-shell black console windows (bun server context); this issue pins the node-path root cause to playwright's launcher and proposes a concrete mechanism.
- #1989 found the identical `taskkill` gap in the **vendored** playwright-core inside the compiled binary; this is the `node_modules` twin of that finding (the node path resolves playwright from `node_modules`, not the vendored copy).
- #2151 / #2153 fixed gstack's own spawn surfaces; this is the last remaining one on the node path.

## Proposed fix (PR incoming)

Bun's native `patchedDependencies`: `bun patch playwright-core`, add `windowsHide: true` to `spawnOptions` and to the `taskkill` `spawnSync` options, `bun patch --commit`. The patch applies automatically on every `bun install` — nothing changes for contributors or `./setup`.

Known caveat: bun applies patches per exact version (`playwright-core@1.58.2`), so a playwright bump would silently orphan the patch. The PR includes a tripwire test that reads the **installed** `node_modules` file and fails if the patch didn't apply — a version bump then fails CI instead of silently re-flashing consoles, and the fix is re-running `bun patch` against the new version.

Verified on Windows 11 (gstack v1.58.5.0 fork, bun 1.3.14): fresh `bun install` re-applies the patch; the patched launcher file carries both `windowsHide` sites.

## Env

- OS: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200
- gstack: main @ v1.58.5.0
- playwright-core: 1.58.2, Bun: 1.3.14, node 22 (server-node.mjs path)

title: context-restore reports NO_CHECKPOINTS in non-git dirs: save/restore compute different project slugs
body:
## Summary

`/context-restore` reports `NO_CHECKPOINTS` for a checkpoint that exists, when the working directory is a **non-git directory** (e.g. running straight from `$HOME`). Root cause: the project slug is computed two different ways between the save side and the restore side, so each reads/writes a different `~/.gstack/projects/<slug>/checkpoints` folder.

This has bitten me three separate times from the same home-folder workflow. Work done inside real project dirs (with a git remote) is unaffected — those get a stable slug from the remote URL.

## Environment

- gstack **1.58.5.0**
- macOS (Darwin 25.5.0)
- Working dir: `$HOME` (`/Users/<you>`), **not** a git repo

## Repro

1. From a non-git directory (e.g. your home folder), run a skill that saves a checkpoint (`/context-save`).
2. Later, from the same directory, run `/context-restore`.
3. Restore reports `NO_CHECKPOINTS` even though the checkpoint file exists on disk.

## What actually happens

The checkpoint got written under a **full-path** slug:

```
~/.gstack/projects/-Users-<you>/checkpoints/20260703-095500-....md
```

but `/context-restore` computed a **basename** slug and looked in:

```
~/.gstack/projects/<you>/checkpoints/          # empty → NO_CHECKPOINTS
```

Same directory, two different slugs.

## Root cause

`bin/gstack-slug` fallback order for a non-git dir with no cached slug is:

1. cached slug (`~/.gstack/slug-cache/<key>`)
2. git remote name — none here
3. `basename "$PWD"` → e.g. `harry333414`

So the *current* binary returns the **basename** for a non-git home dir. But the checkpoint on disk was saved under the **full slugified path** (`-Users-<you>`, slashes → dashes — the same scheme Claude Code uses for its own `.claude/projects/` dirs). The two schemes don't agree, so save and restore never meet.

Making it sticky: after the save, a `slug-cache` entry got written pinning the dir to the basename slug:

```
~/.gstack/slug-cache/_Users_<you>   ->   <you>
```

so every subsequent restore is now permanently pointed at the empty basename folder, even though the data lives under the full-path folder. The mismatch is self-perpetuating once the cache is written.

## Impact

- Silent data-appears-lost for any checkpoint/save workflow run from a non-git directory.
- `NO_CHECKPOINTS` is misleading — the file exists, restore is just looking in the wrong folder.
- Only affects non-git working dirs; git-repo projects slug off the remote and are stable.

## Suggested fixes (pick one)

1. **Make the slug scheme identical on both sides for non-git dirs.** Whatever `/context-save` used to land in `-Users-<you>` and whatever `gstack-slug` now returns (`<you>`) must be the same function. One canonical slugifier, called everywhere.
2. **Restore-side fallback:** if the canonical slug folder is empty/missing, also probe the full-path slug (and vice-versa) before declaring `NO_CHECKPOINTS`.
3. **One-time migration** in `gstack-upgrade/migrations/` that merges any `-Users-*` full-path project dirs into their basename equivalents and heals the slug-cache.

Happy to test a patch against this exact repro.

body:
## Context

Small-company founders need affordable executive judgment that compounds across decisions. The approved CEO/ENG/DESIGN plan defines an AI executive operating system with a persistent synthetic leadership team, but implementation must start with the domain architecture before UI, Slack/Teams, or live LLM role calls.

This epic builds the replayable boardroom foundation: typed events, snapshots, evidence ledger, meeting state machine, decision templates, role contracts, and golden simulations.

## Current State

Verified July 6, 2026.

- Existing append-only JSONL store: `lib/jsonl-store.ts`.
- Existing event-sourced decision memory: `lib/gstack-decision.ts`.
- Existing decision logging CLI: `bin/gstack-decision-log`.
- Existing tests for JSONL and event-sourced decisions: `test/jsonl-store.test.ts`, `test/gstack-decision.test.ts`.
- No boardroom-specific domain modules exist yet.
- Worktree has untracked `pascal_ideas/`; spec implementation should not depend on those files unless intentionally added later.

## Proposed Change

Create boardroom-specific domain modules using existing JSONL/event-sourced patterns, without overloading generic decision memory.

Dependency graph:

```text
#1 Boardroom Events
  ├─> #2 Company Snapshot + Read Model
  ├─> #3 Evidence Ledger
  ├─> #4 Meeting State Machine
  └─> #5 Decision Templates + Role Contracts
          └─> #6 Golden Boardroom Simulations
```

## Child Issues

| # | Title | Priority | Effort | Dependencies |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | Add boardroom event taxonomy and schema versioning | P1 | 1 day | none |
| 2 | Add company snapshot and boardroom read-model rebuilders | P1 | 1 day | #1 |
| 3 | Add immutable evidence ledger and claim references | P1 | 1 day | #1 |
| 4 | Add orchestrator-owned meeting state machine | P1 | 1 day | #1 |
| 5 | Add hiring/spend decision template and role contracts | P1 | 1 day | #1, #3 |
| 6 | Add golden boardroom simulation fixtures | P1 | 1 day | #1-#5 |

## Sequencing Rationale

Start with event taxonomy because every snapshot, evidence record, meeting phase, role output, and golden fixture depends on stable event shapes. Build snapshot/read-model and evidence ledger next because they define what role contracts may cite. Add meeting state and decision templates before fixtures so simulations test real phase and evidence-gate behavior rather than ad hoc flows.

## Implementation Details

Target files:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `lib/boardroom-events.ts` | Event union, schema versions, validators, append/read helpers |
| `lib/company-snapshot.ts` | Snapshot model and deterministic rebuild from events |
| `lib/evidence-ledger.ts` | Evidence records, extracted claims, freshness/dispute metadata |
| `lib/meeting-state.ts` | Phase enum, legal transitions, timeout/degraded states |
| `lib/decision-template.ts` | Hiring/spend template, required evidence gates |
| `lib/role-contracts.ts` | CFO/CRO/COO/Risk/Chief of Staff input/output schemas |
| `lib/boardroom-read-model.ts` | Boardroom table read model for future UI |
| `test/boardroom-*.test.ts` | Unit and golden simulation tests |
| `test/fixtures/boardroom/*.json` | Golden event streams and expected outputs |

Core event shape:

```ts
interface BoardroomEventBase {
  id: string;
  type: string;
  schemaVersion: 1;
  companyId: string;
  meetingId?: string;
  decisionId?: string;
  createdAt: string;
  actor: "human" | "orchestrator" | "role_worker" | "system";
}
```

Required event families:

- `company_fact_recorded`
- `evidence_added`
- `claim_extracted`
- `decision_opened`
- `meeting_phase_changed`
- `role_output_recorded`
- `dissent_recorded`
- `ceo_intervention_recorded`
- `decision_captured`
- `follow_up_assigned`

V1 storage:

- File-backed JSONL using existing `appendJsonl` / `readJsonl` patterns.
- Boardroom logs live under a boardroom-specific project path, not `decisions.jsonl`.
- Database migration is out of scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Boardroom event types are versioned and validated.
2. Snapshot rebuild from the same event stream is deterministic.
3. Evidence records are immutable and cited by stable IDs.
4. Role outputs cannot cite raw docs directly; they cite evidence/claim refs.
5. Meeting phase transitions reject illegal transitions.
6. Hiring/spend decision template defines required evidence gates.
7. Role contracts exist for CFO, CRO, COO, Risk, and Chief of Staff.
8. Golden fixtures cover normal flow, missing evidence, stale evidence, disputed claims, malformed role output, CEO intervention, timeout/degraded states, and follow-up generation.
9. `bun test test/boardroom-*.test.ts` passes.
10. Existing `bun test test/jsonl-store.test.ts test/gstack-decision.test.ts` still passes.
11. No UI, Slack/Teams, live LLM calls, avatars, or autonomous external actions are introduced.

## Testing Plan

| Layer | What | Count |
|---|---|---:|
| Unit | Event validation, evidence validation, transition validation | +15 |
| Unit | Snapshot/read-model rebuild determinism | +6 |
| Unit | Decision template evidence gates | +5 |
| Integration | Full hiring/spend event stream to snapshot/read model/memo/follow-ups | +3 |
| Regression | Existing JSONL and decision tests still pass | existing |

## Rollback Plan

Revert the PR. Since V1 adds isolated boardroom modules and test fixtures only, rollback does not require data migration. If local boardroom JSONL fixtures are created during tests, they must live under temp dirs and be deleted by test cleanup.

## Effort Estimate

Total: about 6 engineering days, or one focused Codex implementation pass per child issue.

| Component | Effort |
|---|---:|
| Boardroom event taxonomy | 1 day |
| Snapshot and read model | 1 day |
| Evidence ledger | 1 day |
| Meeting state machine | 1 day |
| Decision template and role contracts | 1 day |
| Golden simulations and regression tests | 1 day |

## Files Reference

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `lib/jsonl-store.ts` | Reuse append/read patterns; do not fork JSONL plumbing |
| `lib/gstack-decision.ts` | Reuse event-sourced pattern as reference; do not store boardroom data here |
| `bin/gstack-decision-log` | Reference CLI pattern only; boardroom CLI is not required in this spec |
| `test/jsonl-store.test.ts` | Regression coverage must remain green |
| `test/gstack-decision.test.ts` | Regression coverage must remain green |

## Out of Scope

- UI implementation.
- Slack/Teams integration.
- Live LLM role execution.
- Broad self-serve onboarding.
- Human fractional-exec marketplace.
- Video/avatar simulation.
- Autonomous writes to external systems.
- Database persistence.

## Definition of Done

1. All six child issues are represented as executable tasks or follow-up issues.
2. Boardroom domain tests pass on the Windows-safe test path.
3. Existing `jsonl-store` and `gstack-decision` tests still pass.
4. The next step can be `/design-shotgun` using concrete domain architecture.

title: feat(browse): opt-in automatic cookie persistence for the headless daemon
body:
## Opt-in automatic cookie persistence for the headless browse daemon

### Problem

Device-trust cookies set by a web app (the kind a site drops after you approve a
new device) do not survive a `browse` daemon restart. The daemon runs Playwright
with a non-persistent browser context, so every cookie — including long-lived
`__Host-`/`Secure` device-trust cookies — is gone the moment the context is torn
down. For any workflow that leans on `browse` against an authenticated site, this
means re-approving the device again and again after each restart. The server side
is fine; the gap is purely on the browse client.

### Root cause

Two things compound:

1. **Non-persistent context.** `browse` launches a fresh, in-memory browser
   context each boot. Nothing is written to disk, so cookies live only as long as
   the process.
2. **No auto-save.** There is no mechanism that captures cookies on shutdown or
   periodically and replays them on the next launch. Manual `cookies export` /
   `import` exists, but nothing does it automatically across the daemon lifecycle.

### Solution

Add **opt-in** automatic cookie persistence, off by default, gated behind
`BROWSE_AUTO_COOKIE_PERSIST=1`. When enabled, the daemon saves eligible cookies to
a per-workspace file and restores them into the context on the next launch. The
server itself is unchanged — this is entirely inside the browse client, and the
default behavior of every existing session is untouched.

When enabled, the feature emits a one-time plaintext-storage warning so the user
knows cookies are being written to disk.

### Design

- **Opt-in, default off.** `BROWSE_AUTO_COOKIE_PERSIST=1` turns it on; one-time
  plaintext warning on first save.
- **Persistent cookies only.** Only cookies with `expires !== -1 && expires > now`
  are saved. Session cookies are dropped. An optional
  `BROWSE_AUTO_COOKIE_DOMAINS` allowlist narrows what gets persisted, and
  internal/private-network hosts are excluded.
- **storageState-shaped file, cookies only.** Saved in Playwright's storageState
  shape but carrying cookies alone (no `localStorage`). `__Host-` prefixes and
  `partitionKey` are preserved verbatim so partitioned/`__Host-` cookies restore
  correctly.
- **Three save triggers.** Shutdown flush (just before context close), a debounce
  after mutating commands, and a periodic 60s flush. Crash-path emergency cleanup
  deliberately does **not** save (avoids persisting a torn state).
- **Single restore point.** State is injected once, at `launch()`, right before
  `newContext`. `recreateContext` is intentionally left alone to avoid a
  double-restore.
- **Per-workspace isolation + exclusive lock.** The state file is hashed from
  `realpath(projectDir)`, and an `mkdir`-based atomic lock (with dead-PID
  reclaim) prevents two daemons for the same workspace from clobbering each
  other's file.
- **Torn-write-safe writes.** State is written via a new `writeSecureFileAtomic`
  helper (temp file + `rename` + `fsync`, `0600` perms) so a crash mid-write never
  leaves a half-written state file.
- **Why not `launchPersistentContext`.** That would persist much more than
  cookies and collides with the existing `recreateContext` flow, so this stays on
  a targeted cookies-only storageState instead.

### Testing

`bun test browse/test/auto-cookie-persist.test.ts` → **20 pass, 0 fail**. Coverage
spans the unit level (eligibility filtering, `__Host-`/`partitionKey`
preservation, atomic write, lock acquire/dead-PID reclaim), a Playwright
round-trip (save cookies → restore into a fresh context), and a real
`BrowserManager.launch()` integration that confirms a persisted device-trust
cookie is restored on the next boot.

No regressions against `main`: the pre-existing failing tests (headed-browser
suites that need a Chromium build not installed in this environment) fail
identically on `main`, verified by comparing with the feature stashed.

### Commits (bisected)

- `feat(browse): add writeSecureFileAtomic for torn-write-safe state`
- `feat(browse): auto-cookie persistence module (opt-in, persistent-cookie-only)`
- `feat(browse): wire auto-cookie persistence into launch + daemon lifecycle`
- `test(browse): auto-cookie persistence — unit, round-trip, launch, wiring`
- `fix(browse): surface auto-cookie state read errors instead of swallowing`

title: gbrain serve (local-stdio MCP) holds PGLite exclusively; probe exit-124 misclassified as broken-config — /sync-gbrain deterministically skips code+memory inside any Claude session (lock variant of #1964, timeout raise cannot fix)
body:
## Symptom

Same output as the #1964 family (`#1792` `#1832` `#1969` `#2051`), but with a root cause none of them cover:

```
gstack-gbrain-sync (incremental):
  SKIP  code         skipped — local engine broken-config — config at ~/.gbrain/config.json is malformed; see /setup-gbrain Step 1.5 (0.9s)
  SKIP  memory       skipped — local engine broken-config — config at ~/.gbrain/config.json is malformed; see /setup-gbrain Step 1.5
  OK    brain-sync   curated artifacts pushed (2.8s)
```

Meanwhile the engine is healthy: `gbrain doctor --fast --json` answers with only warnings, and `~/.gbrain/config.json` is valid, well-formed JSON (pglite engine, voyage-code-3 embeddings).

## Root cause: `gbrain serve` holds the PGLite database exclusively

PGLite is an embedded single-process engine — whichever process opens `~/.gbrain/brain.pglite` owns it. With the recommended default setup (`/setup-gbrain` → PGLite + local-stdio MCP), **Claude Code spawns `gbrain serve` at session start, and serve opens the database eagerly at boot** — even if no `mcp__gbrain__*` tool is ever called in the session:

```
$ pgrep -fl gbrain
95427 bun /Users/.../.bun/bin/gbrain serve        # parent PID = the live `claude` process

$ lsof +D ~/.gbrain/brain.pglite | head -3
COMMAND   PID          USER   FD   TYPE   ... NAME
bun     95427 yannpringault    6u   REG   ... .../brain.pglite/pg_wal/000000010000000000000004
bun     95427 yannpringault    7u   REG   ... .../brain.pglite/global/2672
```

Every gbrain CLI command that needs the DB then times out at connect:

```
$ gbrain sources list --json
gbrain sources: connect timed out (default 10000ms; pass --timeout=Ns to override).
$ echo $?
124
```

`freshClassify` in `lib/gbrain-local-status.ts` probes exactly that command. The failure matches none of its patterns — stderr contains neither `"Cannot connect to database"` nor `"config.json"`, and the process wasn't killed by the classifier's own timer (gbrain exits 124 on its internal timeout, so `e.killed`/`SIGTERM`/`ETIMEDOUT` are all false) — and it falls through to the defensive default at `lib/gbrain-local-status.ts:304`: `broken-config`. The user is told their valid config is malformed.

Killing the serve process unblocks everything instantly — `gbrain sources list --json` returns in well under a second and the re-run syncs clean (`OK code ... page_count=130`). Which confirms it was a lock, not a slow engine.

## Why this is distinct from #1964 (and why its fix makes this variant worse)

#1964's cause is a *slow* connection (Supabase transaction-mode pooler, 6.9–10.7s) — raising the probe timeout fixes it. This variant is a *held lock*: the probe can **never** succeed while any Claude session is alive, because serve spawns per-session and owns the engine for the session's lifetime. A longer timeout just makes `/sync-gbrain` wait longer before mislabeling the same lock.

It also hits harder than the pooler variant: it affects the **default setup path** (PGLite + local-stdio is what `/setup-gbrain` recommends), and it's deterministic from the second session onward. It only ever works on setup day because the first sync runs before a session restart spawns serve. Every `/sync-gbrain` run inside a live Claude session hits it.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Classifier (gstack, small):** treat gbrain's own connect-timeout as its own state — match `"connect timed out"` in stderr and/or exit code 124 → a new `engine-locked`/`timeout` classification instead of the `broken-config` defensive default. Bonus: when the engine is pglite, check for a `gbrain serve` process (or `lsof` on the database path) and name the holding pid in the SKIP message — "database held by `gbrain serve` (pid N); stop it or run the sync outside a Claude session".
2. **Skill docs (gstack, tiny):** `/sync-gbrain`'s safety note already warns about racing `gbrain autopilot` (#1734); the session's own MCP serve process is the same class of conflict and deserves the same sentence.
3. **Upstream (gbrain):** the CLI should either proxy through a running serve or fail with "database held by pid N" instead of a generic connect timeout. Happy to file that on the gbrain repo if useful — flagging it here first since gstack owns the misdiagnosis and the user-facing message.

## Environment

- gstack 1.58.5.0, gbrain 0.42.57.0, macOS (darwin 24.6.0)
- Engine: PGLite, embeddings voyage-code-3 (1024d), schema pack gbrain-base-v2
- MCP: local-stdio, registered user-scope in Claude Code (spawns `gbrain serve` per session)
- Workaround that recurs every session: `kill $(pgrep -f "gbrain serve")` → `GSTACK_DETECT_NO_CACHE=1 /sync-gbrain` (the 60s classifier cache otherwise replays the stale negative)

title: gstack-repo-mode crashes on Windows Git Bash: stat -f means something different under GNU coreutils
body:
## Bug

`bin/gstack-repo-mode` crashes on Windows Git Bash (GNU coreutils):

```
gstack-repo-mode: line 40: File: unbound variable
```

Exit code 1.

## Root cause

The script's cache-check path runs `stat -f %m "$CACHE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y ...` as a BSD/macOS-vs-GNU fallback. On BSD/macOS, `-f` means "custom format string". On GNU coreutils (Windows Git Bash, Linux), `-f` means "display filesystem status instead of file status" — so the first branch doesn't fail over, it *succeeds* with unexpected multi-line `stat` filesystem output instead of a single mtime. That breaks the arithmetic substitution downstream under `set -euo pipefail`.

## Impact

Low in practice — `/review` and `/cso` both source this with `|| true`:

```bash
source <(~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-repo-mode 2>/dev/null) || true
```

So `REPO_MODE` silently degrades to `unknown` instead of blocking anything. But the failure is invisible unless you run the bin directly, and any skill logic branching on `REPO_MODE=solo` vs `collaborative` silently loses that signal on Windows.

## Repro

```bash
# Windows Git Bash (GNU coreutils), any repo with an existing 7-day cache file
~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-repo-mode
# gstack-repo-mode: line 40: File: unbound variable
# exit 1
```

## Suggested fix

Detect GNU vs BSD stat explicitly rather than relying on `-f` failing over, e.g.:

```bash
if stat --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # GNU coreutils
  mtime=$(stat -c %Y "$CACHE_FILE" 2>/dev/null)
else
  # BSD/macOS
  mtime=$(stat -f %m "$CACHE_FILE" 2>/dev/null)
fi
```

Possibly related to the same class of bash-portability issue as #824 (CDPATH breaking `bin/` scripts) — different root cause, same symptom category (POSIX-assumption bugs surfacing only on non-macOS shells).

Found while running `/review` and `/cso --comprehensive` for real (not just reading source) on a Windows Git Bash setup.

title: Install footprint: 1.1GB in ~/.claude/skills (739MB node_modules + 21MB .git) and connect-chrome duplicates open-gstack-browser
body:
Two packaging observations from a routine setup audit of a gstack install (v1.58.x):

**1. Install size.** The gstack skill directory is a full git clone weighing ~1.1GB inside `~/.claude/skills/gstack`: 739MB `node_modules`, 151MB `browse`, ~61MB each for `design`/`bin`/`make-pdf`, plus a 21MB `.git`. For a skills directory that agents scan every session, a slimmer release artifact (pruned dev dependencies, shallow/no .git, optional heavy modules downloaded on first use) would help.

**2. Duplicate skill registration.** `connect-chrome/` ships byte-identical to `open-gstack-browser/`, so both register as separate skills with the same content. Deleting one locally works until `/gstack-upgrade` restores it — probably worth deduplicating at the packaging level (alias or single skill).

title: connect-chrome and open-gstack-browser install with the same frontmatter name, so one silently shadows the other
body:
## Summary

`connect-chrome` and `open-gstack-browser` are installed into `~/.claude/skills/` as two separate skill directories that both declare `name: open-gstack-browser` in their frontmatter. Claude Code keys skills on that frontmatter name, so the two collide: one is silently discarded, and **which one survives follows unsorted `readdir` order**.

On my machine `connect-chrome` won, so `/open-gstack-browser` is not a registered command — even though `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, the router `SKILL.md`, and the sidebar extension's copy-to-clipboard button all tell users to run exactly that.

## Why it happens

In the repo, `connect-chrome` is a symlink to `open-gstack-browser` (one skill, correct). The collision is created at install time, by two independent paths:

1. **`bin/gstack-relink`** discovers skills with `for skill_dir in "$INSTALL_DIR"/*/`. The trailing-slash glob matches the `connect-chrome` symlink, and the loop names the installed entry from the *directory basename* while symlinking the canonical `SKILL.md` into it. Result: `skills/connect-chrome/SKILL.md -> .../open-gstack-browser/SKILL.md`, carrying `name: open-gstack-browser`.

2. **`setup`** then re-creates the same alias explicitly:
   ```bash
   # Backwards-compat alias: /connect-chrome → /open-gstack-browser
   _OGB_LINK="$INSTALL_SKILLS_DIR/connect-chrome"
   ...
   _link_or_copy "gstack/open-gstack-browser" "$_OGB_LINK"
   ```
   which symlinks the alias directory straight at the canonical skill directory — so its `SKILL.md` is, again, the canonical one.

Note that `setup`'s own `link_claude_skill_dirs` is *not* the culprit: it derives the entry name from the frontmatter `name:`, so it maps both directories onto a single `open-gstack-browser` target. Only the two paths above mint a second, differently-named directory holding the same frontmatter name.

## Reproduction

Against `11de390` (v1.58.5.0), using only the shipped scripts:

```bash
T=$(mktemp -d); I="$T/gstack-install"; S="$T/skills"
mkdir -p "$I/bin" "$S"
cp bin/gstack-config bin/gstack-relink bin/gstack-patch-names "$I/bin/"; chmod +x "$I/bin"/*
mkdir -p "$I/open-gstack-browser"
printf -- '---\nname: open-gstack-browser\ndescription: launch\n---\n# ogb\n' > "$I/open-gstack-browser/SKILL.md"
ln -s open-gstack-browser "$I/connect-chrome"          # exactly as the repo ships it
printf -- '---\nname: gstack\ndescription: root\n---\n# root\n' > "$I/SKILL.md"

GSTACK_STATE_DIR="$T" GSTACK_INSTALL_DIR="$I" GSTACK_SKILLS_DIR="$S" "$I/bin/gstack-config" set skill_prefix false
GSTACK_STATE_DIR="$T" GSTACK_INSTALL_DIR="$I" GSTACK_SKILLS_DIR="$S" "$I/bin/gstack-relink"

for d in "$S"/*/; do
  echo "$(basename "$d") -> $(grep -m1 '^name:' "$d/SKILL.md")"
done
```

Actual:

```
_gstack-command -> name: gstack
connect-chrome -> name: open-gstack-browser      # <-- collides
open-gstack-browser -> name: open-gstack-browser # <-- collides
```

Expected: three distinct names.

This also matches a real install (`~/.claude/skills/connect-chrome/SKILL.md` is a symlink into `gstack/connect-chrome/SKILL.md`).

## Impact

- `/open-gstack-browser` is missing on an arbitrary subset of installs, while every doc and the browser extension reference it.
- Which command exists is non-deterministic across machines, so the failure is hard to reproduce and reads to users as "gstack is broken on my laptop."
- A user auditing their skills sees two entries for one skill.

## Suggested fix

Install the backwards-compat alias as a *thin skill with its own `name:`* that delegates to the canonical skill, rather than as a symlink to the canonical skill directory. Then both `/connect-chrome` and `/open-gstack-browser` register, on every machine.

I have a PR ready that does this in `bin/gstack-relink` (making it the single owner of the alias), removes the now-duplicated alias blocks from `setup`, and adds five regression tests to `test/relink.test.ts` covering the name-uniqueness invariant, the `skill_prefix` flip, idempotency, and in-place upgrade of existing symlinked aliases.

## Environment

- gstack `11de390` (v1.58.5.0)
- Claude Code 2.1.205, native install, macOS 15 (Darwin 25.5.0)
- bun 1.3.14

title: setup: cleanup_old_claude_symlinks() derives orphans from the payload dir, so it can never clean orphans (37 dead skill dirs, ~3 months)
body:
## Summary

`cleanup_old_claude_symlinks()` discovers orphaned skill directories by iterating the gstack payload directory. When the payload is gone — which is exactly when orphans exist — the loop body never executes, so the orphans are never cleaned. The function is structurally incapable of running in the situation it exists to handle.

In my case this left **37 dead skill directories** in a project repo for roughly three months. Each `.claude/skills/<name>/` contained only a `SKILL.md` symlink into a `.claude/skills/gstack/` payload that no longer existed. They never loaded; nothing surfaced an error; `/gstack-upgrade` never repaired them.

Verified present on `origin/main` @ `11de390` (v1.58.5.0).

## The defect

`setup:613` (as of `11de390`):

```bash
cleanup_old_claude_symlinks() {
  local gstack_dir="$1"
  local skills_dir="$2"
  local removed=()
  for skill_dir in "$gstack_dir"/*/; do        # <-- iterates the PAYLOAD
    if [ -f "$skill_dir/SKILL.md" ]; then
      ...
      elif [ -d "$old_target" ] && [ -L "$old_target/SKILL.md" ]; then
        link_dest="$(readlink "$old_target/SKILL.md" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        case "$link_dest" in
          *gstack*) rm -rf "$old_target"; removed+=("$skill_name") ;;
```

The list of directories to clean is derived from `"$gstack_dir"/*/`. If `$gstack_dir` has been deleted, the glob doesn't match, the loop body never runs, and zero orphans are removed. The orphans live in `$skills_dir`, not `$gstack_dir` — that's where the scan should happen.

## Why `/gstack-upgrade` can't recover

`gstack-upgrade/SKILL.md`, install-type detection:

```bash
elif [ -d ".claude/skills/gstack" ]; then       INSTALL_TYPE="vendored"
elif [ -d "$HOME/.claude/skills/gstack" ]; then INSTALL_TYPE="vendored-global"
```

Once the project payload is deleted, detection falls through to `vendored-global`. Every subsequent upgrade operates on `$HOME/.claude/skills/gstack` and never revisits the project directory. The orphans are permanent — I had to remove them by hand.

## How the payload likely disappeared

The team-mode branch in `gstack-upgrade/SKILL.md` deletes the payload and does not touch its 37 siblings:

```bash
git rm -r --cached .claude/skills/gstack/ 2>/dev/null || true
if ! grep -qF '.claude/skills/gstack/' .gitignore 2>/dev/null; then
  echo '.claude/skills/gstack/' >> .gitignore
fi
rm -rf "$LOCAL_GSTACK"
```

My repo's `.gitignore` contains exactly that appended line, committed the same day the 37 symlinks were created. I want to be careful here: I **cannot prove** this branch ran — `gstack-config get team_mode` returns empty on my machine today, and the `.gitignore` line landed inside a human commit, so it may have been added by hand.

It also doesn't matter much, because the payload is gitignored in the vendored layout, so **any** of these removes it with no way back:

- `git clean -fdx`
- a fresh clone or `git worktree add`
- the team-mode branch above

Whatever the trigger, `cleanup_old_claude_symlinks()` cannot subsequently clean up. That's the part worth fixing.

## Reproduction

```bash
# from a repo with a vendored gstack install
rm -rf .claude/skills/gstack          # simulate clean -fdx / fresh worktree / team-mode branch
~/.claude/skills/gstack/setup         # or: /gstack-upgrade

# every .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md is now a dangling symlink, and stays that way
find .claude/skills -maxdepth 2 -name SKILL.md -type l ! -exec test -e {} \; -print
```

These orphans are easy to miss: a directory whose `SKILL.md` is a dangling symlink is invisible to `[ -f "$d/SKILL.md" ]` but still shows up in `find` and in a plain `ls`. `diff -rq` against a good copy reports `DIFFERS`, which reads as "contents differ" and sent me down the wrong path for a while.

## Suggested fix

Scan the destination, not the source. Roughly:

```bash
cleanup_old_claude_symlinks() {
  local gstack_dir="$1" skills_dir="$2"
  local removed=()
  for old_target in "$skills_dir"/*/; do
    [ -L "$old_target/SKILL.md" ] || continue
    link_dest="$(readlink "$old_target/SKILL.md" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    case "$link_dest" in *gstack*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
    # dangling, or points into the payload we're replacing → stale either way
    if [ ! -e "$old_target/SKILL.md" ] || [ -n "$gstack_dir" ]; then
      rm -rf "$old_target"
      removed+=("$(basename "$old_target")")
    fi
  done
  [ ${#removed[@]} -gt 0 ] && echo "  cleaned up old entries: ${removed[*]}"
}
```

This keeps the existing migration behavior (payload present → clean the flat names it's replacing) and additionally reaps dangling `*gstack*` symlinks when the payload is gone. The `*gstack*` guard on `readlink` preserves the current provenance check, so user-authored skills are never touched.

Two smaller things that would have helped independently:

1. **`setup` could warn** when it finds `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` symlinks with no payload, even if it declines to delete them.
2. **The team-mode branch** in `gstack-upgrade/SKILL.md` should call the cleanup helper after `rm -rf "$LOCAL_GSTACK"`, rather than leaving the siblings behind.

## Environment

- gstack `1.58.5.0` (`11de390`), global install at `~/.claude/skills/gstack`
- macOS (Darwin 27.0.0), Claude Code `2.1.205`
- Affected project had a vendored install created 2026-04-12; orphans discovered and removed 2026-07-09

## Possibly related

- #954 — `setup` creates absolute symlinks for vendored installs, breaks portability
- #896 (closed) — `gstack-uninstall` leaves orphaned `~/.claude/skills/gstack-*` directories (prefix-mode)
- #1882 — skills hardcode `~/.claude/skills/gstack/` paths

Distinct from all three: this is the *flat-name* layout, the payload is absent rather than misnamed or non-portable, and the failure is in cleanup reachability rather than path resolution.

title: gstack-config key validator rejects brain_trust_policy@local (endpoint-hash returns literal 'local' for local engines)
body:
## What happened

`/setup-gbrain` Step 9.5 persists the brain trust policy with:

```bash
~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-config set brain_trust_policy@$_HASH personal
```

where `_HASH=$(gstack-config endpoint-hash)`. For local engines (PGLite path), `endpoint-hash` returns the literal string `local`, but gstack-config's key validator only accepts hex suffixes after `@` (`@[a-f0-9]+`), so the `set` call is rejected and the policy is never persisted under the per-endpoint key.

## Impact

- Step 9.5 fails on every fresh local-PGLite setup (the default try-first path).
- On subsequent runs, `gstack-config get brain_trust_policy@local` returns unset, so skills see the policy as never-set and retry the auto-set each time (harmless but noisy, and the per-endpoint tracking the feature was built for never engages for local engines).
- `/sync-gbrain` Step 1's trust-policy gate hits the same mismatch.

## Workaround

Store under the plain key: `gstack-config set brain_trust_policy personal`. Works, but loses the per-endpoint scoping.

## Suggested fix (either works)

1. Allow `local` as a valid endpoint-hash value in the key validator (`@([a-f0-9]+|local)`), or
2. Have `endpoint-hash` return a stable hex digest for local engines instead of the literal `local`.

## Environment

- gstack 1.58.5.0, macOS (Darwin 25.5.0)
- gbrain 0.42.26.0, engine=pglite, mode=local-stdio
- Repro: fresh `/setup-gbrain` picking Path 3 (PGLite local), reach Step 9.5
