title: Windows: link_codex_skill_dirs skips already-installed skill dirs on re-run — ./setup --host codex reports ready but never refreshes SKILL.md (same guard in factory/opencode)
body:
## Summary

On Windows (MSYS2/Git Bash, MINGW64), `./setup --host codex` reports `gstack ready (codex).` and exits 0, but **never refreshes the SKILL.md of skills that are already installed**. Only the very first install lands; every subsequent run after a `git pull` is a silent no-op for `~/.codex/skills/gstack-*/`.

This is the Codex-side twin of #1456 (`link_claude_skill_dirs`, fixed in v1.38.0.0). The `_link_or_copy` fallback introduced by that fix exists and works — it just isn't reachable on re-runs here, because of the guard in front of it. The same guard is present in `link_factory_skill_dirs` and `link_opencode_skill_dirs`.

## Root cause

`setup`, `link_codex_skill_dirs`, line 731 (at `a325940`, VERSION `1.60.1.0`):

```bash
target="$skills_dir/$skill_name"
# Create or update symlink
if [ -L "$target" ] || [ ! -e "$target" ]; then
  _link_or_copy "$skill_dir" "$target"
  linked+=("$skill_name")
fi
```

The copy only runs when the target is a **symlink** or **does not exist**.

- On macOS/Linux the target is always a symlink → the condition passes on every run → skills refresh.
- On Windows, `_link_or_copy` deliberately does `rm -rf "$dst"; cp -R "$src" "$dst"`, so the target is a **real directory**. From the second run onward, `-L "$target"` is false and `! -e "$target"` is false → **the whole block is skipped**.

The comment on line 730 ("Create or update symlink") describes an update path that Windows can never take.

`link_claude_skill_dirs` does not have this problem: it calls `_link_or_copy` unconditionally for `SKILL.md` (line 571) and additionally carries an explicit Windows branch for a real-directory target:

```bash
elif [ "$IS_WINDOWS" -eq 1 ] && [ -d "$prefixed_target" ] && [ -f "$prefixed_target/SKILL.md" ]; then
  rm -rf "$prefixed_target"
```

The Codex/Factory/OpenCode paths never got that treatment.

Same guard, same missing `IS_WINDOWS` branch:

| Function | Line |
|---|---|
| `link_codex_skill_dirs` | 731 |
| `link_factory_skill_dirs` | 932 |
| `link_opencode_skill_dirs` | 964 |

## Minimal repro (no gstack needed — isolates the guard)

```bash
SRC=/tmp/guard-test/src/gstack-demo
DST=/tmp/guard-test/dst/gstack-demo
mkdir -p "$SRC" "$(dirname "$DST")"

echo "v1-original" > "$SRC/SKILL.md"
cp -R "$SRC" "$DST"                 # first run: Windows _link_or_copy => real directory

echo "v2-UPDATED" > "$SRC/SKILL.md" # upstream ships a doc change

# second run, guard as written at line 731:
if [ -L "$DST" ] || [ ! -e "$DST" ]; then
  cp -R "$SRC" "$DST"
fi

cat "$DST/SKILL.md"
# => v1-original      the update never landed, and nothing was printed
```

## Full repro on Windows

```bash
cd ~/.claude/skills/gstack
git pull
./setup --host codex
```

Observed:

- Log ends with `gstack ready (codex).` and **no `linked skills:` line at all** (the `linked` array stays empty because the guard skipped every iteration). The `--host claude` run on the same machine does print its `linked skills:` line.
- `ls -la ~/.codex/skills/gstack-careful/SKILL.md` still shows the **install-time mtime**, days older than the pull.

## What made this hard to notice

`create_codex_runtime_root` runs on the same invocation and **does** rewrite `~/.codex/skills/gstack/` (sidecar `bin/`, `browse/`, `review/`, `ETHOS.md`). So implementation changes under `bin/` do land, while changes to generated skill **docs** silently do not. On my machine, after fast-forwarding `7c9df1c` → `a325940`:

- `~/.codex/skills/gstack/bin/` — 76 files, byte-identical to the repo. Refreshed correctly.
- `~/.codex/skills/gstack-*/SKILL.md` — untouched, install-time mtime.

I compared all 53 generated docs (`.agents/skills/gstack*/SKILL.md`) against the installed ones and got 53 identical / 0 different, so this particular range happened to change no Codex doc. That is luck, not correctness: the first update that does change a generated SKILL.md will leave Codex stale while `setup` reports success.

This also directly contradicts the note `setup` prints a few lines earlier on Windows:

> note: Windows install uses file copies (no Developer Mode required). Re-run ./setup after every 'git pull' to refresh skill files.

Re-running is exactly what does not refresh them.

## Expected behavior

`./setup --host codex` after a `git pull` refreshes every installed `gstack-*` skill doc on Windows, the same way the Claude host path does.

## Suggested fix

Mirror the `link_claude_skill_dirs` approach — add the Windows real-directory branch in all three functions:

```bash
      target="$skills_dir/$skill_name"
      if [ -L "$target" ] || [ ! -e "$target" ]; then
        _link_or_copy "$skill_dir" "$target"
        linked+=("$skill_name")
      elif [ "$IS_WINDOWS" -eq 1 ] && [ -d "$target" ] && [ -f "$target/SKILL.md" ]; then
        # Previous run left a real directory copy (no Developer Mode) — refresh it,
        # otherwise `git pull` + ./setup silently keeps install-time docs.
        _link_or_copy "$skill_dir" "$target"
        linked+=("$skill_name")
      fi
```

Since `_link_or_copy` already starts with `rm -rf "$dst"` on Windows, calling it unconditionally would work too.

Worth extending `test/setup-windows-fallback.test.ts` with an invariant in the spirit of the existing D7 assertion: every `link_*_skill_dirs` that can receive a non-symlink target must have a refresh path, so the next host added does not reintroduce this.

## Workaround for users on Windows

```bash
rm -rf ~/.codex/skills/gstack-* && cd ~/.claude/skills/gstack && ./setup --host codex
```

Deleting the targets makes `! -e "$target"` true again, so the copy runs.

## Environment

- gstack `a325940`, VERSION `1.60.1.0`
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Git Bash (MINGW64), Developer Mode off
- bun 1.3.14, Node v24.16.0
- Hosts installed: Claude Code 2.1.193 and Codex

title: browse: hover scrolls its target and the tab persists across sessions — both silently invalidate screenshots
body:
Two daemon behaviours that silently invalidate a verification pass. Both are doc-level: the tool is behaving as designed, but the design surprises you in a way that produces confidently wrong output rather than an error.

Hit while running a screenshot audit loop on a local page with `browse` v1.45.0.0.

### 1. `hover` scrolls its target into view

`SKILL.md` already warns that the mouse stays where you left it, and tells you to park it somewhere neutral before a rest-state shot. What it does not say is that parking is itself a navigation.

```bash
$B hover ".kp-sub"          # in view — fine
$B hover ".kp-practices"    # below the fold — scrolls the page
$B screenshot out.png --viewport
```

The second call scrolled to roughly y=700. The screenshot came back showing a completely different section of the page, labelled as the hero's resting state. No warning, exit 0.

The existing advice ("park it somewhere neutral") actively leads you into this. The natural neutral target is a large inert container, and those tend to be below the fold.

**Suggested wording:**

> Never park the mouse on an element below the fold. `hover` scrolls its target into view, so parking on a lower section silently scrolls the page and the rest-state shot captures the wrong part of the site. Park on something non-interactive that is already visible, then assert `window.scrollY` before shooting.

### 2. The tab can drift, and `reload` follows it

The daemon holds one tab across commands, which is the point. But it also holds it across *sessions*. My tab had been left on a different local page by earlier work. My next `reload` reloaded that page.

Every subsequent measurement then described a document I had never opened:

```
rule .kp-brand:hover = false
rule a:focus-visible = false
btn padding = NOFOUND
line-hi count = 0
```

That reads exactly like a stylesheet that failed to apply. I spent a round debugging CSS that was fine. The tell was buried in the `reload` output, which echoed the other page's URL.

**Suggested wording:**

> Pin the address before every verification run. The daemon holds one tab across commands and sessions. `reload` reloads whatever that tab is on, not your page, and measurements come back describing a document you never opened. Always `goto` the explicit URL, then confirm with `browse js "location.href"`.

### Why doc-level and not a code fix

Both behaviours are reasonable. Scroll-into-view is correct for interaction, and a persistent tab is the feature. The cost is that the failure is silent and the output looks legitimate. A line in the skill file is enough, since that file is what the agent reads before acting.

If a code change is wanted, the cheapest would be `reload` printing its URL more prominently, or a `--expect-url` guard. Happy to send a PR against `browse/SKILL.md.tmpl` if the wording above is close.

title: Windows/Codex: plan-eng-review inline office-hours path is not installed by setup
body:
## Summary

After running the official Codex setup on Windows through Git Bash:

```bash
./setup --host codex --prefix
```

the generated `gstack-plan-eng-review` skill instructs Codex to inline-read `office-hours` from:

```bash
GSTACK_ROOT="$HOME/.codex/skills/gstack"
$GSTACK_ROOT/office-hours/SKILL.md
```

However, setup installs the skill at:

```text
$HOME/.codex/skills/gstack-office-hours/SKILL.md
```

and does not create:

```text
$HOME/.codex/skills/gstack/office-hours/SKILL.md
```

As a result, the official inline `office-hours` step in `plan-eng-review` points to a path that does not exist.

## Environment

- Windows
- Git Bash
- Codex host
- gstack `1.60.1.0`
- setup flags: `--host codex --prefix`

## Reproduction

1. Run the official setup command above.
2. Check the installed paths:

```bash
test -f "$HOME/.codex/skills/gstack-office-hours/SKILL.md"   # succeeds
test -f "$HOME/.codex/skills/gstack/office-hours/SKILL.md"   # fails
```

3. Inspect the generated `$HOME/.codex/skills/gstack-plan-eng-review/SKILL.md`. It sets `GSTACK_ROOT="$HOME/.codex/skills/gstack"` and later reads `$GSTACK_ROOT/office-hours/SKILL.md`.

## Source mismatch

In `hosts/codex.ts`, the Codex transform rewrites `~/.claude/skills/gstack` to `$GSTACK_ROOT`. The Codex global runtime symlink list does not include `office-hours`. Meanwhile, setup exposes generated skills as top-level `gstack-*` directories under `$HOME/.codex/skills`.

## Expected behavior

Either:

1. The generated parent skill should inline-read the actual installed `gstack-office-hours/SKILL.md` path, or
2. Setup should install/link `office-hours` under `$GSTACK_ROOT/office-hours`.

The important behavior is to preserve the documented inline execution inside `plan-eng-review`, rather than launching `office-hours` as a separate full skill.

## Temporary workaround

A Windows directory Junction from:

```text
$HOME/.codex/skills/gstack/office-hours
```

to:

```text
$HOME/.codex/skills/gstack-office-hours
```

makes the inline read work, and the two `SKILL.md` files can be hash-verified as identical. This is only a local workaround because a future setup/upgrade may recreate the runtime root.

title: fix: raise gbrain version-probe timeout to 10s on Windows
body:
## Problem

On Windows the gbrain CLI is a `.cmd` shim that runs `bun run cli.ts`. A cold spawn takes over 2s (warm runs are ~700ms). `resolveGbrainBin` in `lib/gbrain-local-status.ts` probes `gbrain --version` with a 2s timeout, so the cold probe times out and `localEngineStatus` returns `no-cli`. The 60s status cache then serves that false negative to every skill preamble and sync run. Net effect: `/sync-gbrain` skips the memory stage with "gbrain CLI not on PATH; install via /setup-gbrain" on a machine where the CLI works.

## Fix

Add `VERSION_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`: 10s when `NEEDS_SHELL_ON_WINDOWS`, 2s otherwise. Used by both `resolveGbrainBin` and `readGbrainVersion`. POSIX keeps the cheap 2s probe; only the Windows shim path gets headroom.

## Verification

On Windows 11 (bun 1.3.14, gbrain 0.42.59.0):
- Before: `gstack-gbrain-detect` reported `gbrain_on_path: false`, `gbrain_local_status: "no-cli"`; sync skipped the memory stage.
- After: detect reports `gbrain_on_path: true`, `gbrain_local_status: "ok"`; memory stage runs (`OK memory — persisted 23 pages`).
- `bun test test/gbrain-local-status.test.ts` shows the same 7 pass / 17 fail before and after the patch on this Windows machine — the 17 failures are pre-existing environment issues (the tests build fake POSIX shims on PATH), not caused by this change.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix: exec gstack-brain-sync through bash on Windows
body:
## Problem

The #1731 fix gated the orchestrator's brain-sync spawns behind `shell: NEEDS_SHELL_ON_WINDOWS`, but that routes through cmd.exe, which cannot execute an extensionless bash shebang script. Every `/sync-gbrain` run on Windows errors:

```
'C:\Users\...\gstack\bin\gstack-brain-sync' is not recognized as an internal or external command
```

and the stage reports `ERR brain-sync — gstack-brain-sync exited 1`.

## Fix

In `runBrainSyncPush` (bin/gstack-gbrain-sync.ts), exec the script through bash explicitly on Windows: `spawnSync("bash", [brainSyncPath, flag])`. Git Bash ships with git, which gstack already requires, so bash is a safe dependency. POSIX keeps the direct shebang exec with no shell. Spawn errors (e.g. bash missing from PATH) now surface in the stage summary instead of a bare exit code.

The #1731 tripwire test pinned the old shape (`spawnSync(brainSyncPath, ...)` with the shell flag), so it is updated to pin the new invariant: brain-sync spawns must exec bash on Windows and must not rely on `shell: true`.

## Verification

On Windows 11 (bun 1.3.14):
- Before: `ERR brain-sync — gstack-brain-sync exited 1` with the "not recognized" cmd error.
- After: `OK brain-sync — curated artifacts pushed (0.2s)`.
- `bun test test/gbrain-spawn-windows-shell.test.ts`: 5 pass, 0 fail.

Related: #2450 fixes the separate Windows probe-timeout false-negative in the same sync pipeline.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix: Windows build and ACL issues
body:
Fixes two Windows-specific issues that prevented gstack from working out-of-the-box:

1. **Build failure for browse/server-node.mjs**
   - On Windows (MSYS/Git Bash), Bun cannot resolve MSYS-style `/c/...` absolute paths.
   - The build-node-server.sh script now converts the GSTACK_DIR to a Windows-style path via `cygpath -m` when running under MINGW/MSYS/CYGWIN.

2. **ACL lockout on .gstack directory**
   - gstack's file-permissions.ts used bare username (`chirag`) for icacls grants.
   - When the hostname equals the username (e.g., host `CHIRAG`, user `chirag`), the bare name resolves to the *machine SID* instead of the user SID.
   - This left the real user without access to the .gstack directory, causing EPERM on reads/writes and the "Another instance is starting the server, waiting..." loop.
   - Changed to use the fully-qualified `%USERDOMAIN%\%USERNAME%` (with fallback to the SID via `whoami /user`) so the correct user gets access.

After applying these patches:
- A fresh `.gstack` directory is created with the correct `CHIRAG\chirag:(OI)(CI)(F)` ACL.
- The browse server starts successfully (tested with `browse goto https://example.com` → text extraction).
- Both the Bun-compiled `browse.exe` and the Node.js compatibility bundle (`server-node.mjs`) are built and functional.

Tested on:
- Windows 10 (MSYS2/Git Bash from git-bash)
- Bun 1.3.14
- Node 24.18.0

Fixes:
- "FileNot able to build browse/server-node.mjs on Windows (FileNotFound opening root directory)"
- Browse server fails with EPERM on .gstack directory due to mistaken ACL granting machine SID

Related to: https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/issues/997 (the codesign note is unrelated, but same class of Windows-specific issues)

title: fix: preserve gbrain argv on Windows without a shell
body:
## Summary

- run direct `gbrain` invocations through `cross-spawn` without `shell: true`
- centralize synchronous, text, and asynchronous argv handling
- preserve source IDs, paths, and search arguments as literal argv values
- exercise the regression in the existing `windows-latest` test job

## Why

On Windows, launching the `gbrain.cmd` shim through Node's shell mode can reinterpret argument metacharacters. `cross-spawn` resolves the command shim while keeping the argument vector separate from a composed shell command.

This is a focused alternative to #2272. That PR includes broader Windows runtime and release changes; this one intentionally limits scope to direct `gbrain` process creation and its regression coverage.

## Validation

- `bun run build`
- targeted gbrain tests: 38 passed, 0 failed
- full `bun run test` completed locally with exit 0; relevant targeted tests are clean

Windows CI now runs both the argv round-trip and shell-free adapter invariants.

title: setup: Claude host installer drops review/qa/etc. runtime assets (only copies SKILL.md)
body:
### Summary

`./setup` for the Claude host only copies each skill's `SKILL.md` (and a `sections/` dir, if present) into `~/.claude/skills/<name>/`. Skills whose `SKILL.md` reads sibling runtime files at a path like `.claude/skills/<name>/<file>` — `review/`, `qa/`, `plan-devex-review/`, `gstack-upgrade/`, `careful/`, `freeze/` — end up broken after a clean install, because those files never get copied for the Claude host.

`/review` is the clearest case: its `SKILL.md` says "Read `.claude/skills/review/checklist.md`... If the file cannot be read, STOP and report the error," but that file is never installed for the Claude host, so `/review` cannot run its structured pipeline out of the box.

### Root cause

`link_claude_skill_dirs()` in `setup` (around line 540) only handles `SKILL.md` and `sections/`:

```bash
# setup:566-579
_link_or_copy "$gstack_dir/$dir_name/SKILL.md" "$target/SKILL.md"
if [ -d "$gstack_dir/$dir_name/sections" ]; then
  ...
  _link_or_copy "$gstack_dir/$dir_name/sections" "$target/sections"
fi
```

Compare this to `create_codex_runtime_root()` (around line 808), `create_factory_runtime_root()` (~848), and `create_opencode_runtime_root()` (~890), which all explicitly copy `review/`'s runtime files:

```bash
# setup:808-816 (Codex host)
# Review runtime assets (individual files, NOT the whole review/ dir which has SKILL.md)
for f in checklist.md design-checklist.md greptile-triage.md TODOS-format.md; do
  if [ -f "$gstack_dir/review/$f" ]; then
    _link_or_copy "$gstack_dir/review/$f" "$codex_gstack/review/$f"
  fi
done
```

The Claude host (the primary target for most users) never got the equivalent treatment. This isn't Windows-specific — `_link_or_copy` falls back to `cp` there, but on macOS/Linux the same gap exists via `ln -snf`, since `link_claude_skill_dirs` simply never references these files at all for any platform.

### Repro

```bash
cd ~/.claude/skills/gstack && ./setup   # default: --host claude
ls ~/.claude/skills/review/
# SKILL.md   <- only this. checklist.md, design-checklist.md,
#               greptile-triage.md, TODOS-format.md, specialists/ all missing
```

Then invoke `/review` in a project with a real diff: it hits Step 2 ("Read `.claude/skills/review/checklist.md`") and stops with "file cannot be read."

### Affected skills (source has extra runtime files the Claude-host installer drops)

| Skill | Missing after `./setup` |
|---|---|
| `review` | `checklist.md`, `design-checklist.md`, `greptile-triage.md`, `TODOS-format.md`, `specialists/` |
| `qa` | `references/`, `templates/` |
| `plan-devex-review` | `dx-hall-of-fame.md` |
| `gstack-upgrade` | `migrations/` |
| `careful` | `bin/` |
| `freeze` | `bin/` |

(`sections/` is handled correctly for `cso`, `design-consultation`, `document-release`, `office-hours`, `plan-ceo-review`, `plan-design-review`, `plan-eng-review`, `ship`, etc. — only non-`sections/` extras are affected.)

### Suggested fix

Generalize `link_claude_skill_dirs()` to copy any non-`SKILL.md`/`SKILL.md.tmpl` sibling (not just `sections/`), the way `create_codex_runtime_root()` already special-cases `review/`. Or extract the per-host "review runtime assets" list into a shared helper called from all five host installers (Claude, Codex, Factory, OpenCode, Kiro) instead of duplicating (and, in Claude's case, omitting) it per host.

### Environment

- gstack VERSION: `1.60.1.0`
- OS: Windows (MINGW64/Git Bash, `MINGW64_NT-10.0-26200`)
- Host: `claude` (default, no `--host` flag)
- `./setup` run with no arguments

title: gstack-diff-scope misses db/data data migrations, so /review skips the data-migration specialist
body:
`gstack-diff-scope` classifies database *schema* migrations but not *data* migrations, so `SCOPE_MIGRATIONS` stays `false` on a diff that contains only data migrations, and `/review` silently skips the data-migration specialist.

## Where

`bin/gstack-diff-scope`, the migrations case arm:

```sh
db/migrate/*|*/migrations/*|alembic/*|prisma/migrations/*) MIGRATIONS=true ;;
```

The Rails [`data_migrate`](https://github.com/ilyakatz/data-migrate) gem — the common way to ship data migrations in Rails — puts them in `db/data/`, not `db/migrate/`. Since the `case` matches one pattern per file, `db/data/20260804123456_backfill_x.rb` falls through to `*.rb) BACKEND=true` and never sets `MIGRATIONS`.

## Repro

On a branch whose diff includes `db/data/<timestamp>_*.rb`:

```
$ gstack-diff-scope master
SCOPE_MIGRATIONS=false   # expected true
SCOPE_BACKEND=true
```

## Why it matters

`data-migrate` runs these files as **arbitrary Ruby against production data**, typically unattended in a release/deploy phase. That is a strictly higher-risk artifact than a schema migration, and it is exactly what the data-migration specialist checklist is for (idempotency, re-run safety, missing-row assumptions, `down` correctness). `data-migration` is marked `[NEVER_GATE]`, which signals it should always run when relevant — but scope gating means it never gets the chance.

Noticed on a Rails project where a data migration created a user-facing record; the specialist only ran because it was dispatched manually.

## Suggested fix

Add a separate arm. It should also set `BACKEND`, because unlike a schema migration these files are ordinary app code and deserve the backend reviewers too — and because the current fall-through means they already get `BACKEND=true` today, so matching only `MIGRATIONS` would *reduce* coverage:

```sh
# Data migrations (data_migrate gem). Also BACKEND: unlike a schema
# migration these are arbitrary app code, run unattended in the release
# phase, so they need the backend reviewers as well as the migration one.
db/data/*|*/data_migrations/*) MIGRATIONS=true; BACKEND=true ;;
```

Verified locally against gstack 1.60.1.0: purely additive (5 insertions, no existing line modified), so `db/migrate` behaviour is unchanged, and the previously-misclassified branch now reports `SCOPE_MIGRATIONS=true SCOPE_BACKEND=true`.

Happy to open a PR if useful.

title: engine-locked is classified but never whitelisted: #2194 moved the symptom from "broken-config" to "gbrain not detected" (3 gates, patch + test included)
fix(diff-scope): detect Drizzle migrations, root-level migrations/, and singular migration/
body:
## What

`SCOPE_MIGRATIONS` returned `false` on a PR whose diff contained a migration, so
`/ship` never dispatched the **data-migration specialist** — on a diff that dropped a
column `DEFAULT`. Found while shipping a Drizzle + Postgres app; I force-included the
specialist manually, and it turned out to be the pass that mattered most on that diff.

The pattern list matched `db/migrate/`, `*/migrations/`, `alembic/` and `prisma/migrations/`.
Three gaps:

1. **Drizzle** writes bare `.sql` files plus a `meta/` journal into its `out` dir (default
   `./drizzle`), matching none of them. This is the case that surfaced it.
2. **`*/migrations/*` requires a parent segment**, so a **root-level** `migrations/` dir —
   Knex, Sequelize, golang-migrate, Atlas — fell through.
3. **Flyway** and some Java/Ecto layouts use the singular `migration/`.

Matching is deliberately broad, on the asymmetry that a false positive costs one extra
specialist pass while a false negative silently skips the reviewer on the diff that most
needed one.

## Also: the test file could not run on Windows at all

Every one of `test/diff-scope.test.ts`'s 16 tests failed before this change — not from a
regression, it had simply never worked there. `createRepo` derived the parent directory with:

```js
const dirPath = fullPath.substring(0, fullPath.lastIndexOf('/'));
```

`join()` emits **backslashes** on Windows, so `lastIndexOf('/')` returned `-1`,
`substring(0, -1)` gave `''`, and `mkdirSync('')` threw `ENOENT`. Now uses `dirname()`.

I verified this is pre-existing rather than mine by stashing both files and re-running:
**0 pass / 16 fail** on a clean checkout.

## Verification

`bun test test/diff-scope.test.ts` on Windows:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| pass | 0 | **21** |
| fail | 16 | **0** |

Six new cases cover Drizzle output (bare `.sql`, `meta/` journal, monorepo package),
root-level `migrations/`, singular `migration/`, and a **negative** case asserting the
widened patterns do *not* fire on `drizzle.config.ts` or on prose like
`docs/migration-guide.md` — only on a real path segment.

## Note

Branched from `v1.60.1.0`, which is what my install was pinned at. `bin/gstack-diff-scope`
and `test/diff-scope.test.ts` are both untouched upstream since then, so it should apply
cleanly — happy to rebase if you'd prefer.

title: Fix browse daemon crash-loop diagnostics + a shell-injection bug found along the way
body:
## Summary
- The detached browse daemon's stdout/stderr were wired to `'ignore'` on every platform, so every `console.error('[browse] FATAL: ...')` from a crash (Chromium disconnect, uncaughtException, unhandledRejection) went nowhere — a restart was indistinguishable from any other cause of a dropped session, with nothing on disk recording why.
- `cli.ts`: both the Windows and macOS/Linux spawn paths now redirect stdout/stderr to `<stateDir>/browse-daemon.log` (append mode, accumulates across the daemon's full lifetime and every respawn).
- That immediately surfaced two real, previously invisible bugs, both fixed here:
  1. **`spawn bun ENOENT`** — `bun-polyfill.cjs`'s `Bun.spawn`/`spawnSync` polyfill called Node's `child_process.spawn` with a bare command name (`'bun'`), which Windows can't resolve without PATHEXT lookup.
  2. **`browser?.process is not a function`** — `resolveDisconnectCause()` (the crash classifier itself) threw on some browser/connection-mode shapes, and being an unhandled fire-and-forget rejection, took the whole daemon down a second, harder-to-diagnose way.

## A note on how the fix for #1 evolved
My first attempt used `shell:true` with hand-rolled double-quote escaping to fix the PATHEXT resolution. I verified empirically (not just reasoned about it) that this does **not** neutralize cmd.exe metacharacters (`&|^%<>`), and is reachable via `browser-skill-commands.ts`'s `...opts.skillArgs` passthrough from `$B skill run <name> --arg k=v`. Spawning a resolved `.cmd` path with an arg containing `& echo INJECTED > proof.txt` actually created the file.

Replaced it with [`cross-spawn`](https://github.com/moxystudio/node-cross-spawn) — already resolved in `node_modules` transitively via `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, now added as a direct dependency — the established library for correct Windows PATHEXT resolution + argument escaping together. Re-verified the same injection payload no longer executes, and normal resolution (`bun --version`) still works.

## Test plan
- [x] Killed the live Chromium child under a running daemon — log now shows a single clean `FATAL: Chromium process crashed or was killed`, terminal-agent respawns successfully, daemon auto-recovers to a healthy new PID
- [x] Re-ran the same test after reverting each fix individually to confirm each is load-bearing (not just cosmetically present)
- [x] Confirmed the shell-injection payload (`& echo INJECTED > proof.txt`) no longer executes after the `cross-spawn` fix
- [x] Confirmed normal resolution (`bun --version` via both `spawn` and `spawnSync`) still works, including paths/args containing spaces
- [x] 24/24 pre-existing `browser-manager-unit` tests pass
- [x] `bun build --compile` succeeds for both `cli.ts` and the Node server bundle

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: gstack-version-bump classify ignores .gstack/version-path when reading the base version
body:
`gstack-version-bump classify` resolves the VERSION file two different ways in adjacent lines, and only one of them honours `.gstack/version-path`. In any monorepo using that config (the layout added by #1627), the base version is read from a repo-root `VERSION` that usually does not exist, silently becomes `0.0.0.0`, and every classification downstream of it is wrong.

## The two lines

`bin/gstack-version-bump:136-139`

```js
const versionPath = resolveVersionPath(cwd, argVal(args, "--version-path")); // honours the config
const versionRel  = argVal(args, "--version-path") ?? "VERSION";             // does NOT
const current = readVersionFile(versionPath);
const baseV   = baseVersion(cwd, base!, versionRel);   // git show origin/<base>:VERSION
```

`versionRel` falls back to the literal `"VERSION"` instead of going through `resolveVersionPath`. `baseVersion()` catches the failed `git show` and returns `DEFAULT` (`:42`, `"0.0.0.0"`), so there is no error — just a wrong answer, plus a stray `fatal:` on stderr from the inner git call.

## Reproduction

```bash
D=$(mktemp -d); cd "$D"
git init -q -b main repo && git init -q --bare origin.git && cd repo
git remote add origin "$D/origin.git"
mkdir -p .gstack sub && echo "1.2.3.4" > sub/VERSION && echo '{"version":"1.2.3.4"}' > package.json
printf 'sub/VERSION\n' > .gstack/version-path
git add -A && git commit -qm init && git push -q origin main

gstack-version-bump classify --base main
```

Actual:

```
fatal: path 'VERSION' does not exist in 'origin/main'
{"state":"DRIFT_STALE_PKG","baseVersion":"0.0.0.0","currentVersion":"1.2.3.4",...}
```

Expected: `baseVersion` `1.2.3.4`, state `FRESH`. Passing `--version-path sub/VERSION` explicitly gives the correct `baseVersion`, which confirms the config path is the only thing being dropped.

## Why it matters in /ship

Step 12 calls `classify --base <base>` with no `--version-path`, so this fires on every ship in a config-using repo. `baseVersion` is stuck at `0.0.0.0` while `currentVersion` is the real subproject version, so `current === base` is never true and **classify can never return `FRESH`** — Step 12's normal path. It lands on `ALREADY_BUMPED` (skip the bump) or `DRIFT_STALE_PKG` (run `repair`) instead, neither of which is what happened.

## Secondary: the two binaries disagree on a multi-line config

`gstack-next-version:134` takes the first line:

```js
const firstLine = readFileSync(configFile, "utf8").split("\n")[0]?.trim() ?? "";
```

and `test/gstack-next-version.test.ts:184` pins that as intended — extra lines are discarded.

`gstack-version-bump:60` trims the whole file:

```js
const p = readFileSync(pin, "utf-8").trim();
```

So a config containing two paths (the obvious thing to try in a repo with two versioned subprojects) resolves to `sub-a/VERSION` in one binary and to the literal string `"sub-a/VERSION\nsub-b/VERSION"` in the other. The latter is joined into a path, the read fails, `readVersionFile` swallows it, and `currentVersion` also becomes `0.0.0.0`. Observed state flips to `DRIFT_UNEXPECTED`, which Step 12 treats as a hard stop with the message "a manual edit bypassed /ship" — an accusation about an edit nobody made.

`test/gstack-version-bump.test.ts` has no multi-line case; `gstack-next-version.test.ts` does.

## Suggested fix

Both are one-liners:

1. `versionRel` should go through the same resolution as `versionPath` — the config-relative path, not `"VERSION"`.
2. `gstack-version-bump`'s `resolveVersionPath` should use `.split("\n")[0].trim()` to match `gstack-next-version`, so a multi-line config degrades identically in both rather than into a broken path.

Happy to send a PR with a regression test mirroring `gstack-next-version.test.ts:184` if that is useful.

Found while shipping a subproject in a monorepo that pins `.gstack/version-path` (config added in #1627).

title: question-preference-hook returns permissionDecision:"defer" — hangs every AskUserQuestion on non-interactive hosts
body:
# `question-preference-hook` returns `permissionDecision: "defer"` — this permanently hangs every AskUserQuestion call on non-interactive hosts (Claude Desktop)

## TL;DR

`hosts/claude/hooks/question-preference-hook.ts:98` returns `permissionDecision: 'defer'` as its **default** path. In Claude Code, `defer` does not mean "don't interfere" — it means **"suspend this tool call, end the turn, resume later."** On non-interactive hosts (Claude Desktop / SDK-driven sessions) this makes **every** AskUserQuestion call hang forever with no `tool_result`. The user sees the question card render, then `Stopped` / `Tool execution was interrupted.`

On the CLI this is invisible: `defer` is ignored in interactive mode. That's why it hasn't been caught.

Measured on my machine: **16/16 AUQ calls hung** after the hook was installed (2026-07-28). **35/35 succeeded** before it. Zero exceptions either side.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| gstack | `1.60.1.0` @ `a3259400` (current `origin/main`) |
| Claude Code | `2.1.221` (Desktop), `2.1.212` (CLI binary inspected) |
| Host | Claude Desktop — transcripts show `entrypoint: "claude-desktop"` |
| OS | macOS (darwin 25.4.0), arm64 |
| Install | global-git at `~/.claude/skills/gstack` |

## Root cause

`defer` **is** a valid `permissionDecision` value, but it is gated. From the Claude Code bundle (`strings` over the 2.1.212 binary):

```js
case "defer": {
  if (!n.options.isNonInteractiveSession) {
    C(`Hook ${ae.hookName} returned permissionDecision=defer in interactive mode; ignoring (defer is print-mode only)`, {level:"warn"});
    break                                    // ← CLI interactive: ignored, tool runs normally
  }
  let se = Array.isArray(i.message.content) ? br(i.message.content, (oe)=>oe.type==="tool_use") : 1;
  if (se > 1) {
    C(`Hook ${ae.hookName} returned permissionDecision=defer but ${se} tool calls are in this batch; ignoring (defer is solo-only — siblings would be orphaned on resume)`, {level:"warn"});
    break
  }
  ...                                        // ← non-interactive + solo: defer takes effect
```

Two gates: **print-mode only** and **solo-only**. Claude Desktop's local agent mode is a non-interactive session, and an AUQ call is typically the sole `tool_use` in its message — so both gates pass and `defer` actually fires.

The hook's own docstring shows the intent was the opposite:

```
 *        never-ask + one-way → defer (safety override; one-way always asks).
 *        always-ask, or no preference → defer.
```

and `defer()` is the terminal path of `main()` — plus the `main().catch()` handler — so it fires on essentially every call:

```ts
// question-preference-hook.ts
async function main() {
  const raw = await readStdin();
  if (!raw.trim()) { defer(); return; }             // :349
  try { stdin = JSON.parse(raw); }
  catch { logHookError(...); defer(); return; }     // :357
  if (toolName !== 'AskUserQuestion' && ...) { defer(); return; }   // :366
  if (questions.length === 0) { defer(); return; }  // :372
  ...
  defer(memoryContext);                             // :474  ← default exit
}
main().catch((e) => { logHookError(...); defer(); });  // :479
```

Only the `deny` path avoids it — and `deny` works correctly, which is consistent with the CHANGELOG note that only that path was ever validated:

> ...enforcement uses `permissionDecision: "deny"` + reason instead of `"allow"` + `updatedInput` **until the AUQ input shape is verified against real Claude Code** (T6 conservative path)

## Reproduction

```bash
cat > /tmp/auq.json <<'EOF'
{"session_id":"probe","hook_event_name":"PreToolUse","tool_name":"AskUserQuestion",
 "tool_use_id":"toolu_probe","cwd":"/tmp",
 "tool_input":{"questions":[{"question":"probe","header":"probe","multiSelect":false,
 "options":[{"label":"A (recommended)","description":"a"},{"label":"B","description":"b"}]}]}}
EOF

~/.claude/skills/gstack/hosts/claude/hooks/question-preference-hook < /tmp/auq.json
```

Actual:

```json
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"defer"}}
```

With the hook installed, every AUQ call on Claude Desktop then produces this transcript sequence and **never** a `tool_result`:

```
assistant  tool_use   AskUserQuestion                       toolu_01QJuz…
attachment hook_success        PreToolUse:AskUserQuestion   exitCode 0, stdout = the defer JSON above
attachment hook_deferred_tool  toolName: AskUserQuestion    ← suspended here, forever
```

The suspended call is never resumed — the session continues (thousands of records later) with the question silently dropped.

## Impact

Beyond the hang itself, the failure mode is *silent and misattributed*, which is what makes it costly:

- The agent gets **no** `tool_result`, so it never learns the call failed. It keeps using AUQ — I logged 3 hangs in a single session.
- The agent misdiagnoses it. Mine repeatedly told the user "the tool returned an internal error" and "you probably didn't see the question" — both wrong. The card *does* render; the user sees the question and simply cannot answer it.
- The user's only recovery is to type "continue" (observed waits: 1.5 min to 40 min). At that point the agent commonly treats "continue" as authorization and **decides on the user's behalf using its own recommended options**. In my logs that happened 5 times, and code based on those unilateral decisions has already been merged.
- 4 more questions were dropped permanently — the session ended before the user typed anything.

The irony worth flagging: these hooks exist to stop the agent from deciding unilaterally and to route decisions through recorded preferences. The `defer` bug produces exactly the outcome they were built to prevent. The `setup` log even calls AUQ "the flaky AskUserQuestion tool" while installing the thing that breaks it.

## Suggested fix

`passthrough` is not a valid hook output value (the schema accepts `allow | deny | ask | defer`). The correct way to express "no opinion" is to **omit** `permissionDecision` — it's optional.

```diff
 function defer(additionalContext?: string): void {
-  const out: Record<string, unknown> = {
-    hookEventName: 'PreToolUse',
-    permissionDecision: 'defer',
-  };
-  if (additionalContext) out.additionalContext = additionalContext;
-  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ hookSpecificOutput: out }));
+  // NOTE: Claude Code's permissionDecision:'defer' means "suspend this tool call
+  // until resume", NOT "don't interfere". It is gated to non-interactive sessions,
+  // so on the CLI it is ignored (warn) while on Claude Desktop it hangs AUQ forever.
+  // Omitting permissionDecision (it is optional) is the real passthrough.
+  if (!additionalContext) process.exit(0);
+  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({
+    hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', additionalContext },
+  }));
   process.exit(0);
 }
```

Renaming the function (`passThrough()`?) would help keep the two meanings from being conflated again.

## Second, smaller bug found while investigating

```console
$ ~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-settings-hook list-sources
(no gstack-tagged hooks)
```

My three AUQ hooks are registered in `~/.claude/settings.json` but carry **no `_gstack_source` tag** (installed 2026-07-28). `setup`'s idempotence check is:

```bash
if printf '%s' "$_HOOK_SOURCES" | grep -q "plan-tune-cathedral" \
   && printf '%s' "$_HOOK_SOURCES" | grep -q "auq-error-fallback"; then
  ALREADY_INSTALLED=1
fi
```

With untagged entries this never matches, so `ALREADY_INSTALLED` stays 0 and `setup` will re-install on every run — risking duplicate hook entries. It also means the entries can't be removed with `gstack-settings-hook`, only by hand-editing `settings.json`. A migration that back-fills the source tag on untagged gstack hook entries would close this.

## Workaround for other Desktop users

Both steps are needed — removing the hook alone gets undone by the next `./setup`:

```bash
~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-config set plan_tune_hooks no
# then hand-remove the PreToolUse entry matching
# (AskUserQuestion|mcp__.*__AskUserQuestion) from ~/.claude/settings.json
```

The two PostToolUse hooks (logging, error fallback) are harmless — they don't gate execution.

Note that patching the hook source directly is **not** upgrade-safe: `/gstack-upgrade` runs `git stash` + `git reset --hard origin/main`, which silently restores the `defer` version and re-breaks AUQ with no warning.

title: fix(slug): canonicalize slash branches to dash form so review rows stop splitting (#1127)
body:
Fixes the **writer** half of #1127. Complements #1851, which fixes the **read**
half (Context Recovery lookup across 44 `SKILL.md` files). The two are
independent and land cleanly in either order — #1851 canonicalizes the reads,
this canonicalizes the writes. I have not touched the read path.

## The problem

Three different sanitizations of the same branch name coexist in gstack:

| # | Transform | `feat/foo` becomes | Where |
|---|-----------|--------------------|-------|
| 1 | `tr -cd 'a-zA-Z0-9._-'` — **deletes** the slash | `featfoo` | `bin/gstack-slug:52` → `gstack-review-log`, `gstack-review-read` |
| 2 | `tr '/' '-'` — **replaces** the slash | `feat-foo` | `ship/sections/plan-completion.md:19` (Step 8) |
| 3 | none — **raw** | `feat/foo` | `ship/SKILL.md:1356` (Step 20) |

So one branch's review rows land in up to three places, and `/retro` sees a
fraction of its own history.

### Live evidence, one project dir

**20 branches are split across two files each**, and the pattern is perfectly
consistent: the dash-form file holds *only* the `ship` row, the strip-form file
holds *only* the other skills' rows. Not one of the 20 is mixed.

Clearest single case, branch `feat/cdk-app-scaffold-R-1053`:

- `feat-cdk-app-scaffold-R-1053-reviews.jsonl` (form 2) — the `/ship` row
- `featcdk-app-scaffold-R-1053-reviews.jsonl` (form 1) — the `/review` row,
  written three hours earlier the same day

`feat/partners-list-page-R-620` is the same shape with more on the strip side:
`/ship` in the dash file, `/review` and `/plan-eng-review` in the strip file.
`/retro` reading either filename sees half the branch's history.

### Transform 3 has two failure modes, not one

This is the part worth stating plainly, because the two reports on #1127 look
like different bugs and are not:

- **No `feat/` directory exists** → the redirect dies with
  `no such file or directory` and the row is lost silently. Reported upstream on
  1.60.1.0 for `feat/4-posting-service`.
- **A `feat/` directory already exists** → the write *succeeds into it*, and the
  row is invisible to every flat glob. That is the machine this was found on:
  5 rows sit in `projects/<slug>/feat/`.

"Rows are lost" and "rows are fragmented" are the same bug seen from two
machines.

## The fix

**1. `bin/gstack-slug`** — replace the slash instead of deleting it, so
transform 1 agrees with transform 2:

```diff
-BRANCH=$(printf '%s' "${RAW_BRANCH:-}" | tr -cd 'a-zA-Z0-9._-')
+BRANCH=$(printf '%s' "${RAW_BRANCH:-}" | tr '/' '-' | tr -cd 'a-zA-Z0-9._-')
```

The file's header promises a `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]` invariant. Still holds — the
`tr -cd` stays as the final filter. Verified across shapes:

```
feat/foo-R-1   -> feat-foo-R-1      main          -> main
fix/logout     -> fix-logout        feature/a/b/c -> feature-a-b-c
chore/x_y.z    -> chore-x_y.z
```

**2. ship Step 20** — the old block interpolated `$BRANCH` into a redirect path
*and* carried a literal `BRANCH` token in the JSON, with a "substitute BRANCH =
current branch name" instruction below it. A model doing that substitution can
hit the path too, which is what produces the `feat/` subdirectory.

It now routes through `bin/gstack-review-log`, which takes **no path argument**,
so there is nothing left to corrupt. The helper already resolves slug and branch,
creates the directory, validates the JSON, and enqueues for gbrain sync — the
step gets shorter, not longer. The `BRANCH` placeholder is gone entirely,
replaced by a real shell expansion.

Edited `ship/SKILL.md.tmpl` and regenerated via `bun run gen:skill-docs`; the
three ship golden fixtures are regenerated in the same commit.

## Migration: deliberately deferred

Change 1 renames `featfoo-reviews.jsonl` to `feat-foo-reviews.jsonl`, so existing
files are orphaned rather than rewritten. Not adding a migration, for a measured
reason: on the machine this was found, 303 of 308 rows (98.4%) are already
top-level and reachable by a flat glob. The 5 stranded rows are all `ship` rows
carrying a `coverage_pct` but no plan-item counts (four `0`, one `-1`). A
one-time merge folding `featfoo-*` and `feat/*` into the canonical
`feat-foo-*`, sorted by timestamp, is easy to add as a follow-up if a maintainer
wants it — say the word and I will.

@kkru-labs suggested a shared canonical normalizer that every caller imports.
Aligning `gstack-slug` is the minimal version of that idea (one authority instead
of three); extracting a real shared helper is a clean follow-up on top.

## Verification

- `bun run test` — green, except two failures **proven pre-existing** by running
  the same two files against `origin/main` in a clean worktree:
  `test/skill-e2e-ios-swift-build.test.ts` (Swift toolchain, local) and
  `test/helpers/observability.test.ts` (counts `/* non-fatal */` comments in
  `session-runner.ts`). Neither touches anything in this diff.
- `test/gstack-slug-sanitize.test.ts` passes unchanged — it asserts the charset
  invariant on `SLUG` and never pinned BRANCH slash-deletion.
- `test/gen-skill-docs.test.ts` passes — the ship union still contains
  `reviews.jsonl` via the Context Recovery block.
- The three ship golden-file regressions in `test/host-config.test.ts` are green
  against the regenerated fixtures.
- `slop-scan: no new findings in 6 changed files.`
- End-to-end from a slash-named branch in a scratch repo: all five branch shapes
  above normalize as expected, one canonical flat file written, zero nested
  directories created.

## Conflict risk

Four open PRs also touch `ship/SKILL.md.tmpl`: #2343, #2334, #2303, #2301. None
of them touch Step 20, so this is textual-conflict risk on the generated
`SKILL.md` and goldens, not a scope overlap. Happy to rebase behind whichever
lands first.

No `VERSION` bump or `CHANGELOG` entry here — following #1851, the sibling PR on
the same issue, and keeping this out of the way of the four in-flight ship
template PRs. Happy to add both if that is the house preference.

title: Decision cards never appear in the Claude desktop app (PreToolUse hook sends permissionDecision: 'defer')
body:
## Summary

If you use gstack inside the **Claude desktop app**, AskUserQuestion decision cards never appear. The question is silently swallowed and the agent gets back `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`. The user just sees the agent go quiet, or ask a question in prose that they never got buttons for.

It works fine in the terminal CLI, which is probably why this hasn't surfaced before.

**Cause:** `hosts/claude/hooks/question-preference-hook.ts` emits `permissionDecision: 'defer'` on its no-enforcement path. In Claude Code, `defer` does not mean "no opinion" — it means *park this tool call so a later resume can pick it up*.

## Root cause detail

From the Claude Code 2.1.221 binary, the `defer` branch of the PreToolUse handler:

```js
case "defer": {
  if (!n.options.isNonInteractiveSession) {
    C(`Hook ${ce.hookName} returned permissionDecision=defer in interactive mode; ignoring (defer is print-mode only)`, {level:"warn"});
    break;                                   // ignored → card renders normally
  }
  ...
  return T.push({ message: al({ type: "hook_deferred_tool", ... }) })   // tool parked, never runs
}
```

So `defer` is only honored when the session is flagged `isNonInteractiveSession` — and the Claude desktop app is flagged non-interactive even with a human sitting in front of it. The AskUserQuestion call gets parked, never executes, and never returns a result.

The valid enum is `allow | deny | ask | defer`, so this passes schema validation and fails silently.

## Evidence

Bisected against a single session with all three AUQ hooks registered:

| Hooks live | Result |
|---|---|
| none | card renders ✅ |
| `question-preference-hook` only (emits `defer`) | `[Tool result missing due to internal error]` ❌ |
| all three, with fix below | card renders ✅ |

Across that machine's full transcript history: **3,700+ tool calls of every other kind resolved 100%. AskUserQuestion: 8 calls, 0 resolved.**

Reproduced on gstack `1.60.1.0` at `origin/main` (`a325940`), Claude Code 2.1.221, macOS.

## Why omitting is the correct fix (not switching to another value)

The hook's own docstring states the intent:

> `never-ask + one-way → defer (safety override; one-way always asks)`

If `defer` parked the tool, a one-way door would *never* reach the human — the exact inverse of the documented safety override. So the intent here is "no enforcement, proceed normally, let the user be asked". Claude Code encodes that by **omitting** `permissionDecision`; it is `.optional()` in the PreToolUse `hookSpecificOutput` schema:

```js
E.object({
  hookEventName: E.literal("PreToolUse"),
  permissionDecision: DM_().optional(),
  permissionDecisionReason: E.string().optional(),
  updatedInput: E.record(E.string(), E.unknown()).optional(),
  additionalContext: E.string().optional()
})
```

## Fix

In `defer()`, drop the `permissionDecision` key and keep everything else:

```ts
function defer(additionalContext?: string): void {
  const out: Record<string, unknown> = {
    hookEventName: 'PreToolUse',
  };
  if (additionalContext) out.additionalContext = additionalContext;
  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ hookSpecificOutput: out }));
  process.exit(0);
}
```

This preserves everything that path was doing:

- `additionalContext` still flows, so plan-tune memory-nugget injection is unaffected
- the `deny` paths (never-ask auto-decide, and the Conductor prose redirect) are untouched — `deny` is a valid, honored value
- the PostToolUse logging hooks are unaffected

Only `allow` / `deny` / `ask` are safe to emit from a PreToolUse hook that expects the tool to actually run.

## Tests

14 assertions across `test/question-preference-hook.test.ts`, `test/memory-cache-injection.test.ts`, and `test/skill-e2e-plan-tune-cathedral.test.ts` assert `permissionDecision === 'defer'` and need updating to `toBeUndefined()`. After that, 93/93 pass across the five hook suites.

Happy to open a PR with the fix, the updated assertions, and a regression guard asserting the hook never emits `'defer'` if that's useful.

title: fix(make-pdf): hide empty TOC page numbers and dot leaders in print
body:
## Problem

`make-pdf generate --toc` produces a table of contents where dot leaders run from each entry title into blank space. It reads as a broken document.

Cause: `.toc-page` is filled by a CSS `target-counter`, which only resolves under Paged.js. Paged.js is not vendored in gstack, and Chrome has no native `target-counter`, so the spans stay permanently empty while the leader dots still render. `browse/src/meta-commands.ts:545` already documents the constraint: *"make-pdf v1 ships without Paged.js; TOC renders without page numbers."*

This is not fixable in CSS alone as long as the counter has nothing to resolve against.

## Fix

Hide `.toc-dots` and `.toc-page` in print until page numbers actually exist. `screenCss()` already does exactly this for HTML output, so this brings print in line with the path that was already correct. A comment marks the two rules to restore the day Paged.js lands.

Also: `buildTocBlock` mapped every heading at H2 or deeper to `level-2`, so H3 sub-sections sat at the same indent as numbered sections and read as top-level peers. H3 now gets its own `level-3` class.

## Result

Clean, clickable, correctly nested TOC. No trailing dots. Cover page, running headers, `N of M` footers unaffected.

## Testing

- `bun test` in `make-pdf/`: **189 pass, 0 fail**, 393 `expect()` calls across 11 files.
- Verified visually on a 9-page letter-format document with a cover page: rasterized the output and confirmed zero leader-dot glyphs in the TOC region, correct H2/H3 nesting, and intact headers and footers.

## Note

If Paged.js is ever vendored, revert the single `display: none` rule and the original two declarations are restored verbatim from the comment. The `level-3` change is independent and should stay either way.

title: fix(design): create OpenAI key file owner-only to close write-then-chmod race
body:
## What

`saveApiKey()` in `design/src/auth.ts` persists the OpenAI API key to `~/.gstack/openai.json` by writing at the process default umask and only tightening permissions afterwards:

```ts
fs.writeFileSync(configPath(), JSON.stringify({ api_key: key }, null, 2));
fs.chmodSync(configPath(), 0o600);
```

On a typical umask (022) the file is created `0644` (group/world-readable). Between the `writeFileSync` and the `chmodSync` there is a window where the file containing the OpenAI API key is readable by any other local user. This is CWE-377 (insecure file creation) / CWE-367 (TOCTOU) — low severity, only exploitable by a co-located local user on a shared/multi-user host, but it's a real key-disclosure window and a cheap thing to close.

## Fix

Create the file owner-only up front by passing `{ mode: 0o600 }` to `writeFileSync`, so it is never briefly world-readable. The trailing `chmodSync` is kept as a backstop that still tightens a pre-existing loose file.

```ts
fs.writeFileSync(configPath(), JSON.stringify({ api_key: key }, null, 2), { mode: 0o600 });
fs.chmodSync(configPath(), 0o600);
```

This matches the convention already used for session files in `design/src/session.ts` (`{ mode: 0o600 }` on create, landed in #859). #859 hardened the session files but the actual API key file kept the write-then-chmod pattern — this brings it in line.

## Test

Adds a `saveApiKey` regression test that writes the key under a deliberately permissive umask (`0o000`) and asserts the resulting file is exactly `0600` with no group/other bits.

```
$ bun test design/test/auth.test.ts
 7 pass
 0 fail
```

## Scope

Two files, `design/src/auth.ts` (+3/-1) and `design/test/auth.test.ts` (+21). No behavior change beyond the file-creation mode.

title: investigate hooks still use ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} — freeze scope lock silently never runs (#1871 follow-up)
body:
## Summary

`#1871` (fixed in v1.57.6.0) anchored the `guard`, `freeze`, and `careful` frontmatter hooks to `$HOME/.claude/skills/gstack/...` because Claude Code 2.1.162+ no longer populates `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`.

**`investigate` was not included in that fix and still uses `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`.** As of v1.60.1.0 its freeze scope lock never runs — silently.

## Affected (v1.60.1.0)

`investigate/SKILL.md.tmpl` (and the generated `investigate/SKILL.md`):

- **L33 / L38** — the Edit and Write `PreToolUse` hooks
- **L121-123** — the Scope Lock availability check in the body

```yaml
command: 'bash -c ''S="${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/../freeze/bin/check-freeze.sh"; [ -x "$S" ] || S="${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/../gstack-freeze/bin/check-freeze.sh"; [ -x "$S" ] && bash "$S" || exit 0'''
```

Compare with the three skills fixed by #1871:

```yaml
# guard / freeze / careful
command: "bash $HOME/.claude/skills/gstack/freeze/bin/check-freeze.sh"
```

## Why it fails silently

With the variable unset, both candidates resolve to non-existent absolute paths and the trailing `|| exit 0` swallows it:

```
$ env -u CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR bash -c 'S="${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/../freeze/bin/check-freeze.sh"; echo "$S"'
/../freeze/bin/check-freeze.sh          # -x fails
/../gstack-freeze/bin/check-freeze.sh   # -x fails
-> exit 0                               # hook reports success, check never ran
```

The body block has a visible symptom: the Scope Lock section always prints `FREEZE_UNAVAILABLE`, so `/investigate` skips scope locking entirely.

## Second, independent breakage

Even with `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` populated, the first candidate would still miss. Linked skill directories ship `SKILL.md` only:

```
$ ls ~/.claude/skills/freeze
SKILL.md

$ ls ~/.claude/skills/gstack/freeze
SKILL.md  SKILL.md.tmpl  bin/
```

`bin/` exists only in the checkout, so `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/../freeze/bin/` can never resolve in a bundled install. The checkout-anchored path from #1871 is the only form that works.

## How the regression test locked it in

`test/investigate-freeze-path.test.ts` was added in v1.58.4.0 — two weeks *after* #1871 — and asserts the dead form:

```ts
expect(content).toContain('${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/../freeze/bin/check-freeze.sh');
```

It only checks that a string is present, never that the hook resolves to an executable, so it stayed green while the hook was dead.

## Suggested fix

Match the three sibling skills, and have the test assert behaviour (that the anchored path is executable) rather than the literal variable:

```yaml
command: "bash $HOME/.claude/skills/gstack/freeze/bin/check-freeze.sh"
```

```bash
_FREEZE_SCRIPT="$HOME/.claude/skills/gstack/freeze/bin/check-freeze.sh"
[ -x "$_FREEZE_SCRIPT" ] && echo "FREEZE_AVAILABLE" || echo "FREEZE_UNAVAILABLE"
```

Applied locally against v1.60.1.0: `bun test test/investigate-freeze-path.test.ts` → 7 pass / 0 fail, the hook command runs and returns `{}` / exit 0, and the Scope Lock block reports `FREEZE_AVAILABLE`. Happy to open a PR if useful.

## Environment

- gstack v1.60.1.0
- Claude Code 2.1.224
- Bundled global install at `~/.claude/skills/gstack`
- Linux (WSL2)

title: spawnSync(shell: true) on Windows breaks every gbrain call when a path contains a space
body:
Every `gbrain` invocation fails on Windows when any path contains a space, because `spawnSync` is called with `shell: true` and an args array. Node joins that array into a single unquoted command string for `cmd.exe`, so the first space ends the argument.

This affects any Windows user whose home directory has a space in it — `C:\Users\First Last` — which is the default for a great many Windows installs.

## Symptom

`/sync-gbrain` fails with an error that gives no hint of the real cause:

```
gstack-gbrain-sync (full):
  ERR   code   source registration failed: gbrain sources add gstack-code-<id> failed:
        Unknown flag: MUSIC/Downloads/pfn-gei-engine
```

The path is `C:/Users/WATER MUSIC/Downloads/pfn-gei-engine`. It split at the space in `WATER MUSIC`, and `gbrain` then parsed the remainder as a flag.

## Root cause

`lib/gbrain-sources.ts` (~line 173):

```ts
const addArgs = ["sources", "add", id, "--path", path];
if (federated) addArgs.push("--federated");
const add = spawnSync("gbrain", addArgs, {
  encoding: "utf-8",
  timeout: 30_000,
  env,
  shell: NEEDS_SHELL_ON_WINDOWS, // #1731: gbrain is a .cmd shim on Windows
});
```

`lib/gbrain-exec.ts:137`:

```ts
export const NEEDS_SHELL_ON_WINDOWS = process.platform === "win32";
```

Passing args as an array is normally safe, but `shell: true` changes the contract: Node concatenates `args` onto the command with spaces and hands the result to `cmd.exe` **without quoting any element**. The array no longer delimits anything.

The `shell: true` was introduced to fix #1731 (gbrain is a `.cmd` shim on Windows and can't be spawned directly). That fix is correct in intent; the quoting consequence just wasn't accounted for.

## Minimal reproduction

Independent of gstack and gbrain — Node v22.16.0, Windows 11:

```js
import { spawnSync } from 'child_process';
const args = ['show.mjs', '--path', 'C:/Users/WATER MUSIC/repo'];
for (const shell of [false, true]) {
  const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, args, { encoding: 'utf8', shell });
  console.log(`shell:${shell} ->`, (r.stdout || r.stderr).trim());
}
```

```
shell:false -> ["--path","C:/Users/WATER MUSIC/repo"]          // intact
shell:true  -> 'C:\Program' is not recognized as an internal or external command
```

Note the `shell: true` case fails on the **executable** path too (`C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe`), not only the argument — so this is not specific to the `--path` value.

## Blast radius

`shell: NEEDS_SHELL_ON_WINDOWS` appears 13 times across 5 files:

```
lib/gbrain-exec.ts
lib/gbrain-guards.ts
lib/gbrain-local-status.ts
lib/gbrain-sources.ts
bin/gstack-gbrain-sync.ts
```

Every one has the same exposure. `sources add` is simply the first call that carries a user path, so it's where it surfaces.

## Robustness note (not a reported vulnerability)

Being precise about scope: I have **not** demonstrated an exploit, and in normal use the path comes from the user's own filesystem, so this is defense-in-depth rather than a remote vector.

That said, `shell: true` means these paths are parsed by `cmd.exe`. Directory names containing `&`, `|`, `^`, or `>` are legal on Windows, so a checkout at

```
C:\Users\me\foo & whoami\repo
```

would run `whoami` as a side effect of a sync. Since the second fix below removes the shell entirely, it resolves both the spaces bug and this surface at once — which may be worth weighing when choosing between the two.

## Suggested fix

Two options.

**Quote at the call site** — smallest change, keeps the #1731 fix intact:

```ts
const quoteForCmd = (s: string) =>
  process.platform === "win32" && /[\s&|<>^"]/.test(s)
    ? `"${s.replace(/"/g, '""')}"`
    : s;

const add = spawnSync("gbrain", addArgs.map(quoteForCmd), { /* ... */ shell: NEEDS_SHELL_ON_WINDOWS });
```

Best applied inside a shared helper in `lib/gbrain-exec.ts` so all 13 sites get it at once, rather than patching each.

**Or drop `shell: true`** and invoke the interpreter explicitly, which keeps Node's own quoting:

```ts
const isWin = process.platform === "win32";
spawnSync(
  isWin ? (process.env.ComSpec ?? "cmd.exe") : "gbrain",
  isWin ? ["/d", "/s", "/c", "gbrain", ...addArgs] : addArgs,
  { shell: false, /* ... */ },
);
```

The second is more robust — it removes the shell-metacharacter surface rather than escaping around it — but it's a wider change.

## Workaround for affected users

Register the source manually with a quoted path, then sync:

```bash
gbrain sources add <source-id> --path "C:/Users/First Last/path/to/repo" --federated
gbrain sync --strategy code --source <source-id>
```

## Environment

- Windows 11 Home 26200
- Node v22.16.0, bun 1.3.14
- gstack 1.60.1.0
- gbrain 0.42.73.2
- Home directory contains a space

Fixes #2035, fixes #2006, fixes #2039, fixes #2024, fixes #2032, fixes #2067, fixes #2052, fixes #2051, fixes #1985. Also fixes #2473 (three E2E budget/starvation fixes landed here after CI diagnosis; all verified locally and green on CI run 3).

Every AskUserQuestion died with "Tool result missing due to internal error" on current Claude Code builds. `permissionDecision:'defer'` is a real PreToolUse value, but since CC v2.1.89 it means "pause this tool call for external resumption" (a headless feature), never "abstain" — interactive sessions have nothing to resume the paused call. The hook's pass-through is now exit 0 with exactly-empty stdout (or additionalContext-only output, which keeps plan-tune memory nuggets working). title: Fix: decision cards never appear in the Claude desktop app (AskUserQuestion parked by permissionDecision 'defer')
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2466 — AskUserQuestion decision cards never appear when gstack runs in the **Claude desktop app**. The question is silently swallowed, the user sees nothing, and the agent gets back `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`.

`hosts/claude/hooks/question-preference-hook.ts` emitted `permissionDecision: 'defer'` on its no-enforcement path. In Claude Code, `defer` does **not** mean "no opinion" — it means *park this tool call so a later resume can pick it up*.

From the Claude Code 2.1.221 binary:

```js
case "defer": {
  if (!n.options.isNonInteractiveSession) {
    C(`Hook ${ce.hookName} returned permissionDecision=defer in interactive mode; ignoring (defer is print-mode only)`, {level:"warn"});
    break;                                   // ignored → card renders normally
  }
  ...
  return T.push({ message: al({ type: "hook_deferred_tool", ... }) })   // parked, never runs
}
```

`defer` is honored only when the session is flagged `isNonInteractiveSession` — and the Claude desktop app is flagged non-interactive even with a human present. So the AskUserQuestion call is parked, never executes, and never returns.

**This is why it went unreported:** in the terminal CLI `defer` is ignored and cards work fine, which is how most people run gstack. It reproduces only in the desktop app.

## The fix

Omit `permissionDecision` on the no-enforcement path. It is `.optional()` in the PreToolUse `hookSpecificOutput` schema:

```js
E.object({
  hookEventName: E.literal("PreToolUse"),
  permissionDecision: DM_().optional(),
  permissionDecisionReason: E.string().optional(),
  updatedInput: E.record(E.string(), E.unknown()).optional(),
  additionalContext: E.string().optional()
})
```

Omitting it is also what this path already *means*. The hook's own docstring states:

> `never-ask + one-way → defer (safety override; one-way always asks)`

If `defer` parked the tool, a one-way door would never reach the human — the exact inverse of the documented safety override. So the intent is "no enforcement, proceed normally, let the user be asked."

Only `allow` / `deny` / `ask` are safe to emit when the tool is expected to actually run.

## What is preserved

- `additionalContext` still flows → plan-tune memory-nugget injection unaffected
- `deny` paths untouched → never-ask auto-decide and the Conductor prose redirect both still work (`deny` is a valid, honored value)
- PostToolUse logging hooks unaffected

## Verification

Bisected on a real desktop-app session with all three AUQ hooks registered:

| Hooks live | Result |
|---|---|
| none | card renders ✅ |
| `question-preference-hook` only (emits `defer`) | `[Tool result missing due to internal error]` ❌ |
| all three, with this patch | card renders ✅ |

Across that machine's full transcript history before the fix: **3,700+ tool calls of every other kind resolved 100%; AskUserQuestion went 0-for-8.** After the fix, decision cards render and return normally, including multi-question and `multiSelect` cards.

## Tests

14 assertions across three suites encoded the old contract and are updated to `toBeUndefined()`. Added a regression guard (`never emits permissionDecision:defer`) covering the no-preference, no-marker, empty-stdin, and non-AUQ paths, plus the one-way-door safety override.

**93/93 passing** across the five hook suites against current `main` (v1.60.2.0):

```
bun test test/question-preference-hook.test.ts test/memory-cache-injection.test.ts \
         test/auq-error-fallback-hook.test.ts test/question-log-hook.test.ts \
         test/hook-scripts.test.ts
# 93 pass, 0 fail
```
