title: gstack-review-log stamps wtree unconditionally: a non-converged /ship review loop grades unreviewed code CURRENT in the land-and-deploy readiness gate
body:
## Summary

`bin/gstack-review-log` stamps the gating `wtree` fingerprint at log time with no evidence that a review pass ever read that tree. When `/ship`'s review-army fix-and-rerun loop does not converge — including when the agent simply skips it — the record still certifies the final tree. `/land-and-deploy`'s readiness gate then applies its content-first rule and grades the review **CURRENT**, which a reader takes to mean "this code was reviewed."

`bin/gstack-evidence` already solved this for test runs with a before/after TOCTOU guard. Review flows never got the equivalent.

gstack 1.79.0.0.

## The design is correct when the loop is followed

`ship/sections/review-army.md` step 7 mandates the loop:

> If ANY fixes were applied: commit fixed files by name [...] then **stay in this invocation and loop**: re-run the test suite (Step 5) on the fixed code, then re-run this review (Step 9 items 2-6) against the updated diff. Repeat until one full pass applies ZERO fixes

Step 9 logs only after that, with `"commit":"'"$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"'"`. In the converged case the final pass applies zero fixes, so HEAD is unchanged between the last review and the log and the binding window is **zero**, not merely small. Nothing to fix there.

## The gap

The stamp is unconditional and unfalsifiable downstream. `bin/gstack-review-log:14-18` documents the window honestly:

```
# Known limitation: binding happens at LOG time, not review-START time — edits
# made between finishing a review and logging it (including fixes the review
# itself applied) are certified by the stamped fingerprint. gstack-evidence
# closes this window for test runs (before/after capture); review flows log
# immediately after reviewing, which keeps the window small but nonzero.
```

"Keeps the window small" is a claim about agent compliance, not an invariant. Nothing in the emitted record says whether the loop converged, how many cycles ran, or whether any pass read the stamped tree. A non-converged run and a converged one produce byte-identical bindings.

The readiness gate in `land-and-deploy/sections/readiness-gate.md` then consumes it:

> If the entry has a `wtree` field AND it equals the `---WTREE---` section of the output → **CURRENT**, full stop. Identical working-tree content, regardless of commit count, rebase, amend, or whether it was committed yet (wtree equality alone proves identical content) — skip steps 3-4 for this entry.

That wording is careful and literally true. Identical content is not a review, though, and the grade name collapses the distinction. The gate skips its commit-distance heuristic precisely when the stamp is least trustworthy.

## Observed

Real run, private repo, ~6,200-line branch. The agent ran the eight-reader review, applied fixes across three commits (36 files, 1,065 lines), and skipped the mandated re-run loop. Ledger rows, abridged:

```
{"skill":"review","timestamp":"...T09:28:28Z","commit":"a35d094","wtree":"3a1891f8...","dirty":true}
{"skill":"review","timestamp":"...T20:44:14Z","issues_found":51,"critical":7,"quality_score":0,
 "commit":"5846078","via":"ship","wtree":"febca88f...","dirty":false}
```

Current `---WTREE---` is `febca88f...`, so the second row grades CURRENT. No review pass read `febca88f`. The three `fix:` commits between `a35d094` and `5846078` are the unreviewed delta, and they are the *only* part of the branch a reviewer had not seen.

Note the second row also carries `"critical":7,"quality_score":0` and still grades CURRENT — the gate keys on binding alone, so an unresolved-critical record certified against the final tree reads as clean.

## Contrast: gstack-evidence already does this right

`bin/gstack-evidence:393-400`:

```js
// TOCTOU guard: the fingerprint is only trustworthy when the content was
// IDENTICAL before and after the run. A mid-run edit omits wtree, so
// check grades STALE instead of certifying content the suite never ran.
const wtreeAfter = currentWtree();
if (wtreeBefore && wtreeAfter && wtreeBefore === wtreeAfter) {
  rec.wtree = wtreeAfter;
} else if (wtreeBefore || wtreeAfter) {
  warn("working-tree content changed during the run — evidence recorded without a content fingerprint (will grade STALE)");
```

In the same session that produced the rows above, this guard worked exactly as intended: a later docs commit invalidated the recorded test run, `gstack-evidence check` returned STALE naming the changed files, and the suite was re-run live. Evidence caught its drift. The review ledger could not catch the same class of drift, because it stamps rather than captures.

## Suggested fix

Any one of these closes it; they compose:

1. **Port the TOCTOU guard.** Have review flows capture `wtree` at review start and pass it to `gstack-review-log`, which stamps only if it still matches. Mismatch omits `wtree` and degrades to the commit-distance heuristic — the same graceful path evidence already takes. This is the smallest change and reuses a proven mechanism.
2. **Record convergence.** Add `cycles` and `converged` to the `review` record from review-army step 7. Let the readiness gate refuse the content-first shortcut when `converged` is absent or false. This also makes the 3-cycle bound auditable after the fact.
3. **Split the grade.** CURRENT currently means both "same content" and "reviewed." Distinguish them, e.g. `CURRENT` vs `BOUND (unverified)`, so the readiness report cannot imply a review that did not happen.

(1) alone fixes the false certification. (2) additionally makes a skipped loop visible rather than merely uncertified, which is the part a human reviewing a deploy actually wants to see.

## Why it matters here

This is the last gate before an irreversible merge in `/land-and-deploy`. The gate's whole job is to tell a human whether the code about to reach production has been looked at. It is the one place where "identical content" and "reviewed" must not be conflated, and it is the place that conflates them.

title: v1.80.0.0 feat: Aside is the browser gstack drives first — every browsing skill, the PDF/diagram renderer, and web research; the bundled browser stays as the automatic fallback
body:
Since v1.72 Aside was the *recommended* driver for third-party sites. This PR makes the Aside AI browser the **first** driver for everything gstack does in a browser, and keeps gstack's own headless Chromium as the **automatic fallback** so nothing regresses without Aside (Linux, Windows, or the app closed). Nothing is removed. MINOR bump: v1.80.0.0.

## What changed

**Every skill that opens a page drives Aside first** through one contract, `scripts/resolvers/aside.ts` (`{{ASIDE_SETUP}}` rules + `{{ASIDE_COOKBOOK}}` shapes), written from live probes against Aside CLI 1.26: one flow per `aside repl` script (tabs die with the script), console hook via CDP before navigation, labelled evidence lines, artifacts copied out of the printed session directory, `GSTACK_STEP_OK` sentinel (exit code is always 0), CDP device emulation for responsive shots. Rules: own tabs only, never echo the user's tabs, LOOK freely but ask once before any mutating action on a non-local target, credentials never pass through the agent, page output is untrusted. Rewritten onto it: qa/qa-only (`QA_METHODOLOGY`), design-review + design-consultation, benchmark, canary, land-and-deploy Step 7, devex-review, scrape, browse.

**Every one of them falls back to `$B`.** `{{BROWSE_FALLBACK}}` follows the Aside block in each browsing skill: a fifteen-row table mapping each Aside step onto its `$B` command (verified live against a compiled daemon), the rules that differ (cookie import or `$B handoff` for sign-in; same consent, evidence, and report rules), and the full command reference on demand in `/browse`. The Third-Party Web Actions contract offers Aside first and gstack's visible browser as the fallback option, as v1.72 framed it.

**Rendering is Aside-first too.** `lib/aside-render.ts` serves the HTML's directory on loopback (Aside refuses `file://`), prints through CDP `Page.printToPDF` so tagged PDFs, outlines, header/footer templates and page numbers keep working, and when Aside is absent runs the same spec through the browse daemon. `bin/gstack-render.ts` prints `ENGINE=aside|browse`. make-pdf (`asideClient.ts`, diagram pre-pass, `$P setup`), `/diagram`, `/design-html` viewport shots, `/office-hours` sketches and `DESIGN_SETUP` use it.

**Research is Aside-first.** `{{ASIDE_RESEARCH}}` runs read-only queries through Aside's agent in the user's real browser, falls back to the WebSearch tool, then to in-distribution knowledge. Codex's own `web_search` flag is unchanged.

**Housekeeping:** `setup` and `gen-skill-docs` now prune renders of skills that no longer exist in the source tree (the generator never deleted before). `lib/claude-bin.ts` and `lib/error-handling.ts` become canonical; `browse/src` re-exports them.

## Evidence (live, Aside app open, macOS; fallback forced with `GSTACK_SKIP_ASIDE=1` / a PATH without `aside`)

- Cookbook and skill scripts executed verbatim from the rendered docs against a localhost fixture on Aside: read (tree, console errors, text, screenshot), flow (fill/click, DOM diff, injected `console.error` captured), annotated, responsive 375/768/1440, same-origin link status 200/404, performance, benchmark NAV/PAINT/LCP, deploy `responseStatus: 200`, design extraction, scrape JSON.
- Every row of the `$B` translation table executed against a compiled browse daemon (goto, snapshot -i/-D, click, fill, console --errors, links, text, perf, js, eval, screenshot, responsive, annotated snapshot, pdf, handoff, closetab).
- Renderer on both engines: tagged PDF with header + page numbers, JPEG/PNG shots, in-page payloads to files; `ENGINE=browse` path verified with a real JPEG at 375px and `pdfinfo` Tagged: yes. Mermaid SVG/PNG/excalidraw triplet in 6s on Aside.
- make-pdf: real markdown (headings, table, emoji, mermaid fence, `--toc`) → 2-page tagged PDF on Aside; `make-pdf/test/e2e` gates 9 pass on Aside **and** 9 pass on the browse fallback.
- E2E through real `claude -p` sessions: aside-scrape-json, aside-browse-flow, aside-browse-basic, aside-canary-quick, aside-qa-quick, diagram triplet, diagram authoring quality — 7/7 PASS (~$1.00).
- Free suite: `bun run test` green. `test/aside-driver.test.ts` asserts every browsing skill carries `## BROWSER SETUP (Aside` followed by `## Browser fallback`; `test/aside-render.test.ts` runs a live render on each engine present.

**Known limits:** the live Aside gates self-skip in CI (no Aside on runners; the `$B` path covers them there); Aside CLI 1.26 lacks the `session`/`memory`/`skills` commands its own skill doc lists (nothing here depends on them). Follow-ups in TODOS.md: keep the `$B` translation table in sync with the cookbook, a macOS runner for the live Aside E2E, an optional MCP path for a persistent page.

title: browse: headless daemon start in one project kills the live headed browser in another (unconditional killOrphanChromium)
body:
## Environment

- gstack 1.80.0.0 (`c241216`), CLI built from the same tree
- macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6.0), arm64, Bun 1.3.13
- Workflow: several Claude Code sessions open at once in different project directories, one of them driving the headed GStack Browser (`/connect-chrome`) with real logins

## Symptom

The headed browser window "randomly" disappears mid-session. The next `$B` command in that project keeps working, but against a fresh **headless** daemon with no cookies, so the agent hits a login wall and has to re-authenticate. There are no macOS crash reports for Chromium. The profile's `Preferences` records `exit_type: Crashed`.

Reproduced 2026-08-09 and still present in the v1.80.0.0 source.

## Root cause

`startServer()` in `browse/src/cli.ts` calls `killOrphanChromium()` unconditionally before every daemon start, in every project (`browse/src/cli.ts:518`, added in #1781):

```ts
  // #1781: clear a stale Chromium profile lock (and kill the orphan still
  // holding it) before launch ...
  await killOrphanChromium();
  cleanChromiumProfileLocks();
```

`killOrphanChromium()` (`browse/src/cli.ts:283`) reads the **global** `~/.gstack/chromium-profile/SingletonLock`, parses the PID out of it, and SIGTERM/SIGKILLs that PID if it is alive. It never checks whether that PID belongs to a dead daemon's orphan or to a live headed browser owned by a *different* project's daemon.

So with two concurrent sessions:

1. Project A runs `$B connect` (headed). Chromium writes `SingletonLock -> host-<pidA>` in the shared profile.
2. Project B runs any `$B` command (or `/make-pdf`, which starts a browse daemon). Its `startServer()` sees the lock, finds `pidA` alive, and kills it.
3. Project A's headed daemon exits(2). Its stderr is `stdio: 'ignore'`, so nothing is printed.
4. Project A's next `$B` command auto-starts a replacement daemon, which is headless by default, so commands keep succeeding but the window and all logins are gone.

Timeline from the 2026-08-09 reproduction: project B's `/make-pdf` started a daemon at 09:03:46 EDT; project A's headed browser died in the same second; the agent in A then hit a Microsoft login wall on the next navigation; `~/.gstack/.auth.json` shows the manual headed reconnect at 09:07.

This is a different class from #1781 (restart crash-loop on a stale lock) and #2219 (busy daemon mistaken for dead). Here the daemon and the browser are both healthy; a *third party* kills them because the profile lock is machine-global while daemon starts are per-project.

Note the headless launch never uses `userDataDir` (see the comment on `reapRecordedChromium`, #2709), so a headless start has no reason to touch the profile lock at all.

## Suggested fix

Any one of these closes it:

1. Only run `killOrphanChromium()` / `cleanChromiumProfileLocks()` when the new daemon is itself headed (`BROWSE_HEADED=1`). Headless daemons launch without a profile and cannot be blocked by the lock.
2. Before killing the lock holder, verify it is actually an orphan: check that no live browse daemon (any project's state file) records that Chromium PID, or that its parent process is dead.
3. Independently, log headed-daemon stderr to `~/.gstack/browse-daemon.log` instead of `stdio: 'ignore'`, so a kill like this is visible.

Option 1 is the smallest change and matches the existing identity-gated approach in `reapRecordedChromium`.

title: fix(aside): the readiness probe can never detect Aside under zsh
body:
Fixes #2842.

## Why (in your own words)

On any machine whose shell is zsh — the macOS default, and what agent harnesses run their shell tool as — the BROWSER SETUP probe answers `ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING` while Aside is running fine. The status line is the small part. The damage is that every browsing skill then silently drops to the bundled headless browser, which has none of the user's cookies or logged-in sessions, so a page behind a login comes back signed-out and the skill blames the site instead of the probe. #2810 made Aside the browser gstack drives first; under zsh that contract was unreachable, and Aside only ships for macOS, where zsh *is* the shell.

The probe holds its deadline in a variable and expands it unquoted, so it only becomes two words in a shell that word-splits unquoted expansions. zsh does not — it looks for one command named `gtimeout 30`. The variable is the vehicle for all three deadline arms, so under zsh every arm fails, including the `perl` arm that is the only one present on a stock Mac.

This change makes the deadline a function, which takes the command as `"$@"`, already split, and behaves identically in sh, bash and zsh.

## Live evidence

Environment: macOS 15 (Darwin 25.6.0), zsh 5.9, bash 3.2, aside 1.26.906.1630 — installed, signed in, answering `aside repl` in ~5 ms throughout. Each row narrows `PATH` so a different deadline arm is selected; the probe is extracted verbatim from the rendered `browse/SKILL.md`.

**The mechanism, isolated:**

```
$ _T="gtimeout 30"; $_T echo hi
zsh: command not found: gtimeout 30
$ ${=_T} echo hi          # zsh word-split forced, to confirm the cause
hi
```

**Before — `main` at v1.87.0.0.** Aside was up the whole time:

```
deadline arm            zsh                  bash    sh
gtimeout (coreutils)    ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING    READY   READY
timeout only            ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING    READY   READY
perl only (stock Mac)   ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING    READY   READY
```

**After — this branch:**

```
deadline arm            zsh      bash     sh
gtimeout (coreutils)    READY    READY    READY
timeout only            READY    READY    READY
perl only (stock Mac)   READY    READY    READY
none of the three       READY    READY    READY

$ GSTACK_SKIP_ASIDE=1 zsh probe.sh
NEEDS_ASIDE
```

`READY` is the full line `READY: aside 1.26.906.1630` in every cell; trimmed here for width.

**Why not `eval`.** `eval` splits in all three shells and is the obvious one-liner — this PR carried it until I measured the `perl` arm. `eval` re-parses the string, so the parens and the `;` in `perl -e alarm(shift);exec(@ARGV) 30` stop being data and become syntax:

```
$ # with eval, perl arm selected
bash: syntax error near unexpected token `('
zsh:  unknown file attribute: h

deadline arm            eval, zsh            eval, bash
gtimeout                READY                READY
timeout only            READY                READY
perl only (stock Mac)   ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING    ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING
```

A stock Mac has no Homebrew coreutils and no GNU `timeout`, but does have `/usr/bin/perl` — so `eval` trades the zsh bug for a regression on the default macOS install, and takes bash down with it. Recorded here so the next person doesn't reach for it. The same reasoning rules out `${=_T}` (zsh-only): anything that keeps the deadline a string has to re-split or re-parse it.

**Tests:**

```
$ bun test test/aside-driver.test.ts test/host-config.test.ts
 105 pass
 0 fail
 539 expect() calls
```

## Scope

- **Changed:** `scripts/resolvers/aside.ts` — the deadline becomes `_gs_bounded()`, same gtimeout → timeout → perl alarm order, plus a 4th arm that runs the call unbounded when none of the three exists (what the empty `_T` already did). `test/aside-driver.test.ts` — the assertion pinned the broken invocation verbatim, so it now pins the function, asserts the 4th arm, and asserts neither `$_T aside repl` nor an `eval … aside repl` form can come back. The 19 generated `SKILL.md` files and the 3 `test/fixtures/golden/` fixtures are regenerated, not hand-edited (`bun run gen:skill-docs`; goldens rendered the way `test/host-config.test.ts` renders them).
- **Verified live by:** running the probe extracted from the rendered `browse/SKILL.md` under zsh, bash and sh, once per deadline arm (PATH narrowed to select each), before and after, with Aside live — the tables above. Plus the opt-out path and the two test files.
- **Did NOT test:** Linux or Windows hosts (Aside is macOS-only; there the probe short-circuits on `command -v aside` and the fallback browser takes over — that path is unchanged). No `claude -p` E2E run. I did not exercise a machine where `aside` exists but the app is genuinely down; the `ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING` branch is unchanged by this PR.

## Liveness proof (required for external contributors)

Authenticated login: `gh api user --jq .login` → `AntonioVitalic`.

<!-- LIVENESS_SCREENSHOT -->

## Checklist

- [ ] Liveness screenshot attached (`GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface) or PR author is @garrytan (owner exemption)
- [x] This is not a generated-file-only diff (I edited the source/template and regenerated)
- [x] No ETHOS.md edits, and no changes to voice / founder perspective / YC references
- [x] New public command / external service / host adapter has an accepted issue linked (or N/A) — N/A
- [x] Linked issue or reproduction: #2842

## Related

#2848 and #2854 report the same defect and land on the same shape of fix, which suggests a function is the answer rather than a taste call. Two notes for whoever triages:

- #2854 says the perl arm is also broken under bash today. It isn't: an unquoted expansion is split on IFS, but its metacharacters are never re-parsed, so the `;` stays inside a word and the arm runs. It breaks only once the string goes through `eval` — the table above.
- The 4th arm (`else "$@"`) is load-bearing: with none of the three present, today's empty `_T` still runs the call, and a function without that arm would drop it.

Introduced in #2810.

title: gstack-settings-hook renames onto $SETTINGS_FILE without resolving it — replaces a symlinked settings.json with a regular file, and the write misses the real file
body:
## Summary

`gstack-settings-hook` writes `settings.json` with tmp-file + `rename()` but never resolves the target path first. When `~/.claude/settings.json` is a **symlink** (the standard dotfiles pattern — the real file lives in a version-controlled repo), the rename replaces the symlink with a regular file.

Two things then go wrong silently:

1. Live config is decoupled from version control. `git status` in the dotfiles repo stays clean, because the tracked file is no longer the file Claude Code reads.
2. The write itself lands in the wrong place. The repo copy never receives it, so the next `bootstrap.sh`-style re-link overwrites the runtime changes with a stale copy.

Nothing reports an error. Version tested: **1.81.0.0**.

## Reproduction

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/gs-demo/repo /tmp/gs-demo/claude
printf '{\n  "hooks": {}\n}\n' > /tmp/gs-demo/repo/settings.json
ln -s /tmp/gs-demo/repo/settings.json /tmp/gs-demo/claude/settings.json

GSTACK_SETTINGS_FILE=/tmp/gs-demo/claude/settings.json \
  gstack-settings-hook add-event \
    --event PostToolUse --command /tmp/demo-hook --source demo-tag --timeout 5

ls -la /tmp/gs-demo/claude/settings.json
grep -c demo-tag /tmp/gs-demo/repo/settings.json    # the version-controlled copy
grep -c demo-tag /tmp/gs-demo/claude/settings.json  # the new regular file
```

Actual:

```
before: lrwxr-xr-x  settings.json -> /tmp/gs-demo/repo/settings.json
after:  -rw-r--r--  settings.json          # symlink gone, now a regular file

repo copy received the write: 0
live file received the write: 1
```

Expected: the symlink survives and the write lands in `/tmp/gs-demo/repo/settings.json`.

## Cause

`SETTINGS_FILE` is taken as given and never resolved:

```sh
# bin/gstack-settings-hook:70
SETTINGS_FILE="${GSTACK_SETTINGS_FILE:-${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json}"
```

and the write renames straight onto it:

```js
// bin/gstack-settings-hook:242, in gsWriteIfChanged()
fs.renameSync(tmp, path);
```

`rename(2)` operates on the link itself, not its target, so the symlink is replaced.

Same defect in the `rollback` path, which is a second call site:

```sh
# bin/gstack-settings-hook:~815
_RB_TMP="$SETTINGS_FILE.tmp.$$.$RANDOM"
cp "$LATEST" "$_RB_TMP"
mv "$_RB_TMP" "$SETTINGS_FILE"
```

## Suggested fix

Resolve the real path before writing, and derive the temp path from the **resolved** directory so the rename stays atomic and on the same filesystem. `GSTACK_TMP_PATH` (line 325), `GSTACK_BACKUP_PATH` and `GSTACK_BAK_LATEST` are all built from the unresolved `$SETTINGS_FILE`, so they need the same treatment:

```sh
if [ -L "$SETTINGS_FILE" ]; then
  SETTINGS_FILE="$(readlink -f "$SETTINGS_FILE" 2>/dev/null || python3 -c 'import os,sys;print(os.path.realpath(sys.argv[1]))' "$SETTINGS_FILE")"
fi
```

(macOS `readlink` has no `-f` on older systems, hence the fallback.)

A note on why this looks like an oversight rather than a design choice: `gsWriteIfChanged` already goes out of its way to preserve the file **mode** across the rename —

```js
// Preserve the live file mode across the tmp+rename (settings.json can
// carry API keys in its env block -- a user-tightened 0600 must never be
// silently broadened to the default 0644).
```

Symlink-ness is the same class of user-side property, and it is currently the one that gets destroyed.

## Impact in practice

This has clobbered my setup six times since 2026-05-31. The path that triggers it most often is indirect: Claude Code's own settings writes (`/effort`, `/config`, a theme or plugin toggle) re-serialize the `hooks` arrays and drop the `_gstack_source` keys. `prune-stale` then legitimately restores them at the next `./setup` — and that restoring write is what replaces the symlink. So the more correctly gstack heals its own tags, the more reliably it breaks a symlinked `settings.json`.

Because `./setup` is invoked from `/gstack-upgrade`, `bootstrap.sh`, `/setup-gbrain` and the auto-upgrade preamble inside other skills, there is no single moment a user can watch for.

title: v1.84.0.0 feat: impeccable interop: detector pre-pass in four design skills, DOM-mode scans, open DESIGN.md format, one typed slop catalog
body:
## Summary

gstack's design skills gain a deterministic pre-pass from [impeccable](https://impeccable.style)'s engine when the user has installed it, speak its rule ids in gstack's own voice, write and read the open DESIGN.md format, and keep one typed catalog for the AI-slop vocabulary. Plan: `docs/designs/IMPECCABLE_INTEROP.md` (CEO + eng reviewed, one PR by user decision). 28 substantive commits, bisected.

**Detector (`bin/gstack-design-detect.ts`, `lib/design-detect-contract.ts`)**
- `probe | scan | rules`; `design_detector: auto|off` config key. The probe reads files only; READY requires an engine whose real file is named `impeccable` under HOME (cache, env override, PATH, or the skill's sibling engine); anything inside the repository or cwd (project directories, strictly below HOME) is never executed. URLs refused; minimal engine environment (project PATH entries removed); per-batch timeout, whole-scan budget, 50 MB stdout cap, 5,000-finding cap, every field sanitized, sentinel forgery neutralized, `DETECT_TOP` fenced as untrusted, JSON names its untrusted fields; exit 3 = gstack bug.
- `--changed <base>`: NUL-safe git-derived frontend targets through the same allow-list; committed symlinks skipped; unknown, empty, or option-like bases refused with exit 1.
- DOM dumps under `~/.gstack/projects/<slug>/designs/**/dom/` (and any designs/ directory) scan with `--no-inline-ignores`; gstack-authored artifacts and repo files keep theirs.

**Consent-gated engine install (`gstack-design-detect.ts install`, `design_detector_install_prompted`)**
- When the probe finds no engine and the user has never answered, the design skills ask one AskUserQuestion, once, in interactive sessions only (spawned/headless never install or ask; Conductor gets the prose brief): install now, not now, never ask again, or turn the detector off. A yes downloads engine 0.1.3 for this platform from impeccable's own GitHub release, verifies it against the checksum pinned in `lib/design-detect-contract.ts` (all five platforms), writes an egress receipt before the fetch (fail-closed, registered in the wiring test's polarity table), caps and streams the download, writes only after the hash matches, and installs the one file under `~/.impeccable/bin/<version>/`: no skill, no hook, no launcher, no `npx`. Verified end to end against the real release (16 MB, hash matches the fixture engine, binary runs). The `NOT_CACHED` hint no longer repeats once the user has declined, and its npx wording is corrected. License note: MIT and Apache-2.0 are compatible; prompting is not a license event; gstack still redistributes nothing.

**Skill wiring (`scripts/resolvers/design.ts`, `design-checklist.ts`, `review-army.ts`, templates)**
- `/design-review` Phase 0: source mode on a branch (base detected via `gh`, never assumed), DOM mode on any URL through one shared dump script (`lib/dom-dump.js`, an arrow function the page runs; Aside `pg.evaluate` or `$B js`, both spliced through closed-quote segments so a page URL never sits in a double-quoted bash string); dumps are hygiene-stripped, size-capped, redaction-checked at the dump cap, chmod 600, per run, deleted after Phase 9 unless `--keep-dom`; `design-baseline.json` schema 2 with per-page rule counts and an `engine changed` caveat; `Detector: N → M`; `/impeccable <cmd>` handoffs.
- `/review` and `/ship` design pass start with the scan (tier buckets, detector+checklist dedupe); `/design-html` bounded slop gate; PR body `Detector:` line.
- `review/design-checklist.md` is generated from the catalog (Claude host, `--out-dir` aware, dry-run STALE/FRESH).

**Catalog and doctrine (`lib/design-catalog.ts`)**
- 86 typed entries (57 slop, 29 quality, 61 matching impeccable ids, 11 legacy lines byte-identical to the old `AI_SLOP_BLACKLIST`), `mockupNever` (10) feeding the design binary's prompt, `HANDOFF_COMMANDS`, fonts lists. Persuade/Operate/Read/Experience modes with aliases, craft-floor reflexes, calibration, font procedure with a role-scoped overused list, color strategies, landing rules aligned (one authored motion moment, no halo/spotlight/stripe/grid gradients), Codex design-voice prompts aligned.

**Open DESIGN.md format (`lib/design-md.ts`, `bin/gstack-design-md.ts`, `design/src/memory.ts`)**
- `check | convert | tokens | mark`; format marker inside the front matter (YAML comment) or an HTML comment on legacy files; `convert` backs up and refuses ambiguous or duplicate-heading input; text-level editors change one section or one line and preserve every other byte, the BOM, and the majority line ending; symlinked DESIGN.md edited through the link; unclosed fences refused; `~~~` fences honored; YAML emitter quotes control chars, ` #`, and YAML 1.2 numerics. `/design-consultation` writes the spec and asks once about conversion; `PRODUCT.md` prefills; gstack's own DESIGN.md converted.

**Attribution and docs**: `NOTICE.md`, `licenses/Apache-2.0.txt`, changed-file headers; README, ARCHITECTURE, PROJECT_STRUCTURE, skills.md, CONTRIBUTING, TESTING_INTERNALS, CLAUDE.md; TODOS.md carries 7 reasoned deferrals from the reviews.

## Test Coverage

Step 7 coverage audit before the fix rounds: 74% of new code paths covered, 24 gaps; tests were generated for every gap and every review-cycle fix landed with its own test. Static count: 194 new `test()` declarations across 11 files (`gstack-design-detect` 61, `design-md` 48, `design-catalog` 23, `impeccable-fixtures` 16, `design-checklist-sync` 9, `design-detect-contract` 8, `gen-skill-docs` +19, `gstack-config-defaults` +4, `brief` 3, `frontend-scope` 2, `dom-dump-hygiene` 1).

```
lib/design-detect-contract.ts ── contract + neutralizeSentinels ── test/design-detect-contract.test.ts (8)
bin/gstack-design-detect.ts ─── probe/scan/rules, trust rules ──── test/gstack-design-detect.test.ts (61)
lib/design-catalog.ts ────────── invariants, partitions ─────────── test/design-catalog.test.ts (23)
lib/design-md.ts + bin ───────── parse/convert/splice/mark ──────── test/design-md.test.ts (48)
lib/dom-dump-script.ts ───────── hygiene in a real Chromium ──────── test/dom-dump-hygiene.test.ts (CI / opt-in)
scripts/resolvers/* ──────────── rendered prose + bash pins ──────── test/gen-skill-docs.test.ts, design-checklist-sync.test.ts
E2E ──────────────────────────── detector shim (source + DOM), slop gate, review design lite, consultation core/existing
```

## Pre-Landing Review

Three cycles (checklist + security, testing, maintainability, design, performance/simplification specialists), a Red Team pass, and the Claude adversarial subagent. Every CRITICAL was reproduced before the fix and is pinned by a test: repository-local engine execution (any READY candidate is now HOME-rooted, named `impeccable`, checked by realpath); `--changed` allow-list bypass via committed symlinks; VERSION-file and sentinel forgery; a swallowed failing `git diff`; the DOM dump running as an IIFE in Aside's repl sandbox; the double-quoted Aside block that put a page URL under `$(...)` expansion; `mark`/extraction rewriting legacy files (now text-level splices, CRLF and BOM preserved); the redaction gate's 1 MiB default deleting every 1 to 10 MiB dump; the HOME-as-cwd fallback that defeated the project rule; prototype-member rule ids; symlinked DESIGN.md replaced; audit directories walked with page-controlled inline ignores; print/alternate stylesheets scanned as page CSS.

Kept as-is with reasons: `--format raw` (fixture capture path), the hand-rolled argv loop (keeps the unknown-flag warning), the ~13 KB generated checklist (conditional read). Deferred to TODOS.md: scan cache, `$D check` rubric, taste-profile interplay, CEO Section 11 bullets, the `bin/*.ts` `.env` audit, design-review Phases 7-11 carve, Kiro `bin/` linking.

Residual property worth knowing: every Aside script in the tree is a single-quoted bash string, so a `'` inside a pasted URL ends it; the DOM dump prose tells the agent to percent-encode `'` and never paste an unread URL. Tree-wide, not new here.

**Codex passes: no coverage.** `codex exec` and `codex review` both failed to start in this environment (the CLI's sandbox needs `bwrap`, absent here); reported as missing coverage, not a clean bill.

## Design Review

Frontend files in the diff are test fixtures with planted anti-patterns. Design Review (lite) on the doctrine changes ran through the review army's design specialist across the cycles (contradictions found and fixed: motion counts, overused-display scope, Rule 4 wording, blacklist header, slop-gate blessings, DESIGN.md rows, variant dials). Detector: not installed (probe printed `IMPECCABLE_NOT_AVAILABLE` on this machine; the real engine lives in a scratch directory used only to capture fixtures).

## Eval Results

Full diff-selected run (`bun run test:evals` via `gstack-detach`, ~$22.78): 92 PASS, 3 FAIL, of which `/design-consultation core` ×2 was this branch (the open DESIGN.md template's Overview no longer contains the literal "aesthetic"; the section-synonym check now knows "Creative North Star" / "Key characteristics"; the LLM judge had passed both attempts) and `/ship review dashboard via attribution` was a zero-turn harness timeout that passed on its immediate retry. Re-runs on the fixed tree: `test/skill-e2e-design.test.ts` + `test/skill-e2e-review.test.ts` with `EVALS_ALL=1`, 12/12 PASS (~$10.54); after the adversarial fixes, detector shim (source + DOM), slop gate, review design lite, consultation core, 5/5 PASS (~$5.38). Gate tier: `design-review-detector-shim` (source and DOM); periodic: `design-html-slop-gate`.

## Plan Completion

Plan `docs/designs/IMPECCABLE_INTEROP.md` (promoted from the CEO plan), 13 planned commits plus 7b, all landed. Step 8 audit: 47 line items, every one DONE or consciously CHANGED (the 12 CHANGED items are recorded in the plan doc's superseded notes, e.g. the hook never skips a scan, the dump is an arrow function called in the page, the engine version is never a filesystem path); the two items first marked UNVERIFIABLE were verified afterwards (`bun run test:windows` passes; the real engine loads `design-system-*` rules against gstack's converted DESIGN.md). The design-review eager ceiling landed at 31,319 tokens (+2.87K against the review's 2.5K target after every planned lever; the next lever is filed in TODOS.md).

## Verification Results

Skipped: no running server for the plan's verification section (NO_SERVER); the detector shim E2E cases cover the runtime path with the fake engine.

## TODOS

No TODO items completed in this PR. Seven reasoned deferrals filed under "impeccable interop deferrals" in TODOS.md (from the CEO, eng, and code reviews).

## Documentation

- **CLAUDE.md**: quick map names `lib/design-catalog.ts`, `bin/gstack-design-detect.ts`, `bin/gstack-design-md.ts`; SKILL.md workflow now states that `bun run gen:skill-docs` also writes `review/design-checklist.md` (from `lib/design-catalog.ts`) and `lib/dom-dump.js` (from `lib/dom-dump-script.ts`), edit the source never the generated file (`test/design-checklist-sync.test.ts`).
- **CONTRIBUTING.md**: `lib/design-catalog.ts` in the tree; generated-files and rebuild bullets cover the catalog and the two generated artifacts; new tier-1 bullet for the seven design suites plus `test/dom-dump-hygiene.test.ts` (CI or `GSTACK_DOM_DUMP_HYGIENE=1`).
- **ARCHITECTURE.md**: template-system section notes the generator's two non-skill-doc outputs.
- **docs/PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md**: `resolvers/design-checklist`, impeccable fixtures + `fake-impeccable.ts` shim, `review/design-checklist.md` marked GENERATED, `docs/designs/IMPECCABLE_INTEROP.md` named (now discoverable from CLAUDE.md).
- **docs/skills.md**: `/design-consultation` writes the open DESIGN.md format (front-matter tokens, one-time conversion with backup, `PRODUCT.md` prefill); `/design-html` Slop gate paragraph; `/review` Design pass paragraph.
- **docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md**: `dom-dump-hygiene` on the browse-binary leg, opt-in outside CI.
- Verified against code: 86 catalog entries (57 slop / 29 quality), 61 engine rules, 10 mockup-never names, ceiling 31,319. Already current on-branch: README, NOTICE.md, licenses/, TODOS.md deferrals, agents digest v1.82.0.0, CHANGELOG.

### Documentation Debt
- `bin/gstack-design-detect.ts` and `bin/gstack-design-md.ts` have reference coverage (file headers, CHANGELOG, PROJECT_STRUCTURE) but no how-to page; `design_detector` documented in `gstack-config` help plus README/skills.md one-liners. `/document-generate` candidate.

## CI fixes on this branch
- Free tests: the DOM hygiene test drove a private browse daemon that never came up under the six-shard runner and starved two unrelated files; it now drives Playwright Chromium directly (no daemon, no health window) and self-skips without the bundle.
- Windows free tests: the checklist render pins compare paths with forward slashes.
- Quality gate: the redaction test's planted PEM block is assembled at runtime so the diff scan never sees a key-shaped line.

## Test plan
- [x] Free suite (`bun run test`, recorded with `gstack-evidence`): 9,212 tests ran, 9,209 pass. The 3 failures are `browse/test/handoff.test.ts` (needs a display; this Linux box has no X server); `browse/` is byte-identical to `main` on this branch, so they cannot originate here.
- [x] Paid E2E: 92/95 on the full run with both branch-caused failures fixed and re-proven; 12/12 and 5/5 on the reruns against the final tree.
- [x] `bun run test:windows` passes (Step 8 audit).
- [x] `gstack-design-detect.ts install` run for real against github.com/pbakaus/impeccable engine-v0.1.3 into a scratch home: pinned hash matched, receipt + outcome in the ledger, the installed binary runs; a wrong `--sha256` wrote nothing.
- [x] Fixtures captured from a real impeccable install (engine 0.1.3, 61 rules) in a scratch directory outside the repo; the `design-system-*` rules fire against gstack's converted DESIGN.md.
- [ ] Not run here: Codex adversarial and structured review (sandbox launcher missing); `test/dom-dump-hygiene.test.ts` in a quiet Chromium (the browse daemon repeatedly missed its health window under eval load; it runs in CI).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Review docs: AGENTS.md review sections + CodeRabbit config
body:
## Problem

Since the review-layer verdict (Architecture E, VAS-2751) the fleet routes review by artefact class, but the gstack fork carried none of the per-repo review surface it depends on: no `## Review guidelines` / `## Review fix-pass rules` for Codex GitHub review or CodeRabbit to apply and no `.coderabbit.yaml`. Reviewers judged diffs from folklore, severity and scope varied by session, and the 8 Sep calibration showed both single-pass reviewers missing a cross-file defect that the guidelines' diff-expansion triggers now name explicitly.

## Outcome

AGENTS.md gains the canonical review guidelines, the artefact-class triage preamble and the fix-pass rules. .coderabbit.yaml embeds the fleet's generated block with request_changes_workflow: false.

## Evidence

One read-only codex pass on candidate 0cc73067: no P0/P1. CodeRabbit auto-review and CI conclude on this PR (the config lands with `request_changes_workflow: false`, so a CodeRabbit opinion can never hard-block the merge).

Part of VAS-2757.

title: v1.84.1.0 fix: default Codex and Claude to frontier models
body:
## Summary

gstack-owned Codex reviews, consultations, and evals default to `gpt-6-astra`. Claude outside voices and eval capture/judging default to `claude-fable-5-1`.

Explicit model choices still win. Codex supports `GSTACK_CODEX_MODEL`, Claude outside voices support `GSTACK_CLAUDE_MODEL`, and evals preserve their existing model overrides. Readiness checks use the selected model; native Codex review also overrides the CLI's separate review-model pin.

These are release-maintained frontier defaults, not automatic model discovery. Warmup and distillation retain their cheaper defaults.

## CI Repairs

- Give frontier judges enough output budget for thinking and JSON, parse text after thinking blocks, and omit unsupported arm-judge temperature.
- Expand workflow sections in execution order without duplicate content. Include retro Compare Mode in its judge excerpt.
- Use agent-capture time budgets for deploy E2Es instead of shorter judge-call budgets.
- Correct workflow ambiguities exposed by the stronger judge: approval sequencing, native test commands, readiness-gated Aside choices, QA scoring, benchmark timing, deploy setup/recovery, and retro metric sources and report ordering.
- Make documentation review run before committing and publishing its fixes, retain CHANGELOG protection, and preserve raw PR-body bytes across the scan boundary. Ship now composes and scans before either creating or updating a PR.
- Preserve quality thresholds, model defaults, test assertions, and prompt-size limits. Add deterministic regression checks for the repaired contracts.

## Validation

- Full free suite passes on the tree merged with current `main`.
- Build, all-host generated-doc freshness, and diff checks pass.
- 30 affected live workflow-judge and consent tests pass.
- All six deploy E2Es pass locally, and the deploy CI slice passes with the capture-budget fix.
- Both live retro workflows pass; the revised Fable instruction judge scores 4/4/4.
- All six GitHub eval slices and their aggregate report pass on `f0c58b14`. Linux and Windows free tests, Windows setup, macOS PDF, generated-doc freshness, quality, dependency, workflow-lint, and version checks pass. Prior CI failures and their fixes are documented in the comments.

The pre-landing review fixed and rechecked model-argument and thinking-response compatibility. The initial Claude adversarial review timed out; a fresh-context Codex fallback review was completed. Overall line coverage was not measured.

## Documentation

README, CONTRIBUTING, skills documentation, and ARCHITECTURE document the frontier defaults and overrides. Existing paid-run estimates are labeled historical. Version and changelog are advanced to v1.84.1.0, preserving the releases that landed while CI repairs were in progress.

title: v1.83.0.0 feat: Memorable recall bridge, opt-in and receipted (supersedes #2831)
body:
## Summary

Supersedes #2831 (the fork PR from Memorable's engineers). Their three commits are cherry-picked with authorship preserved; everything after them brings the bridge up to gstack's spec as decided in `/plan-ceo-review` and `/plan-eng-review` (four Codex outside-voice passes, 41 of 45 points adopted), then hardened by the `/ship` review army, two adversarial passes, and a Codex structured review. Closing #2831 with a comment is left to the maintainer.

**The bridge (opt-in, default off, Claude Code only)**
- `bin/gstack-memorable enable | disable | status`: registers gstack's UserPromptSubmit hook at the stable install path (timeout 5), verifies the stable install carries this bridge first, refuses when Memorable's own installer already registered its hook, records gstack's own consent key `memorable_recall`, and never runs `memorable enable` (the vendor's consent is the user's to grant). `disable` flips the key off first, removes by identity, verifies both. `status` never executes the vendor. One lifecycle transition at a time (mkdir lock, mtime staleness, inode-checked atomic reclaim, owner liveness). Exit codes mirror the hook manager (1, 3, 4, 5).
- `hosts/claude/hooks/memorable-user-prompt-hook` (bash shim, forwards SIGTERM to bun) + `memorable-user-prompt-hook.ts`: one 4.5 s deadline clock; 1 MiB stdin cap; gate check via `gstack-config`; trust-policy veto by session cwd (fail-closed on any lookup failure, git run without inherited `GIT_*`, English messages, anchored match); HIGH-tier redaction pre-scan on raw bytes and decoded leaves (keys included; walk exhaustion refuses); vendor resolution with bash/TS parity; pre-spawn gate re-check; egress receipt before the spawn (fail-closed, `lockBudgetMs` from the clock, host `local:<executable>`); `runExternal` with an allowlisted env (identity, locale, temp, proxy/TLS/XDG, `MEMORABLE*`); only a string `additionalContext` accepted (tolerant first-object parse), control and Unicode format characters stripped, 8 KiB UTF-8-safe cap, trust envelope; outcome `exit:0 output-written bytes=N gstack_ms=N` after the awaited stdout write; rate-limited, keyed, 0600 `hook-errors.log`; stderr tail withheld when the engine finds a HIGH/MEDIUM shape. Windows refused (no process groups).
- `memorable_recall` config key (reject-and-preserve), `gstack-egress grants` row, `memorable-recall` sink (fail-closed polarity in the wiring test; `hosts/` swept).
- `./setup --no-team` keeps the hook; `gstack-uninstall` removes it by name and revokes the key wherever gstack's config lives, hook manager present or not.
- `docs/memorable-workflow-memory.md` (two consents, what gstack hands over and can attest, vendor claims attributed, runbook), README row + Docs row + privacy pointer, PROJECT_STRUCTURE.

**Hook manager (every gstack hook benefits)**
- `gstack-settings-hook remove-source` is identity-aware: removes the source's items whether or not Claude Code stripped the `_gstack_source` tag; other sources untouched; entries with nothing of ours byte-identical. Pinned for every `KNOWN_HOOKS` source.
- New read-only `list-items --event E [--owned-by S] [--command-regex RE]`: one JSON string literal per matching command, identity from the table, exit 3/4 fail-closed, filters intersect.

**Shared libraries**
- `lib/redact-engine.ts`: line/col by binary search over a lazily built line index. 256 KiB log-like prompt: 1,573 ms → 65 ms; 512 KiB: 6,182 ms → 126 ms (this box, main vs branch).
- `lib/egress-receipt.ts`: optional `lockBudgetMs` on `writeReceipt`/`writeOutcome` (default unchanged, validated).
- `lib/gbrain-repo-policy-client.ts`: `repoPolicyTier(url, env, timeoutMs)`.
- `hosts/claude/hooks/spawn-bin.ts`: `runExternal` (own process group killed on every resolve, resolve on exit with a stdout drain, deadline never rewrites a completed exit, stdout cap, drained stderr tail, stdin errors kept advisory, `onSpawn` kill handle, win32 refused).

**Follow-ups filed in TODOS.md**: mediation seam for a second third-party hook, Windows support (D21), envelope `kind`, payload-minimization ask to the vendor, latency measurement, resolver consolidation (D24), MEDIUM-tier hook policy, `list-items` at setup, one state-root rule for the bridge's stores, shared hook logging helper.

## Test Coverage

Coverage audit (Step 7, before generation): 95/135 paths (70%). The gap was closed with generated tests; the remove-source identity change is pinned for every source in the hook table (IRON RULE regression).

```
CODE PATHS                                                       USER FLOWS
[+] bin/gstack-settings-hook remove-source / list-items          [+] enable / disable / status (37 cases)
  ├── ★★★ identity removal for EVERY KNOWN_HOOKS source            ├── ★★★ happy path, twice, re-pointed, refusals (3/4/vendor-own/no canonical/no vendor/Windows)
  └── ★★★ list-items owned-by / regex / none / 3 / 4 / bad regex  ├── ★★★ disable: tag-stripped, vendor absent, corrupt settings, partial failure
[+] bin/gstack-config memorable_recall                           ├── ★★★ status: fresh, stripped, vendor-own, mismatch, bun missing, ledger line
  └── ★★★ default off, set on|off, typo preserved                 └── ★★★ locks: fresh wait, stale reclaim, mkdir gap, unreclaimable, version skew
[+] hosts/claude/hooks/memorable-user-prompt-hook(.ts)           [+] prompt → recall (59 cases)
  ├── ★★★ gate off / MEMORABLE=0 / gate re-check                   ├── ★★★ receipt before spawn, bytes+sha256, chain verifies, 5 concurrent
  ├── ★★★ policy deny/read-only/none/unreadable/corrupt/GIT_DIR    ├── ★★★ HIGH secret raw + escaped, oversize, walk exhaustion, unwritable ledger
  ├── ★★★ scan admission, budget seam, outcome strings             ├── ★★★ vendor: timeout (group kill), fork shim, flood, stderr flood, EPIPE, exit 1, decoy JSON, banners
  └── ★★★ envelope, 8 KiB UTF-8 cap, control+format strip          └── ★★★ host SIGTERM mid-flight kills the vendor group
[+] hosts/claude/hooks/spawn-bin.ts runExternal                  [+] setup --no-team / uninstall / grants
  └── ★★★ win32, ENOENT, exit-with-straggler, stdinError, ESPAWN   └── ★★★ sweep exclusion, named uninstall arm, consent revoked (kept state, other root, no hook manager), grants row
[+] lib/redact-engine.ts lineColAt                               [+] lib/egress-receipt.ts lockBudgetMs / gbrain-repo-policy-client timeoutMs
  └── ★★★ line start, blank lines, CRLF, first char, redaction      └── ★★★ 0 budget tries once, garbage rejected, default unchanged, 1 ms → unreadable
```

Tests: +133 new test cases across 13 test files (+1,900 lines). All bridge-related files green locally (5 passes of the flaky-prone cases, nonce-scoped orphan checks).

## Pre-Landing Review

Review army (testing, maintainability, security, performance, simplification, red team) ran three cycles; the loop hit the 3-cycle bound with cycle 3 still applying fixes (each cycle found new defects in the previous cycle's fix code, none reappearing), so the outside-model passes below served as the final read.

- Cycle 1: 35 findings (5 critical, 30 informational) + 3 advisory. 29 auto-fixed, 6 skipped with reasons (ledger rotation already filed; one-off CLI spawning `list-items` twice; prose-grepping the hook manager's output; shared hook logging helper filed; duplicated test scaffold; disable mismatch branch). Critical fixes: vendor timeout with empty stderr never logged; `runExternal` waited on `close` so a vendor that exited but left a helper holding pipes read as a timeout; redaction scan superlinear in match density; `repoPolicyTier` 10 s spawn outside the hook clock; system-wide `ps` grep in the orphan test.
- Cycle 2: 24 informational. Fixed: fail-closed policy lookup on git exit 128; tolerant first-JSON-object parse; keyed rate limiter; 0600 log; byte-sized scan admission; stable receipt payload class; doc and comment drift. 
- Cycle 3: 4 findings ≥6/10 + Claude adversarial (10). Fixed: shim forwards SIGTERM and the hook kills the in-flight vendor group; unmatched/brace-bearing banners; `LC_ALL=C` and anchored not-a-repo check; multi-key rate limiter; format-character stripping; stale-lock take-over falls through to the give-up; `disable` without `gstack-config`; ledger size in `status`. Investigate-only, documented: vendor runs in the session cwd (by design); state-root precedence differs across libs (filed).

Fix-First decisions were taken autonomously (spawned-style run in a Conductor workspace, no human in the loop); every skip is listed above.

## Design Review

No frontend files changed — design review skipped.

## Eval Results

`bun run eval:bg` (diff-selected; `hosts/claude/hooks/**` and `bin/gstack-config` are touchfile deps of the plan-tune-cathedral E2E tests): 50 pass, 408 skip, 0 fail. Log: `~/.gstack-dev/eval-runs/evals-gstack-kingstown-20260909-023537-121877.log`.

## Adversarial Review

```codex-review
Claude adversarial subagent (fresh context; fixtures reviewed in summary mode): 10 findings, 3 marked fix-before-merge, all three fixed (localized git message defeated the fail-closed lookup; vendor orphaned if the host kills the hook; a brace in a vendor banner dropped the answer). Recommendation was "fix findings 1-3 before merge".

Codex (gpt-6-astra, reasoning high). Both passes had to be fed the diff on stdin: this host has no bubblewrap, so `codex exec -s read-only` and `codex review --base main` cannot run any command and returned nothing on the first attempt (same launcher panic as the plan-review passes).
- Adversarial: 13 findings (5 P1, 8 P2). Fixed: group kill on every resolve incl. clean close; walk exhaustion refuses the hand-off and keys are scanned; inherited GIT_* dropped for the policy lookup; uninstall revokes consent independently of the hook manager and names a failed revocation; inode-checked stale-lock reclaim + owner liveness; whole stderr tail scanned before cropping; empty-override parity; git leak on cancellation; deadline no longer rewrites a completed exit; unmatched brace banner; status reports a failed receipt query as unknown. Not fixable, documented: a descendant the vendor detaches into its own session (setsid) escapes the group kill. Moot: "unquoted hook path" (the hook manager's ensure-event quotes paths with spaces; verified).
- Structured review: No P1 findings; 6 P2 (all in the adversarial list above, all fixed). GATE: PASS.
```

Cross-model synthesis: agreed by more than one source and fixed: close-vs-exit containment gap, GIT env/locale weaknesses in the policy lookup, brace-bearing banners, lock reclaim races, uninstall revocation placement, empty-override parity. Unique to Claude structured review: redaction scan cost, `repoPolicyTier` timeout, stderr withholding. Unique to Codex: walk-exhaustion refusal, whole-tail scan before crop, setsid boundary.

## Plan Completion

Plan: `~/.claude/plans/system-instruction-you-are-working-eager-hopcroft.md` (approved). Step 8 audit: 45 of 50 checklist items complete at audit time; the 3 PARTIAL items were closed during the ship (per-source remove-source regression for every KNOWN_HOOKS source; list-items combined filters; gbrain backend note and settings-rewrite race in the doc). Plan said v1.82.0.0; shipped as v1.83.0.0 because #2832 and #2835 already claim v1.82.0.0 and v1.82.1.0.

No TODO items completed in this PR. Ten follow-ups filed under "Memorable bridge follow-ups".

title: design detector probes IMPECCABLE_SKILL: absent for every Claude Code plugin install of impeccable
body:
`bin/gstack-design-detect.ts` looks for impeccable under `<root>/<SKILL_ROOTS entry>/skills/impeccable/`, but the normal way to get impeccable today is as a Claude Code plugin, which installs somewhere that pattern never reaches. Every plugin install therefore probes as `IMPECCABLE_SKILL: absent`, and the launcher and sibling-engine discovery in the same loop miss it too.

## Observed

gstack 1.84.1.0, Linux, impeccable plugin 4.3.1 installed via the Claude Code plugin marketplace.

```
$ bun ~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-design-detect.ts probe
IMPECCABLE_READY: /home/dgrant/.impeccable/bin/0.1.5/impeccable
IMPECCABLE_SKILL: absent
IMPECCABLE_HOOK: absent
IMPECCABLE_IGNORED_RULES:
IMPECCABLE_IGNORED_FILES:
IMPECCABLE_IGNORED_VALUES:
IMPECCABLE_ENGINE_UNTESTED: 0.1.5
```

The skill is installed and its 23 `/impeccable <cmd>` commands are live in the session. `IMPECCABLE_SKILL: absent` is wrong.

## Why

`SKILL_ROOTS` (`bin/gstack-design-detect.ts:163`) is `['.claude', '.agents', '.cursor', '.gemini', '.github', '.opencode']`, and the loop at :311 tests `path.join(root, sub, 'skills', 'impeccable', 'SKILL.md')` for each of repoRoot, cwd and HOME. That resolves to `~/.claude/skills/impeccable/SKILL.md`.

A plugin install puts it at:

```
~/.claude/plugins/cache/impeccable/impeccable/4.3.1/skills/impeccable/SKILL.md
~/.claude/plugins/cache/impeccable/impeccable/4.3.1/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable   # the launcher
```

`~/.claude/skills/impeccable/` does not exist and is not created by a plugin install — the manifest points Claude Code at `./skills/` inside the versioned plugin cache directory. The path segment `plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/` sits between the `SKILL_ROOTS` entry and the `skills/` the probe expects, so no amount of the existing pattern matches.

Three things in that one loop miss, not just the flag:

1. `p.skillPresent` stays false.
2. `p.launcher` stays null, so the `NOT_CACHED` state and its `DESIGN_DETECTOR_HINT` can never fire for a plugin user — the probe goes straight from "no engine" to `NOT_AVAILABLE` and the install offer, even though the user already has impeccable's own launcher on disk.
3. The sibling-engine candidate under `path.dirname(launcher)` is never considered.

## Consequence

Cosmetic but load-bearing for the interop story. The handoff lines are gated on `IMPECCABLE_SKILL: present`:

- `ship/sections/review-army.md:101` — "When the probe printed `IMPECCABLE_SKILL: present`, end each NEEDS INPUT detector row with the `handoff=` command"
- `design-review/SKILL.md:856` and `:1699` — same gate on deferred findings
- generated from `scripts/resolvers/design.ts:60` and `:892`, so `/review`, `/ship` and `/design-review` are all affected

So a plugin user gets the `FINDING-NNN [rule-id]` rows but never the `/impeccable typeset|layout|colorize|…` handoff that the v1.84.0.0 release notes describe as the point of the integration — and they have the skill installed and could act on it immediately. Detection itself is unaffected: scans run and findings are correct.

## Related: the engine was found by coincidence

On this machine `IMPECCABLE_READY` resolved even though gstack never installed anything — `design_detector_install_prompted=false` and `grep -c impeccable ~/.gstack/security/egress.jsonl` is 0. impeccable's own launcher had put the engine at `~/.impeccable/bin/0.1.5/impeccable`, which happens to be the exact cache layout gstack reserves for its own download, so the HOME-cache step matched by luck rather than through the plugin.

Two things follow from that. `IMPECCABLE_ENGINE_UNTESTED: 0.1.5` fires on every plugin user whose own launcher keeps the engine current, since gstack's fixtures pin 0.1.3. And a plugin user who says yes to the install offer gets a second, older engine written into the directory their launcher already manages.

## Reproduce

Install impeccable as a Claude Code plugin (`/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable` then install), with no `~/.claude/skills/impeccable/`, and run `gstack-design-detect probe`.

title: Aside probe always reports ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING under zsh: unquoted $_T timeout wrapper is never word-split
body:
## Summary

The `BROWSER SETUP (Aside)` probe reports `ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING` on every run under zsh, even when Aside is installed, running, signed in, and answering `aside repl` in about a second. Every browsing skill therefore silently falls back to the bundled headless Chromium and loses the user's real sessions, which is the whole point of the Aside path.

Under bash the same snippet works. macOS ships zsh as the default login shell, and agent harnesses commonly run their shell tool as zsh, so this likely affects a large share of macOS users.

## Environment

- gstack 1.84.1.0 (global git install)
- zsh 5.9, macOS 26.6.2 (arm64)
- Aside app 1.0.825.1, Aside CLI 1.26.906.1630
- `gtimeout` present (coreutils via Homebrew)

## Cause

`scripts/resolvers/aside.ts` lines 77-81 build the timeout wrapper as a string and then use it unquoted as a command prefix:

```sh
_T=""; command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1 && _T="gtimeout 30"; ...
elif $_T aside repl 'console.log("ASIDE_READY " + pwd)' 2>&1 | grep -q '^ASIDE_READY'; then
```

zsh does not perform word splitting on unquoted parameter expansions (`SH_WORD_SPLIT` is off by default). So `$_T` expands to a single word and zsh tries to execute a command whose name is literally `gtimeout 30`. That fails with `command not found`, the `elif` branch is false, and control falls through to the `else` that prints `ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING`.

The same applies to the `timeout 30` and `perl -e alarm(shift);exec(@ARGV) 30` variants.

## Reproduce

```sh
zsh -c '
_T=""; command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1 && _T="gtimeout 30"
$_T echo hello
'
# zsh: command not found: gtimeout 30
```

Full probe on a healthy install:

```
$ aside --version
1.26.906.1630

$ aside repl 'console.log("ASIDE_READY " + pwd)'
ASIDE_READY /Users/<me>/.aside/u/0/sessions/2026-09-10_Sx4tPfkzHidQY7cz
[ok | 24ms]                       # 1.25s wall clock

$ <BROWSER SETUP snippet verbatim>
ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING                 # expected READY

$ <same snippet, ${=_T} instead of $_T>
READY: aside 1.26.906.1630
```

## Blast radius

The snippet is generated from one template into 20 skills' `SKILL.md`:

`benchmark canary browse design-review cso design-consultation devex-review qa-only review land-and-deploy office-hours plan-eng-review plan-ceo-review investigate qa scrape plan-devex-review setup-deploy ship spec`

The failure is silent and misleading. The skill follows step 2 of the probe contract, asks the user to open Aside, re-runs, gets the same result, then quotes `ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING` and proceeds on the fallback. Nothing points at the shell, so it reads as a broken Aside install.

## Suggested fix

`${=_T}` fixes zsh but is a syntax error in bash. A shell function keeps it portable across both:

```sh
if command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then _t() { gtimeout 30 "$@"; }
elif command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then _t() { timeout 30 "$@"; }
elif command -v perl >/dev/null 2>&1; then _t() { perl -e 'alarm(shift); exec(@ARGV)' 30 "$@"; }
else _t() { "$@"; }
fi

if [ "${GSTACK_SKIP_ASIDE:-}" = "1" ] || ! command -v aside >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "NEEDS_ASIDE"
elif _t aside repl 'console.log("ASIDE_READY " + pwd)' 2>&1 | grep -q '^ASIDE_READY'; then
  echo "READY: aside $(aside --version 2>/dev/null)"
else
  echo "ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING"
fi
```

Worth grepping the rest of the codebase for the same `$VAR` as command-prefix pattern; any other snippet built for bash and executed under zsh has the same failure mode.

title: fix(aside): run the probe deadline through a function so zsh can detect Aside
body:
## Why (in your own words)

On macOS the default shell is zsh, and agent harnesses usually run their shell tool as zsh too. Under zsh, the BROWSER SETUP probe reports `ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING` on every run, even with Aside installed, running and signed in, so every browse-family skill silently falls back to `$B` and the user loses their real logged-in sessions. The probe stores its deadline as a string (`_T="gtimeout 30"`) and runs `$_T aside repl …`, and zsh doesn't word-split that, so it searches for a single command named `gtimeout 30`. This PR makes the deadline a small `_gs_bounded()` function instead. A function passing `"$@"` needs no word splitting, so it behaves the same in zsh, bash and sh. It also makes the failure branch print why it failed, so a signed-out or windowless Aside is no longer reported as "not running".

## Relationship to #2824

#2824 (@AntonioVitalic) diagnosed the same bug first and fixes the common case, zsh with Homebrew `gtimeout`. I'm opening this as an alternative because its `eval` form regresses stock macOS. The perl fallback string `perl -e alarm(shift);exec(@ARGV) 30` only works when it is word-split and never re-parsed, and `eval` re-parses it, so the probe hits `syntax error near unexpected token '('` in every shell. That includes bash users on a stock Mac who detect Aside correctly today (matrix below). Happy for this to be folded into #2824, or closed in its favour if it adopts the function form.

Fixes #2842.

## Live evidence

macOS 26.6.2, zsh 5.9, Aside CLI 1.26.906.1630, Aside signed in.

**The bug, reproduced:**

```
$ zsh <probe from origin/main>
ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING

$ zsh -c '_T="gtimeout 30"; $_T aside --version'
zsh:1: command not found: gtimeout 30
```

**The fix:**

```
$ zsh  <patched probe>   ->  READY: aside 1.26.906.1630
$ bash <patched probe>   ->  READY: aside 1.26.906.1630
$ sh   <patched probe>   ->  READY: aside 1.26.906.1630
```

**All three probes on a stock-macOS PATH** (`/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` plus `~/.local/bin`: no `gtimeout`, no `timeout`, only `/usr/bin/perl`), plus the Homebrew case. #2824 was rebuilt by hand from its diff, not run from its branch:

| Probe | zsh + Homebrew | zsh, stock | bash, stock |
|---|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` | ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING | ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING | READY |
| #2824 (`eval`) | READY | ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING | ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING |
| this PR | READY | READY | READY (sh too) |

What `grep -q` hides on #2824's stock-macOS path:

```
$ env PATH=<stock> bash -c '_T="perl -e alarm(shift);exec(@ARGV) 30"; eval "${_T:+$_T }aside --version"'
bash: eval: line 0: syntax error near unexpected token `('
bash: eval: line 0: `perl -e alarm(shift);exec(@ARGV) 30 aside --version'
```

The perl deadline inside the function really fires:

```
$ perl -e 'alarm(shift); exec(@ARGV)' 2 sleep 10
exit=142 after 2s
```

**The new diagnostic**, captured live while the Aside profile was signed out. `grep -q` used to throw this away, although rule 2 already told agents to quote it:

```
ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING
PROBE_OUTPUT: No browser window is open for account u0 ("Profile 0"). Open a window in that Aside profile and retry, or pick another account with --account.
```

**Tests:**

```
$ bun test test/aside-driver.test.ts test/third-party-actions.test.ts

$ bun test test/parity-baseline-integrity.test.ts test/parity-sectioned.test.ts test/catalog-budget.test.ts test/context-budget-ratchet.test.ts

```

## Scope

- **Changed:** `scripts/resolvers/aside.ts` (the probe and the `ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING` guidance); `test/aside-driver.test.ts` (it asserted the buggy strings verbatim, which is how the bug survived; it now asserts the function form and guards against the string form coming back); 20 SKILL.md files regenerated with `bun run gen:skill-docs`; the three ship goldens, updated only in the probe block because no script regenerates them.
- **Verified live by:** running the rendered probe from `browse/SKILL.md` under zsh, bash and sh against a real, signed-in Aside, on both the Homebrew PATH and a stock-macOS PATH, then driving a real page through `aside repl`.
- **Did NOT test:** the Linux `timeout` branch (no Linux machine; it has the same shape as the `gtimeout` branch), Windows, or the paid evals. The full free suite shows 17 failures in 8 files. None of those files reference the resolver or the generated docs, and two of them, re-run on a clean `origin/main` tree, failed the same way.

## Why (in your own words)

Today `/cso` can describe security risks, but it cannot reliably prove that a vulnerability is reachable, that a proposed repair fixes the same assertion, or that the finding stays closed against current source. This release adds a fail-closed local evidence pipeline: capture the real source safely, distinguish supported findings from hypotheses and coverage gaps, reproduce candidates only in qualified containment, issue replayable repair bundles, and recheck closure from a fresh snapshot.

## Live evidence

I ran the compiled helper against a local vulnerable Node fixture containing a query parameter concatenated into SQL:

```text
$ bin/gstack-cso-launcher start --repo <local-node-fixture> --code --offline --budget 300
$ bin/gstack-cso-launcher submit <run-id> <evidence.json>
$ bin/gstack-cso-launcher finish <run-id>

{
  "status": "finished",
  "completeness": "complete",
  "findingCount": 1,
  "finding": {
    "severity": "high",
    "confidence": "high",
    "evidence": "supported",
    "reproduction": "not_attempted",
    "repair": "not_attempted",
    "closure": "open",
    "title": "Query parameter is concatenated into a SQL statement"

}

title: fix(browse): state save|load carries localStorage, so a saved login restores
body:
## Why (in your own words)

`browse state save <name>` saves cookies and URLs but not localStorage. That makes it useless for the auth it looks like it handles: Supabase, Firebase and most SPA auth keep the session in localStorage, not in a cookie. So `state load` replays hundreds of cookies, prints a success line, and hands back a **signed-out** browser. Nothing errors.

I hit this during real work tonight. A saved operator session wouldn't restore, and the symptom — landing on `/auth` — looks exactly like an expired token, so I went down the wrong path twice: first "the state file is stale, re-save it" (re-saved from a live signed-in daemon, same result), then "a stuck Chromium is holding the profile, kill it and sign in again". The second one was about to throw away a *working* signed-in browser to fix a save that was never going to work. The actual cause only showed up when I dumped the file and found no `origins` key at all.

The omission was deliberate, behind `// V1: cookies + URLs only (not localStorage — breaks on load-before-navigate)`. That reasoning is stale: `BrowserManager.restoreState` navigates each tab to its saved URL **first** and applies storage after, so there's no load-before-navigate window. The sibling persistence path (`session-persist.ts`, #778) already persists per-tab storage through that same restore. Only the manual named-state path was left behind.

## Live evidence

**Before — the file has no storage at all:**

```

title: fix(browse): Aside readiness probe fails under zsh and discards its own error output
body:
## What's broken

The `{{ASIDE_SETUP}}` readiness probe reports `ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING` for a healthy, signed-in Aside. Two independent defects, both in the probe's bash block.

**1. The timeout prefix is not word-split under zsh.**

```bash
_T=""; command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1 && _T="gtimeout 30"
...
elif $_T aside repl 'console.log("ASIDE_READY " + pwd)' 2>&1 | grep -q '^ASIDE_READY'; then
```

bash splits unquoted `$_T` into `gtimeout` + `30`. zsh does not word-split unquoted parameters, so it tries to exec a command literally named `gtimeout 30` and fails with "command not found". Any harness running skill blocks under zsh on macOS hits this every time.

**2. The probe discards the evidence it tells you to quote.**

`2>&1 | grep -q` throws the output away, so every failure collapses into `ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING` regardless of cause. Step 2 then instructs the agent to "quote the probe output verbatim", which is impossible, because it was already discarded.

The two compound. The zsh failure is invisible, so a running Aside looks like a closed app and the skill falls through to the `$B` fallback engine: a lower-fidelity driver with no real sessions and no extensions. The degradation is silent and easy to miss.

## What changed

- Bind the deadline through a function applied to `"$@"` instead of an unquoted variable prefix. Splits correctly in bash and zsh. The chain is unchanged: gtimeout, then timeout, then perl alarm.
- Capture the probe output, match against it, and print it under `PROBE_OUTPUT:` on failure, capped at 5 lines.
- Step 2 now says how to read that output. Aside's own "isn't running on this machine" means the app is closed and should be opened. A permission, sandbox, or helper/signing error means Aside is healthy and the shell could not reach it, so opening the app will not help.

`{{ASIDE_RESEARCH}}` lifts the probe from `{{ASIDE_SETUP}}` at render time, so one edit corrects both copies.

## Verification

Same machine, same shell (`/bin/zsh`), Aside 1.26.906.1630 running and signed in:

- before: `ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING`
- after: `READY: aside 1.26.906.1630`

In a shell that genuinely cannot reach Aside, the new probe prints the real cause under `PROBE_OUTPUT:` instead of a misleading one.

## Note on the test change

`test/aside-driver.test.ts` asserted the literal strings `_T="gtimeout 30"`, `_T="timeout 30"` and `_T="perl -e ..."`. Those pinned the exact syntax the bug lived in, so a correct probe failed them while the broken one passed. I repinned them to the behaviour the surrounding comment says they were meant to protect (the ordered deadline chain), added a regression guard that fails if any unquoted variable is used as a command prefix before `aside repl`, and pinned that a failed probe keeps its output.

Commits are split per the bisect convention: source fix, test repin, then generated output (`bun run gen:skill-docs`; 20 SKILL.md plus the 3 ship goldens, no hand edits).

## CI expectations

This is a fork PR, so the eval and E2E lanes will fail with empty-env auth rather than on the change itself. Per CONTRIBUTING that is expected for fork PRs; free-tests, check-freshness, workflow-lint and windows-tests still give real signal.

Local results:

- `test/aside-driver.test.ts` + `test/host-config.test.ts`: 105 pass, 0 fail.
- `test/gstack-design-detect.test.ts`: 3 failing, pre-existing. Verified by stashing this branch's changes and re-running at a clean HEAD: identical 62 pass / 3 fail. They are realpath (`/private/var` vs `/var`) and mirror-download assertions, untouched by this change.
- `test/parity-suite.test.ts`: unverified. The free runner killed its shard at the 460s wall-clock deadline and reported it TIMED-OUT rather than failed, still in flight at the kill. Flagging it rather than claiming it passes.

title: OSV Scanner failing on main: sharp and adm-zip overrides have fallen behind published fixes
body:
The weekly OSV Scanner run on `main` has been failing since 2026-09-14 ([run 34819144240](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/34819144240)). The 2026-09-07 run was green, so this is fresh.

Two advisories, both in packages that reach the tree only through `package.json` `overrides`:

| Package | Pinned | Advisory | Severity | Fixed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sharp` | `0.35.0` (exact) | GHSA-rgj7-g3m4-5g8c, bundled libheif RCE | 8.9 HIGH | 0.35.4 |
| `adm-zip` | `^0.6.0` | GHSA-vwc7-r8mq-g2x9 / CVE-2026-76845, symlink-follow on extract lets a crafted archive overwrite files outside the target directory | 6.8 MEDIUM | 0.6.1 |

One detail worth flagging, because the scan output actively misleads here: the `adm-zip` advisory records a `last_affected` event rather than a `fixed` event, so the scanner table prints `FIXED VERSION = --` and the summary reads as though the finding is unfixable. It is not. 0.6.1 is published and sits outside the affected range; `POST https://api.osv.dev/v1/query` against `adm-zip@0.6.1` returns zero vulns, as it does for `sharp@0.35.4`.

### Real exposure is low, but that is not the interesting part

The only `sharp` consumer is `browse/src/screenshot-size-guard.ts`, which downscales full-page PNG screenshots and never decodes the AVIF or HEIF paths the libheif advisory covers. Nothing in the tree imports `adm-zip` at all; it arrives via `onnxruntime-node` under `@huggingface/transformers`. Both fixes are a one-line version change, so exposure was never the deciding question.

### The recurring problem

An exact pin is the one dependency shape that cannot drift forward on its own. Dependabot will not move `sharp: "0.35.0"`, and `dependency-review.yml` only inspects newly *added* dependencies at PR time. So an aging pin stays invisible until a weekly cron turns red days later, and a weekly cron that only goes red is a signal nobody is subscribed to.

`.osv-scanner.toml` already solved the mirror-image problem: every `[[IgnoredVulns]]` entry carries an `ignoreUntil`, which forces re-justification. Nothing applied that discipline to the `overrides` block.

### Proposed fix

PR incoming. Three parts:

1. Bump `sharp` to 0.35.4 and `adm-zip` to 0.6.1.
2. Add `.override-pins.json` (a reason and a `reviewBy` date per override) plus `test/override-freshness.test.ts` in the free suite, so a stale pin fails on the PR rather than in a cron.
3. Have the OSV Scanner workflow open an issue on a failed scheduled run, guarded on `repository.has_issues` so forks with issues disabled skip the job.

title: v1.84.2.0 Fix OSV Scanner failures: bump sharp and adm-zip, expire override pins
body:
Closes #2866.

The weekly OSV Scanner run on `main` has been failing since 2026-09-14. Two advisories, both in packages that reach the tree only through `package.json` `overrides`, both already fixed upstream.

## What changed

**`sharp` 0.35.0 to 0.35.4** clears GHSA-rgj7-g3m4-5g8c (bundled libheif RCE, CVSS 8.9). **`adm-zip` 0.6.0 to 0.6.1** clears GHSA-vwc7-r8mq-g2x9 / CVE-2026-76845 (symlink-follow on extract). `POST https://api.osv.dev/v1/query` returns zero vulns for both new versions.

The `adm-zip` advisory records `last_affected` rather than a `fixed` event, so the scanner table prints `FIXED VERSION = --` and reads as though the finding is unfixable. It is not; 0.6.1 is published and outside the affected range.

**`.override-pins.json` + `test/override-freshness.test.ts`** give the `overrides` block the discipline `.osv-scanner.toml` already applies to suppressions. An exact pin is the one dependency shape that cannot drift forward on its own: Dependabot will not move `sharp: "0.35.0"`, and `dependency-review.yml` only inspects newly *added* dependencies at PR time. So each override now carries a reason and a `reviewBy` date, and the free suite fails when a pin has no rationale, when a rationale outlives its override, when a `reviewBy` has passed, or when an exact pin no longer matches what the lockfile resolved. That moves the signal from an unwatched weekly cron to a gate a reviewer is already reading.

**`osv-scanner.yml`** opens an issue on a failed scheduled run, or comments on the open one, guarded on `repository.has_issues` so forks with issues disabled skip the job rather than erroring.

## Exposure

Low, and deliberately not the deciding factor. The only `sharp` consumer is `browse/src/screenshot-size-guard.ts`, which downscales full-page PNG screenshots and never decodes the AVIF or HEIF paths the libheif advisory covers. Nothing imports `adm-zip` directly; it arrives via `onnxruntime-node` under `@huggingface/transformers`. Both fixes are a one-line version change, so there was no reason to weigh exposure against cost.

## Verification

`bun install` relocks cleanly, and the lockfile diff is scoped to `sharp`, `adm-zip`, and the `@img/sharp-*` platform packages. `test/deps-smoke.test.ts` (sharp import, `metadata()`, resize round-trip), `test/override-freshness.test.ts`, and `test/osv-config-wiring.test.ts` pass: 11 tests, 32 assertions.

On the full free suite, honest reporting: it is not green in my container, and it is not green on the base commit either. Base `71f6048e` fails 52 tests, this branch fails 46, and diffing the two failure sets leaves exactly one branch-only entry, a PTY WebSocket test in `browse/test/terminal-agent-integration.test.ts` that passes 3 of 3 in isolation on the branch and 2 of 2 on base. It is flake under shard load, not a regression. The shared baseline failures are environmental (no `file` binary for the compiled-binary check, `~/.gstack` home state, TMPDIR-sensitive path-traversal tests), so CI should be the authority on suite health here rather than my numbers.

VERSION is bumped to 1.84.2.0 with a CHANGELOG entry. Commits are bisected: the dependency bump, the freshness gate, the workflow change, and the release notes are each independently revertable.
