Updates `playwright` from 1.62.1 to 1.63.0
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.63.0

🔒 Test locks

Tests that access a shared resource — an external service, a global account setting — can now declare a named lock. Tests that share a lock name never run concurrently, across files, workers and projects, while everything else keeps running in parallel:

test('update user settings', { lock: 'user-settings' }, async ({ page }) => {
  // never runs at the same time as other tests holding 'user-settings'
});

A test can hold multiple locks, and test.describe() accepts a lock for the whole group. Learn more about test locks.

🪟 Locate across frames

page.frameLocator() and frame.frameLocator() called without a selector search in any frame of the subtree, so you no longer need to locate the iframe first:

// Finds the button in any frame on the page.
await page.frameLocator().getByRole('button').click();

The rest of the locator resolves inside a single frame, just like a regular locator, and an error is thrown when it matches elements in several frames.

👁️ Visible-only locators

New locator.visible() returns a locator that matches only visible elements. It is the recommended replacement for the :visible CSS pseudo-class:

await page.locator('button').visible().click();

🧾 Step params and subtitles

Steps now carry structured data for reporters. Playwright API steps report the target locator and call arguments, and test.step() accepts subtitle and params options for your own steps:

await test.step('Login', async () => {
  // ...
}, { subtitle: 'as admin', params: { user: 'admin' } });

Reporters receive them via testStep.subtitle and testStep.params. For Playwright API

title: v1.87.1.0 fix: update vulnerable sharp and adm-zip overrides
body:
Addresses #2866. Adapts the dependency-only fix from #2867 onto current main. Contributed by @smsmatt; the override-expiry ledger and scheduled-scan notification proposal remain in that PR.

Update `sharp` to 0.35.4 and `adm-zip` to 0.6.1, including their resolved platform packages, without adding vulnerability exceptions or changing the pinned evaluation harness. Regression tests enforce the fixed version floors, load Sharp, and verify that ordinary archive extraction works while file and directory destination-symlink escapes are rejected.

## Verification

- Before: OSV-Scanner 2.3.8 reports `GHSA-rgj7-g3m4-5g8c` and `GHSA-vwc7-r8mq-g2x9`, exit 1. The new regression file has 1 pass and 5 failures with the original lockfile, including both symlink escape cases.
- After: the same scanner checks both lockfiles with the existing `.osv-scanner.toml`, exit 0 with no unsuppressed findings. Three applicable existing exceptions remain; this is not a claim of zero vulnerabilities without exceptions.
- Frozen install and build pass. Final local dependency-security, dependency-smoke, OSV-wiring, and screenshot-guard run: **19 pass, 0 fail, 52 assertions**. Symlink cases intentionally skip Windows.
- An independent reviewer checked all 28 changed package records against published npm metadata and exercised ONNX's actual archive-extraction API. Native-context review and the final parent diff review found no unresolved introduced defects. External Claude/Codex CLI review was unavailable.
- The full local free suite was attempted, not passed: 31 failures across nine unrelated files. An isolated eight-file comparison on unchanged main and this patch gives identical results: 306 pass, seven failures, 1,050 assertions; watchdog passed on both reruns. Git remote rewriting, forced fixture authorship, and live GitHub authentication affect this environment. Full-suite validation relies on CI.
- Local paid evals were blocked by the missing Claude CLI; the dependency-only diff selector found no affected model cases.

Owner liveness exemption verified. No compiled binaries, workflow changes, or suppression changes are included.

## Documentation

- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: documents the focused dependency-security regression command, fixed-version/runtime and ZIP-extraction checks, Windows symlink-test skips, and the unchanged OSV exception policy.

title: v1.87.2.0 fix: preserve headed browsers during headless cleanup
body:
Fixes #2817.

A headless daemon could kill the PID in the shared headed profile's `SingletonLock`, closing another project's healthy browser. Scope profile cleanup to headed lifecycle paths: startup uses the effective headed setting, forced stop/disconnect use the recorded mode, and server shutdown uses the active browser manager. Headed startup retains stale-lock recovery.

The approved Windows CI follow-up gives only the real CSO USERPROFILE integration test a 120-second outer timeout, accommodating its existing subprocess budgets instead of Bun's five-second default. Assertions and subprocess limits are unchanged.

## Verification

- The nine-case regression suite starts a real headless daemon beside a controlled live process holding another project's profile locks. On unchanged main: **3 pass / 6 fail**; patched: **9 pass / 0 fail**. Headed startup controls use a stub daemon so they can inspect cleanup before Chromium reacquires the locks.
- Final local lifecycle, factory, watchdog, timeout-tripwire, and Windows build-contract run: **56 pass, 12 native-Windows skips, 0 fail, 193 assertions**. Native Windows execution belongs to CI, not the Linux run.
- Build passes; build/test evidence is fresh. No compiled outputs are committed.
- Independent native-context review and the final parent diff review found no unresolved introduced defects. The review identified an inherited production Chromium identity-capture limitation, documented below rather than silently expanding this patch. External Claude/Codex CLI review was unavailable.
- The full local free suite was attempted but not green; Git/authentication fixtures and timing failures prevent claiming a full-suite pass here. The affected lifecycle suites were rerun after fixes; full-suite validation relies on CI. Paid model evaluations were unavailable locally because the Claude CLI was missing.

## Scope limits

Headed-versus-headed shared-profile arbitration is unchanged. Tests with a supplied Chromium process identity verify identity-checked cleanup, **not production identity capture**: the existing Playwright `Browser.process()` assumption in `browser-manager.ts` remains unfixed. This PR prevents headless cleanup from touching another project's headed profile; it does not claim to repair that separate orphan-identification defect.

Owner liveness exemption verified.

## Documentation

- `BROWSER.md`: narrows both multi-workspace descriptions to headless isolation, preserves the shared headed-profile limitation, clarifies the `CHROMIUM_PROFILE` scope, and distinguishes identity-checked cleanup from the still-unfixed production identity capture.
- Documentation validation: 368 tests passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed; tracked generated docs are fresh and all ten host profiles generate successfully. Context-budget ceilings and parity tests passed.

### Documentation Debt

- How-to/tutorial: there is no dedicated two-project walkthrough for keeping a headed session open while another project starts and stops a headless daemon. Existing command references and the release entry cover the behavior; `/document-generate` can supply the walkthrough separately.
- Explanation/diagram: the existing `BROWSER.md` architecture diagram labels the daemon as stopping after 30 idle minutes without limiting that label to headless mode. Headed sessions are exempt. No component names moved or changed in this release.
- Contributor reference: `BROWSER.md` still describes Chromium as installed by `bun install` and suggests bare `bun test`; the contributor guide instead documents setup and the strict free-test runner. This pre-existing development-section drift needs a separate correction pass.
- Discoverability: existing CSO qualification/scanner, question-format, and gbrain write-surface references have no explicit Markdown-link path from README/AGENTS. The affected browser reference and internals are reachable.

Suggested label: `docs-debt`.

title: v1.87.3.0 fix: bind review evidence to the reviewed tree
body:
Fixes #2803.

Log-time stamping could certify edits made after a review, and the zero-commit fallback could certify the same unreviewed content even without a stamp. Add single-use review-start receipts scoped to the repository, branch, and review kind. A diff review gets a content binding only when its original start and finish fingerprints match and the reviewer reports a completed, converged pass. Completion remains reviewer-reported, not proof that a model read the code.

Use one computed freshness grade across logging, reading, ship readiness, and deploy readiness. Missing/legacy capture, incomplete or nonconverged passes, unresolved findings, and ship telemetry cannot certify a review; edits during or after the pass grade stale. Plan-file reviews retain their existing handling.

Wire the contract through standalone review, ship's review loop, native/outside adversarial passes, design-lite, and both Codex command paths. A Codex severity-gate pass with unresolved `findings` no longer grades CURRENT; the gate's existing severity policy is unchanged. Regenerate all host outputs and goldens without raising context ceilings.

## Verification

- Baseline scenarios falsely grade CURRENT for tracked/untracked mid-review edits, log-only results, and wholly or partially unresolved Codex findings. Patched scenarios grade STALE or UNVERIFIED. An actual completed, unchanged rerun restores CURRENT.
- Final parent regression run: **1,059 pass, 14 skips, 0 fail, 9,401 assertions across 25 files**, covering evidence, callers, installation, documentation, dependencies, timeout guards, release metadata, and browser isolation. Skips are 12 native-Windows cases plus missing-Claude and missing-zsh checks. The independent reviewer reproduced the two new unresolved-Codex failures before applying the correction; all four resolution-count cases now pass without changing the gate verdict.
- Slim-runtime tests execute start/log/read from all five host roots in both symlink and copy layouts. The shared library is available in all ten installations.
- Build, all-host generated freshness, shell syntax, all 21 parity invariants, and `git diff --check` pass. The completed parent re-review is bound to unchanged content and reads CURRENT.
- The full local free suite was attempted, not passed. Remaining Git/auth fixture failures matched the environment baseline; the CSO Git-pointer race expectation was also reproduced on that untouched baseline. Full-suite validation relies on CI.
- External Claude/Codex CLI review and paid model evaluations were unavailable locally; an installed skill profile is not external-provider authentication.

No merge or deploy behavior is automated. No compiled outputs are committed. Owner liveness exemption verified.

## Documentation

- `README.md`: added `gstack-review-log` and `gstack-review-read` to the existing command table, including single-use scoped receipts, reviewer-reported completion, computed freshness grades, and a dashboard link.
- `docs/skills.md`: clarified CURRENT/STALE/UNVERIFIED, full re-review after fixes, unchanged plan-review handling, and why a Codex severity-gate PASS with unresolved findings cannot grade CURRENT.
- `docs/PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md`: added the shared `review-evidence.ts` library and its receipt-binding/computed-freshness responsibility to the existing project tree.

### Documentation Debt

- Review receipts have command reference and workflow instructions but no newcomer walkthrough covering start, fix, rerun, and final freshness (tutorial/how-to).
- The shared `lib/review-evidence.ts` flow has no dedicated contributor-facing architectural explanation or diagram (explanation). Existing diagrams have no branch-induced entity drift.
- `TODOS.md:493-501` still describes a paid staleness eval that "falls back on mismatch"; its future specification needs the computed-grade/no-HEAD-fallback contract (reference). The paid eval itself remains unfinished.
- The existing depth-two documentation inventory has 80 of 116 files without a strict Markdown-hyperlink path from README or AGENTS, including runtime-discovered skills and referenced checklists. No new orphan document was introduced; a navigation pass should distinguish intentional runtime discovery from missing reader links (reference).

Suggested follow-up: `/document-generate` for the missing walkthrough and architecture explanation; consider the `docs-debt` label.

title: v1.87.4.0 fix: preserve health failures and disclose coverage
body:
## Summary

`/health` could turn a failed checker into a successful result by reading the exit status of `tail`, and count only the displayed output. Capture the complete log privately, preserve the checker status under `set -e`, and parse before displaying its final 50 lines. Capture failures remain explicit errors; executed commands returning 127 remain failures.

Scores now display checked and unavailable categories. Empty runs report `N/A — no checks ran` without appending numeric history, and trend comparisons require identical coverage. Scoring weights and numeric history format are preserved.

The routing evaluation now chooses among installed project skills. Free regression fixtures buffer fragmented terminal input and keep captured permission menus within the terminal width, preserving their behavioral assertions.

## Validation

Final revision: `e966a8db5ddd4493a97a7d6eb8ea3ab7b967ecc4`, based on `origin/main` at `85b8c038fc0002a1549789ea018e924c1d335de4`.

- Full free suite: **14,623 passed, 54 skipped, zero failures**, all 850 files, 346 seconds. No unhandled/module errors; complete logs and successful process cleanup verified.
- Final build, skill validation and all-host generation/freshness passed. Tracked working tree is clean and test evidence is FRESH.
- Focused checks covered full-output capture, exit status, private-log cleanup, zero/partial coverage, history, selection, generated content, release metadata and the repaired terminal fixtures.
- Credential scan: zero high findings; four medium matches were release-version strings misidentified as IP addresses.

## Paid evaluations and accepted coverage exception

**11 logical tests passed:** health reporting at `e69c15cd`, plus ten routing cases at `79253538`. These results are retained because their consumed inputs remain unchanged. Recorded cost of the retained passing results: $1.56. The original routing failure was repaired and passed a fresh run; earlier attempts remain in the evidence records.

The selector includes 17 keys representing 18 logical tests. The following six additional keys represent **seven planning tests intentionally unrun under the accepted coverage exception**:

- `plan-ceo-finding-count`: five-finding and paired-finding cases
- `plan-eng-finding-count`
- `plan-design-finding-count`
- `plan-devex-finding-count`
- `plan-eng-multi-finding-batching`

They are selected by changes to three free-test files that the paid entrypoints do not import. Their production runner, skill prompts, fixture data, model parameters and assertions are unchanged. This source comparison is not a passing evaluation. No quality judges are selected.

## Review and scope

Native review cleared the health/release/routing changes and the three final free-test repairs. Outside Claude review covered the unchanged health implementation at `e69c15cd`; the supported changelog-style finding was fixed and reviewed natively. No outside review is claimed for the later free-fixture repairs.

This is the complete health portion of the roadmap, including a bounded live evaluation for failure, partial coverage and zero tools. Generation infrastructure, Codex evaluations and CEO/review-workflow work remain preserved on the local `nouakchott` branch for separate PRs. The broader roadmap is not represented as complete.

## Documentation
Existing documentation remains accurate for the health reporting changes; no additional files changed. The skill and v1.87.4.0 release entry explain preserved checker failures, full-output counts, partial coverage, unscored empty/capture-error runs, and comparable trends. No architecture diagram drift identified.

### Documentation Debt
Existing /health standalone coverage is reference-only: docs/skills.md links to #health without a corresponding section. A future how-to/tutorial can explain configuration and interpreting coverage; deferred to preserve the accepted release scope.

Windows free tests, the live UI-positive eval, and fail-closed report reconciliation all passed on this head. ## Test execution - Wake plan-count observers on output/exit, settle new output bursts for 250ms before reading split redraws, and preserve the 2s silent fallback, real CLI's 8s startup grace, input debounces, and permission guards. This is one observed planner result; end-to-end workflow savings are not yet measured. ## Measured file-level performance Same Linux machine, Bun 1.4.0. These measurements were taken at `b7539a1`, including output-burst settling; subsequent correctness fixes were validated separately. Polyfill/daemon values are three-run medians on both sides; PTY baselines are single observed runs and final values are three-run medians. These are individual-file timings, not whole-suite wall-time savings. | Test file | Before | Final | |---|---:|---:| | `browse/test/bun-polyfill.test.ts` | 17.30s | 1.29s | | `design/test/daemon-discovery.test.ts` | 17.78s | 11.99s | | `test/plan-count-file-permission.test.ts` | 97.05s | 30.92s | | `test/plan-count-checkbox.test.ts` | 40.9s | 15.46s | | `test/plan-count-completion.test.ts` | 36.6s | 13.91s | All 41 selected PTY tests passed on each of three repetitions; the permission suite retains all 115 assertions. ## Validation fixes - Seed the UI-positive design-review eval with the literal fixture in an isolated repository before invocation, explicitly name `PLAN.md`, and require an answered native design-review question. ## Summary
- Release gstack v1.87.6.0 / package v1.87.6.

CEO reviews now process completed native and external findings through one approval flow, reserve cross-model comparison for external reviews, and give decisions explicit return points. Clarify Eng scope, framework, and test-review decisions.
- Correct Codex discovery when the test environment changes PATH, preserve opaque Windows/UNC hook arguments and captured replay paths, and fix CSO subprocess deadlines.
- Prefer installed PowerShell 7 for bounded Windows daemon identity queries, retaining the legacy fallback and single-query failure behavior. Bind the board deadline assertion to its admission clock.

- Bound source-audit reports while retaining all five questions and the original model, timeout, and retry settings.

CEO approvals distinguish settled scope deferrals from unresolved policy choices and keep strategy-only output at the requested depth.

The PR manifest names selected checks and deferred broad coverage separately. Unknown runtime changes restore the broad gate; this infrastructure-heavy PR uses that fallback. Dynamic agent cases and the other 11 judge cases remain fresh. Reused scores retain their original run, revision and expiry, and failed or retried attempts cannot publish reusable passes.

Timing targets are under one minute for quick edit feedback, 3–5 minutes for typical PR checks, and 60–90 seconds for complete free test execution across isolated CI runners, excluding setup and queue time. The full local suite remains slower at six workers.

its own comment claiming the opposite:

```
# ---- USER ADDITIONS BELOW ---- (survives re-init; above is managed)
```

That line is false. `cat > "$GSTACK_HOME/.brain-allowlist" <<'EOF'` truncates the
file before the heredoc body is written, so any line a user appended below that
marker on a prior run is gone the moment `gstack-artifacts-init` is re-run — no
error, no warning, no diff shown.

### Where

At commit `a6b3a57512ca6d5c6aa5b68f74f736195021f96e`:

- `bin/gstack-artifacts-init:280` — `cat > "$GSTACK_HOME/.brain-allowlist" <<'EOF'`
  (the truncating open; no prior read/merge of the existing file happens anywhere
  before this)
- `bin/gstack-artifacts-init:325` — the heredoc's last emitted line, the
  `USER ADDITIONS BELOW … survives re-init` comment, which the truncation above
  makes false for anything that was already below it

### The doc invites exactly the sequence that loses data

`docs/gbrain-sync.md:28-29`:

> The exact allowlist lives in `~/.gstack/.brain-allowlist`. The CLI manages
> it; you can append your own entries below the marker line.

`docs/gbrain-sync.md:192`:

> Re-init anytime with `gstack-artifacts-init`.

Both statements are true in isolation and false together: appending below the
marker is the documented, sole supported way to add a custom sync path (no
`.local`/`.d` override variant exists, and no `gstack-config` key covers the
allowlist), and re-init is documented as safe to run "anytime." Running the
second destroys the effect of the first.

### Minimal reproduction

```bash
gstack-artifacts-init                       # writes the canonical file + marker
echo 'projects/*/checkpoints/*.md' >> ~/.gstack/.brain-allowlist   # user addition, below the marker
grep -c 'checkpoints' ~/.gstack/.brain-allowlist   # 1

gstack-artifacts-init                       # re-init, per docs, "anytime"
grep -c 'checkpoints' ~/.gstack/.brain-allowlist   # 0 — line is gone, no warning printed
```

### Expected behavior

One of:

1. `gstack-artifacts-init` reads the existing `.brain-allowlist` before writing,
   preserves any non-comment lines found below the `USER ADDITIONS BELOW` marker,
   and re-emits them after rewriting the managed section above the marker; or
2. If preserving user lines across re-init is out of scope, the tool should say so
   truthfully instead of printing a comment that claims the opposite, and should
   warn (or refuse without `--force`) when it is about to discard a non-empty
   user-additions section it can detect.

### Proposed fix

Before the truncating write, read the existing `$GSTACK_HOME/.brain-allowlist` (if
present), split it on the `# ---- USER ADDITIONS BELOW ----` marker, keep the text
found after that marker, and append it back after the heredoc emits the refreshed
managed section and its own fresh marker line. This makes the existing marker
comment literally true instead of aspirational, and needs no new config surface —
it only changes what the write step does with content that is already there.

### Why this is worth catching

There is no supported alternative route for a durable custom sync path: the one
consumer of this file (`bin/gstack-brain-sync`) reads exactly this one path, with
no override variant, so "append below the marker" is the only documented
mechanism — and it is precisely the mechanism this bug destroys on the next
re-init, silently.

title: gstack-cso 3.0.0: every run fails on Windows/NTFS — lease validation rejects inode numbers above 2^53
body:
Version: gstack 1.87.4.0, gstack-cso 3.0.0 (helper ABI 3), Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, NTFS.

Symptom
- `gstack-cso start` succeeds.
- The first mutating command after it (`inspect`) fails with
  `PERSISTENCE_FAILED: Run mutation lease decision changed before cleanup`.
- The stale lease left behind then makes later calls fail with
  `UNSAFE_PATH: Run mutation lease decision is malformed`, including a fresh `start` against the same repo.

Root cause
- `validateLeaseDecision` requires `Number.isSafeInteger(Number(decision.candidateIno))`, and the same for `candidateDev`.
- On NTFS, `stat().ino` is the 64-bit file reference number. Its top 16 bits are the MFT record's sequence number, which goes up by one each time the record is reused.
- The lease files are created and deleted on every mutation, so they keep landing in the same record. Its sequence number climbs past 32 quickly, and from then on every inode is larger than Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.
- Observed candidate inode: 12947848930353416 (sequence number 46).
- The decision is therefore rejected as malformed. `releaseKnownLease` reports that as "decision changed before cleanup".

Reproduction
Creating and deleting a file 300 times in the same directory, then reading `fs.statSync(f, {bigint: true}).ino`, gave 300 of 300 inodes above 2^53 on both C: and D: of this machine. Whether a given run survives depends on which MFT record the lease file happens to get.

Suggested fix
- Compare inodes and devices as strings or BigInt everywhere: `fs.statSync(path, { bigint: true })` and `String(stat.ino)`. Don't convert them to Number, and drop the `isSafeInteger` check on the stringified values.
- The same Number-based dev and ino comparisons also appear in `readOwner`, `recoveryJson`, `releaseKnownLease` and `publishLeasePhase`. With Number, adjacent odd and even file IDs collapse to the same value; for example, 12666373953642761 reads as ...760.

Workarounds tried (none viable)
- A different volume or a fresh NTFS VHD: the sequence numbers climb again.
- FAT/exFAT: no hard links.
- GSTACK_HOME: relocates the state but doesn't change the file system.

title: fix(redact): relocate ^-anchored spans so egress masking stops dropping whole files (#2912)
body:
## What

`locateSpan()` cannot relocate an `^`-anchored pattern, so `redactFindingSpans()` returns `null` and its caller drops the whole payload. This is the mechanism behind #2912.

## Why it happens

A finding's `col` points at the reported span — the capture group when the pattern has one — which sits *after* the start of the whole match. `locateSpan` resumed the scan two characters before that span:

```ts
re.lastIndex = Math.max(0, offset - 2);
const m = re.exec(input);
```

`env.kv` is `^`-anchored:

```ts
regex: /^[ \t]*(?:export[ \t]+)?[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*(?:KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|...)[ \t]*=[ \t]*['"]?([^\s'"]{8,})['"]?/
```

The only position its `^` can match is the line start, and that is already behind `lastIndex`. `exec` scans forward, never matches the line the finding came from, and `locateSpan` returns `-1`. `redactFindingSpans` then returns `null` — which, per its own contract, the caller must read as "drop the whole payload".

## The scope is wider than #2912 reports

#2912 frames this as a false positive on lines that *read* a key from the environment. The trigger is actually any `env.kv` match at all, so a file is dropped just as readily when the match is a **genuine** secret:

```ts
redactFindingSpans('DB_PASSWORD = "s3cr3t-Kx9mQ2vLp7Wn"', { repoVisibility: "private" })
// → null   (before this change)
```

That is the fourth case in the added test file. The practical effect is that the files most likely to contain credentials are the ones most likely to be withheld.

## The fix

Resume the scan at the line start so an anchored match is reachable, then walk matches and accept only the one whose span lands exactly at the reported offset.

Fail-closed behaviour is unchanged: when no match lands at that offset, `locateSpan` still returns `-1` and the payload is still dropped. The change makes a correct relocation possible; it does not make masking more permissive.

## Verification

| | `test/locate-span-anchored.test.ts` (new) | `test/redact-engine.test.ts` |
|---|---|---|
| before | 0 pass / 5 fail | 98 pass / 0 fail |
| after | **5 pass / 0 fail** | 98 pass / 0 fail |

Verified against `main` at v1.87.5.0.

`test/gstack-redact-cli.test.ts`, `test/telemetry.test.ts` and `test/redact-audit-log.test.ts` report an identical 124 pass / 37 fail both with and without this change — those 37 are pre-existing failures in my sandbox (they shell out through `execSync`) and are unrelated to it.

## Deliberately not addressed

The other half of #2912 — `env.kv` firing on `os.environ[` in the first place — is left alone. Tightening that validator trades against false negatives on real secrets, which felt like a maintainer's call rather than mine. This change stops the file loss either way, and the two are independent.

browse: stop terminal-agent processes leaking (owner identity, confirmed kills, sweep, state-file watch)
body: ## Why (in your own words) `browse` spawns one `bun run browse/src/terminal-agent.ts` per daemon, and the only handle on it is a single-slot PID record. That handle gets lost four ways — the daemon is SIGKILLed or crashes (shutdown never runs), the record is unlinked after a SIGTERM that did not land, the record cannot be written at all (a state dir on a cloud mount), or shutdown runs in the window between spawn and the agent writing its record — and a lost handle is an immortal agent. On my Mac 4,995 orphaned agents hit the 5,333 per-user process ceiling and every `fork()` on the box started failing (Claude Code's Bash tool, its sandbox, and Playwright's Chromium all died). Three days later it recurred as 4,952 *live* duplicates under one daemon whose state dir could never be written, so its watchdog respawned blind once a minute. v1.6x added `BROWSE_OWNER_PID` and an owner watchdog in the agent, but the CLI's `connect` and supervisor sites never pass `ownerPid` (`BROWSE_OWNER_PID=undefined`, so the watchdog never arms for CLI-spawned agents), and the other loss modes remained. This PR gives every agent an explicit owner (argv marker + env + record field), writes the record at spawn, confirms kills before unlinking, sweeps dead-owner and duplicate agents at spawn, reaps a half-started daemon on startup timeout, makes the watchdog remember its own agent in memory and refuse to adopt someone else's, and has every daemon watch its own `browse.json` so an unreachable daemon exits instead of living (and spawning) forever. `BROWSE_NO_TERMINAL_AGENT=1` opts out entirely for CLI-only use. Note for reviewers: `ppid == 1` is **not** an orphan signal for agents — the CLI spawns the agent and then exits, so a healthy CLI-spawned agent is always reparented to launchd. The sweep keys on the `--owner-pid` marker, never on ppid (except for pre-marker legacy agents, as a one-time migration). ## Live evidence ``` # Environment: macOS, bun 1.3.13, branch fix/terminal-agent-leak on top of 35dd014 (v1.87.5.0), headless daemon run from source (bun run browse/src/cli.ts) in a scratch git project. # Fast timers for the demo only: GSTACK_AGENT_WATCHDOG_TICK_MS=3000 GSTACK_TERMINAL_OWNER_WATCHDOG_MS=2000 GSTACK_STATE_WATCH_MS=3000 ## A. watchdog-spawned agent carries --owner-pid and self-exits when its daemon is SIGKILLed $ bun run browse/src/cli.ts status [browse] Starting server... Status: healthy $ ps -ax -o pid=,ppid=,args= | grep terminal-agent.ts → [agent pid=55666 owner=55546; ] (daemon pid=55546) $ kill -9 55546 $ ps … (5s later) → [] (expected: none) ## B. a live agent whose owner is dead — one that even wrote the PID record with no owner (what pre-patch code writes) — is replaced, not adopted $ (plant) bun run terminal-agent.ts --owner-pid 999999 → [agent pid=55746 owner=999999; ] $ cat .gstack/terminal-agent-pid → {"pid":55746,"gen":"xduV6bv7ndVh6dhLsyompw","startedAt":1790057902233} $ bun run browse/src/cli.ts status daemon log: [browse] recorded terminal-agent PID 55746 is owned by PID 999999, not this daemon — replacing it|[browse] reaped stale terminal-agent(s): 55746|[browse] terminal-agent respawned by watchdog (PID: 55794)| $ ps … (6s later) → [agent pid=55794 owner=55764; ] (expected: exactly one, owner=55764) ## C. state-file ownership watch: a daemon whose browse.json names another live PID exits and leaves that file alone $ jq '.pid=55821' browse.json # simulate a newer daemon owning the state dir daemon 55764 alive after 11s: no; browse.json pid now: 55821 (dummy=55821) daemon log: [browse] state dir is now owned by PID 55821 — leaving its state/agent files alone|[browse] state file owned by PID 55821 — this daemon (PID 55764) is unreachable, shutting down| $ ps … (agents after exit) → [] (expected: none) ## D. BROWSE_NO_TERMINAL_AGENT=1: no agent is spawned by connect or by the watchdog daemon 55908; after 8s (>2 ticks) → [] (expected: none) $ browse stop → scratch daemons left: 1 ``` `browse stop → scratch daemons left: 1` in D is the daemon still closing Chromium; it was gone a few seconds later (`leftover test procs: 0`). Before the fix (v1.60.1, same machine, `for i in 1 2 3; do browse connect; kill -9 ; done`) left three `terminal-agent.ts` processes at ppid 1 that never exited; with this branch the same loop leaves none within 5 s (section A), and a daemon that lost its record no longer accumulates agents (section B: the foreign agent is replaced, not adopted, and exactly one remains). Tests: `bun test browse/test/terminal-agent-orphan-reap.test.ts browse/test/terminal-agent-watchdog.test.ts browse/test/terminal-agent-pid-identity.test.ts browse/test/server-embedder-terminal-port.test.ts browse/test/cli-supervisor.test.ts browse/test/terminal-agent-integration.test.ts browse/test/sidebar-tabs.test.ts` → 73 pass, 0 fail on this branch. The new test file is pure (injected `ps` output, stubbed `process.kill`), plus static wiring tripwires. ## Scope - **Changed:** `browse/src/terminal-agent-control.ts` (owner marker, record at spawn, `killAgentAndConfirm`, `parseAgentRows`/`reapOrphanAgents`/`agentOwner`), `browse/src/terminal-agent.ts` (gen from env, superseded-before-bind exit, cleanup only when the record is ours), `browse/src/server.ts` (owner-checked watchdog + in-memory last PID + consecutive-failure trip, confirmed kill and ownership-aware shutdown, `BROWSE_NO_TERMINAL_AGENT`, state-file ownership watch), `browse/src/cli.ts` (`ownerPid` at both spawn sites, opt-out gate, `reapLateStarter` on startup timeout), tests. - **Verified live by:** the transcript above (macOS 15, bun 1.3.13, headless daemon from source), plus the same fix running for a day on a 1.60.1 install via a local patch: zero agents with the opt-out, one-per-daemon without it, machine at ~600 processes instead of 5,000+. - **Did NOT test:** Windows (the sweep and `agentOwner` are explicit no-ops there; `reapLateStarter` falls back to `browse.json` on the launcher path), headed mode with the sidebar terminal actually attached, Linux. ## Liveness proof (required for external contributors) ## Checklist - [x] Liveness screenshot attached (`GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface) or PR author is @garrytan (owner exemption) - [x] This is not a generated-file-only diff (I edited the source/template and regenerated) - [x] No ETHOS.md edits, and no changes to voice / founder perspective / YC references - [x] New public command / external service / host adapter has an accepted issue linked (or N/A) — N/A (no new command; two env tunables: `BROWSE_NO_TERMINAL_AGENT`, `GSTACK_STATE_WATCH_MS`) - [ ] Linked issue or reproduction: reproduction is in "Live evidence" above (no existing issue found for this leak)

title: land-and-deploy: poll CI checks every 60s instead of 10s
body:
## What

Adds `--interval 60` to the `gh pr checks --watch` call in Step 3 of `/land-and-deploy` (both `SKILL.md` and the `SKILL.md.tmpl` it is generated from).

## Why

`gh pr checks --watch` defaults to a **10 second** refresh interval:

```
-i, --interval int   Refresh interval in seconds in watch mode (default 10)
```

The skill budgets a 15-minute CI wait, so a single watch costs ~90 polls, and each poll is several GitHub API requests. That lands on the 5,000/hr **per-user** primary quota, which is shared across every credential the user has — so it competes with the rest of the toolchain rather than having its own budget.

I hit this on a machine running several concurrent agent sessions against one `gh` token: the quota drained, and unrelated tooling started failing with `API rate limit exceeded` while the watch loop kept polling.

CI runs here take minutes, not seconds, so a 60s interval costs nothing in practice and cuts the poll count 6x. `--fail-fast` still exits on the first check failure, so a red build is reported as promptly as the interval allows.

## Testing

Flag verified against `gh version 2.x` (`gh pr checks --help`). Docs-only change — no code paths affected.

title: v1.87.7.0 fix(redact-prepush): four paths where the hook exits 0 on a real credential
body:
## Why (in your own words)

`bin/gstack-redact-prepush` is the last thing standing between a working tree and a pushed
credential. On current `main` there are four ways to make it exit 0 with the secret going out
anyway. None of them needs an attacker — three are ordinary git usage and the fourth is a
consequence of the scanner's own slicing.

The first two are range-resolution bugs. `remotesExclusion()` already reasons about *which*
remote the push targets, but `defaultRemoteBranch()` kept asking `origin` regardless, and the two
together choose the scan range. On a repo where `HEAD == origin/main`, `git push publish HEAD:main`
to a second remote resolves a merge-base of `HEAD` against `origin/main`, which is `HEAD..HEAD` —
an empty diff. The whole tree ships to that remote with nothing scanned. Separately, the shape
check accepts any 40 plausible hex digits, so when git names a remote tip we do not have, the base
is *guessed*; when the guess yields an empty diff the hook concludes "nothing to scan" and allows,
while git is about to send whatever the real difference is. A guess that scanned nothing is not
evidence that there is nothing.

The other two come from `scanAddedLines()`. Its comment argues that overlap between slices is
unnecessary "because every pattern is single-line … a line boundary cannot bisect a detectable
secret". That is true of the **match** and false of the **proximity requirement**: five patterns in
`lib/redact-patterns.ts` carry a `nearRegex` and fire only when their qualifying label sits within
`nearWindow` characters — `aws.secret_key` (HIGH) needs `aws_secret_access_key` within 100,
`gcp.service_account` (HIGH) within 300. Put the label at the end of one slice and the secret at the
start of the next and the pattern never fires at all. The zero-width variant is the same hole
measured in the wrong unit: the engine strips zero-width characters before matching, so a budget
counted in raw bytes decides the seam using bytes the engine will never see, and invisible padding
can separate a label from its secret while their normalized distance stays a couple of characters.

Two adjacent defects in the same functions have to land with them. The fallback range used a
hardcoded SHA-1 empty-tree object id, which does not exist in a SHA-256 repository and hard-blocks
every legitimate first push of a new branch there — and the remote-scoping fix above makes that
fallback reachable more often, so it stops being cosmetic. And an over-budget single line (a
minified bundle, a one-line JSON blob) was handed to the engine whole, tripping
`engine.input_too_large`: blocked, which is safe, but blocked *without the content ever being
read*. That is the behavior that teaches an operator to reach for the skip switch, and the next
time the gate is right they skip anyway.

This is a follow-up to #2498, which you closed as absorbed by v1.67.0.0. Five of those six paths
are indeed closed on `main` today — `++`-prefixed lines, unparseable stdin, `diff.external`, the
shape check on both shas, and `localSha="0"`. My gate confirms all five still hold. These four are
the ones that survived, plus two the slicing introduced afterwards. The change is deliberately
targeted and leaves your architecture alone: `addedLinesFromNewCommits()` (#2592/#2573),
`remotesExclusion()`'s push-target scoping, and the 768 KiB slicing are all preserved.

## Live evidence

`test/redact-prepush-fail-open.sh` is new in this PR: 32 scenarios, each driving the real scanner
through real git repositories with synthetic credentials assembled at runtime from halves that
match nothing on their own. It defaults to the in-tree scanner and takes an optional path, so the
same gate runs against any build.

**Against the scanner on `main` (v1.87.5.0, `bin/gstack-redact-prepush` sha256
`f9c85d22cdd13803ebaaf8cfbe9aa2469524bc47b51367a6cdb41ae219e5f209`), the rows that differ:**

```
$ bash test/redact-prepush-fail-open.sh /path/to/main/bin/gstack-redact-prepush
12 push to a non-origin remote                   BLOCK(aws.access_key)      ALLOW                      FAIL
16 missing-but-shaped remote sha                 BLOCK(aws.access_key)      ALLOW                      FAIL
17 zero-width across slice boundary              BLOCK(aws.secret_key)      ALLOW                      FAIL
18 proximity split by slice cut                  BLOCK(aws.secret_key)      ALLOW                      FAIL
20 absent named tip, non-empty wrong guess       BLOCK(aws.access_key)      ALLOW                      FAIL
E5 URL push does not borrow origin's base        BLOCK(aws.access_key)      ALLOW                      FAIL
19 label at the end of an over-overlap line      BLOCK(aws.secret_key)      ALLOW                      FAIL
21 short line between label line and secret     BLOCK(aws.secret_key)      ALLOW                      FAIL
22 several short lines between them             BLOCK(aws.secret_key)      ALLOW                      FAIL
```

**Free suite.** The full local `bun run test` fails in `test/pty-screen.test.ts`,
`test/relink.test.ts` and the Chromium and compiled-CSO lanes — they need artifacts CI builds first
(`build:gates`, `build:cso`, `vendor:xterm`, the browse node server) which I did not build here, and
CONTRIBUTING notes dev boxes see flakes in that lane while the required CI free lane turns on its
retry pass. Following CLAUDE.md's blame protocol, I measured it rather than asserting it: the same
two files, same machine, runs serialized — `main` (35dd014c) **62 pass / 8 fail**, this branch
**62 pass / 8 fail**, and a `diff` of the sorted failing-test lists is identical. This branch
introduces none of them.

## What changed after review

A first version of this branch closed the four classes only partially, and your review process
should see that rather than discover it. An independent cross-family review found three shapes the
first version still let through with exit 0, and one gate row that could not have caught a broken
fix. All four are fixed in a separate commit so the delta is readable:

- **URL push (the most important one).** `pushRemote()` returns null for a URL, and
  `defaultRemoteBranch()` then fell back to `origin`; `remotesExclusion()` fell back to a bare
  `--remotes`. With the credential already on `origin/main` and a harmless local commit, a first
  push to a new empty URL remote anchored on origin, excluded everything origin had seen, scanned
  the harmless commit only, and shipped the credential. **My gate's E5 row asserted `ALLOW` for
  exactly that shape** — it encoded the hole as expected behaviour. The push target is now a
  three-way value (configured remote / URL / unknown): a URL anchors on nothing and excludes
  nothing; an unknown target (no argv, stdin or CLI) keeps the historical origin-shaped behaviour.
  E5 now expects the block, and E5b pins that a clean URL push is still allowed.
- **Absent tip, non-empty guess.** The first version blocked only when the guessed range was
  EMPTY. A stale tracking ref holding the credential plus one harmless commit gives a non-empty,
  credential-free guess, and it passed. An absent named tip now gets no local narrowing: the whole
  reachable history is scanned. That is slower on that rare path and affordable only because every
  scan is sliced under the engine's cap — which is exactly why the old code avoided it. A new branch
  (zero remote sha) is deliberately not treated this way, since git named no tip there and the
  tracking refs are not contradicted. Row 20.
- **Over-overlap line.** The inter-slice overlap carried whole lines, so a single line longer than
  16 KiB contributed nothing to the seam. A ~770 KB line ending in `aws_secret_access_key =`
  followed by the key never fired. The overlap now carries such a line's suffix. Row 19.
- **E8 could not discriminate.** It carried a credential, so a build that cannot resolve the
  SHA-256 fallback range still "blocked" — with a diff error instead of a finding. E8b is a clean
  SHA-256 first push that must be allowed, and `main` fails it.

A second review round found that my overlap fix was itself incomplete: it carried a long line's
suffix only when the tail was otherwise empty, so one short line between the long label line and
the secret landed in the tail first and the label was dropped again. The overlap is now filled from
the seam backwards to its exact budget, taking a partial line wherever a whole one no longer fits.
Rows 21 and 22 pin the one-short-line and several-short-lines forms; `main` fails both.

**One upstream test changes, and I want to be explicit about it because it reverses a choice you
made.** In `test/redact-prepush-scan-range.test.ts`, the S1 case "an unconfigured name (URL push)
also falls back rather than erroring" asserted `exit 0`. Its fixture merges a commit whose secret
was pushed only to a private `other` remote, then pushes to a URL whose claimed tip does not
contain it — so that push really delivers the secret to the URL. The S1 comment accepts this as
"falling back scans LESS than the narrowed form would, but never less than the hook historically
did". That trade is the same fail-open as E5. I kept the test's stated purpose — it still asserts
the hook does not error on an unconfigured name — and changed the outcome assertion to the block.
The updated test fails on `main` and passes here. If you would rather keep the historical leniency
for URL pushes, this is the one assertion to revert, and E5 goes with it.

**Why S1's URL case changes but its no-argv neighbour does not**, since the two share a fixture and
now carry opposite verdicts. The URL case is a real push: git hands the hook a destination, and that
destination is described by no tracking ref, so nothing may be excluded. The no-argv case is the
documented contract for invoking the hook without arguments — stdin or a direct CLI call, where no
destination exists at all — and real pushes always carry the name. There is nothing to protect
there, so it keeps the historical behaviour, and `pushTarget()` models it as its own `unknown` state
rather than as a URL.

## Known limitation, not addressed here

The hook scans the **net diff** of the range it computes, never each commit. A credential added in
one commit and removed in a later one within the same push is absent from that diff, so it is not
seen — yet git delivers both commits. I measured this on `main` and on this branch, across the three
push shapes that pick different ranges:

```
                                         main        this branch
new branch (zero remote sha)             ALLOW       ALLOW
absent named remote tip                  ALLOW       ALLOW
existing branch (remote tip present)     ALLOW       ALLOW
```

It is identical on both, including the ordinary existing-branch push, so this branch neither causes
nor widens it; it is a property of diff-based scanning. Closing it means scanning each commit's own
diff in the range, which changes the hook's cost profile on every push and deserves its own PR and
its own review rather than riding in on this one. The code comment on the absent-tip path now says
this plainly instead of claiming to scan "everything reachable".

## Scope

- **Changed:** `bin/gstack-redact-prepush` (`pushRemote()` added; `defaultRemoteBranch()` scoped to
  the push target and nullable; `unknownRemoteTipBase()` falls through on a null default;
  `addedLinesFor()` blocks when a guessed base scanned nothing; `emptyTree()` asks git for the
  object id; `SCAN_OVERLAP_BYTES` + `LINE_BUDGET_BYTES` + zero-width stripping on ingest +
  `sliceLongLine()` in `scanAddedLines()`, with finding dedup on `id+preview` because overlap
  deliberately re-scans the seam). New: `test/redact-prepush-fail-open.sh`,
  `test/redact-prepush-fail-open.test.ts`; the S1 URL-push assertion in `test/redact-prepush-scan-range.test.ts` (see above). `VERSION` → 1.87.7.0 and a `CHANGELOG.md` entry.
- **Verified live by:** the 32-scenario gate above, run against both the `main` scanner and this
  head; `bun run test`; `shellcheck --severity=error`; and a spawn-based bun test so the gate is
  part of the free suite rather than a script nobody runs.
- **Did NOT test:** a real `git push` to a real second remote over the network (the gate drives the
  hook's stdin protocol against local repositories instead, which is what the hook actually sees);
  Windows; a genuinely huge repository for wall-clock regression beyond the gate's fixtures.
- **Deliberately not ported:** streaming the diff instead of `spawnSync`, and a wall-clock budget.
  Both would mean rewriting `addedLinesFor()`/`addedLinesFromNewCommits()` and throwing away your
  range narrowing, and the remaining 64 MiB `maxBuffer` limit is fail-closed (`BLOCK(unscannable)`),
  not a hole. One thing stays open and I am not claiming otherwise: a **stale tracking ref** for the
  target remote. If local `<remote>/<branch>` survives a reset of the remote and the local commit
  is its descendant, the range is computed against that stale tip and the real content is not
  scanned. Fixing that honestly needs `git ls-remote` — a network call inside a pre-push hook —
  which is your call, not something to append here. Scenario 16 does not cover it: 16 is about a tip
  git named that we do not have, not a tip we have wrongly.

## Liveness proof (required for external contributors)

I have not attached a `GSTACK PR` screenshot, and I would rather say why than quietly skip the box.
This change was prepared with agent assistance on my own machine and under my own account, so an
image produced from that session would be me manufacturing the human-presence attestation the gate
exists to check. GitHub also has no API for attaching an image to a PR body — only drag-drop in the
web UI — so it is not something that session could have produced honestly anyway.

What I can give you is the provenance the template asks agents for:

```
$ gh api user --jq .login
lubosxyz
```

If you want the screenshot before reviewing, say so and I will add it myself in the web UI.

## Checklist

- [ ] Liveness screenshot attached (`GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface) or PR author is @garrytan (owner exemption) — **not attached; see the section above, `gh api user --jq .login` → `lubosxyz`, happy to add on request**

title: cookie-import-browser: add Dia (Chromium-based, identical v10 cookie layout)
body:
**What's missing**

`BROWSER_REGISTRY` in `browse/src/cookie-import-browser.ts` covers Comet, Chrome, Chromium, Arc, Brave and Edge. Dia (The Browser Company, same vendor as Arc) is not in it. On a machine where Dia holds every live session, this is what `/setup-browser-cookies` does:

```
$ browse cookie-import-browser
Cookie picker opened at http://127.0.0.1:32969/cookie-picker
Detected browsers: Chrome, Arc

$ browse cookie-import-browser dia --domain github.com
Unknown browser 'dia'. Supported: comet, perplexity, chrome, google-chrome, google-chrome-stable, chromium, arc, brave, edge
```

The picker then shows a near-empty domain list, because the two detected browsers are the ones the user stopped using. The reasonable conclusion from the outside is that cookie import is broken.

**Why it is a one-line fix**

Dia's on-disk layout is Chrome's. Verified against a real profile on macOS 15:

- profile root `~/Library/Application Support/Dia/User Data/`, profile `Default`
- cookie DB `Default/Cookies`, same schema (`host_key`, `encrypted_value`, `expires_utc` in 1601-epoch microseconds, `samesite`)
- Keychain service `Dia Safe Storage`
- `v10` payloads, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 over `saltysalt` at 1003 iterations, AES-128-CBC with a 16-space IV
- the plaintext carries the 32-byte domain-hash prefix that `decryptCookie()` already strips unconditionally

So the existing decryptor needs no change at all.

**Patch**

```ts
{ name: 'Dia',      dataDir: 'Dia/User Data/',             keychainService: 'Dia Safe Storage',            aliases: ['dia'] },
```

placed next to the Arc entry. Everything else derives from `BROWSER_REGISTRY` (detection, picker pills, alias resolution, the "Supported:" error), so no other code path is touched. The browser lists in `README.md`, `BROWSER.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/skills.md` need the name added.

With the entry in place, on the same machine:

```
$ browse cookie-import-browser
Detected browsers: Chrome, Arc, Dia

$ browse cookie-import-browser dia --domain github.com
Imported 6 cookies for github.com from dia

$ browse goto https://github.com/settings/profile
Navigated to https://github.com/settings/profile (200)   # authenticated
```

**Secondary, if you want it**

Every new Chromium fork costs a release. An opt-in override such as `BROWSE_COOKIE_DATA_DIR` plus `BROWSE_COOKIE_KEYCHAIN_SERVICE` would cover the next one without a code change. The "Hardcoded — NEVER interpolate user input into shell commands" constraint on the registry is the obvious objection, so this only works if the override is path-validated and passed as an argv element rather than through a shell. Happy to leave it out if that trade isn't worth it.

PR with the registry entry and the doc lines follows.

title: feat(browse): add Dia to the cookie-import browser registry
body: ## Why I run Dia as my daily browser, so every session I care about lives in Dia's profile. `/setup-browser-cookies` told me "Detected browsers: Chrome, Arc" and the picker listed almost nothing, because those two are the browsers I stopped using. From the outside that reads as "cookie import is broken", and I nearly wrote it off. Dia is Chromium and stores cookies exactly like Chrome, so it only needs a registry entry. Closes #2938. ## Live evidence **Before**, built from this branch's parent commit (v1.87.5.0): ``` $ ./browse/dist/browse cookie-import-browser Cookie picker opened at http://127.0.0.1:32969/cookie-picker Detected browsers: Chrome, Arc $ ./browse/dist/browse cookie-import-browser dia --domain github.com Unknown browser 'dia'. Supported: comet, perplexity, chrome, google-chrome, google-chrome-stable, chromium, arc, brave, edge ``` **After**, same machine, same binary rebuilt with the one-line entry: ``` $ ./browse/dist/browse cookie-import-browser Cookie picker opened at http://127.0.0.1:33620/cookie-picker Detected browsers: Chrome, Arc, Dia $ ./browse/dist/browse goto https://github.com Navigated to https://github.com (200) $ ./browse/dist/browse cookie-import-browser dia --domain github.com macOS is waiting for Keychain permission. Look for a dialog asking to allow access to "Dia Safe Storage". Imported 6 cookies for github.com from dia $ ./browse/dist/browse goto https://github.com/settings/profile Navigated to https://github.com/settings/profile (200) ``` The last step is the one that matters: `/settings/profile` redirects an anonymous session to the login page, and here it renders the signed-in settings page with my account name in the nav. The imported Dia session authenticates. Decryption needed no change. Dia writes `v10` payloads, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 over `saltysalt` at 1003 iterations, AES-128-CBC with a 16-space IV, and the 32-byte domain-hash prefix that `decryptCookie()` already strips unconditionally. ## Scope - **Changed:** one entry in `BROWSER_REGISTRY` (`browse/src/cookie-import-browser.ts`), plus the browser lists in `README.md`, `BROWSER.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/skills.md`. No `VERSION` or `CHANGELOG.md` edit, so the version gate stays out of it. - **Verified live by:** the before/after runs above against a real Dia profile on macOS 15, and `bun test test/skill-validation.test.ts test/setup-browser-hint.test.ts` (354 pass, 0 fail). - **Did NOT test:** Windows and Linux, since Dia is macOS-only today, which is why the entry carries no `linuxDataDir` or `windowsDataDir`. I also did not run the full `bun run test:free` suite to green: it has failures on my machine in `cso-*` and `plan-count-*`, and those same tests fail identically on an unmodified v1.87.5.0 checkout, so they are pre-existing here and untouched by this diff. ## Liveness proof (required for external contributors) `gh api user --jq .login` → `JonnyFi`. title: v1.88.1.0 fix: harden credential boundaries and owned state
body:
Seven bounded credential, process-lifecycle, and user-state repairs for `1.88.1.0` (`package.json`: `1.88.1`). Published head: `dc1614d4d1c8b8e9767647990ee690179e14c92b`, against `636175d`.

The final review's Unicode redaction blocker is repaired and has passing before/after regressions, including the actual compiled CSO reader and installed pre-push hook. **Fresh local acceptance and all required CI checks pass on this head: 55 successful, 0 failed, 0 pending, 2 workflow skips.** Earlier green CI at `babc610` remains historical evidence only. The maintainer merged this PR on 2026-09-23 as [`b9706f3`](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/commit/b9706f3635b6a545f46fae607ae9d6bcbfb69b91); its tree exactly matches the accepted head. No deployment was performed by this thread.

## Credential boundaries

- Mask the exact original spans detected through normalization, preserving neighboring text, repeated values, overlap, and marker-only/oversize refusal. Map each normalized UTF-16 unit to its original start and end so supplementary NFKC expansion cannot displace masking or silently skip an EOF finding. Compiled CSO reads retain sanitized readable source while withholding unmaskable payloads.
- Bind pre-push ranges to the actual destination name and effective URL, using fully qualified tracking refs. Handle missing advertised objects and SHA-256 empty trees conservatively, preserve normalized context across bounded windows, and admit each finding only in its owning core without invented anchors or duplicates. Installed-hook regressions cover the supplementary-expansion seam that previously allowed a detected HIGH credential through. Unscannable lines/context still fail closed at the existing 1 MiB cap.
- Exclude credential-shaped variables from broad CI-prefix admission into hermetic children, while preserving CI metadata, explicitly admitted provider authentication, and documented runner overrides. Exercise the actual session launcher rather than only a helper mock.

## Ownership and user state

- Bind terminal agents to the persistent browser daemon and its process generation. Require confirmed exit before replacement, retain uncertain children, bound failed respawns, and serialize publication/shutdown so an older generation cannot remove its successor's state. Native exit observation recognizes zombie/reaped processes without turning uncertain identity into permission to kill.
- Preserve exact CSO filesystem identities and nanosecond timestamps through lease acquisition, comparison, recovery, and release. Keep adjacent high IDs distinct and refuse ambiguous legacy state. Native NTFS tests exercise the compiled helper's repeated lease lifecycle.
- Resolve the selected settings symlink target consistently for locking, mutation, backup, and rollback, preserving links, modes, and unrelated settings. Refuse changed or invalid targets; permission-denied resolution retains exit 3 and unwinds temporary-file cleanup.
- Refresh managed artifact allowlist rules while preserving the user suffix byte-for-byte, including comments and a missing final newline. Refuse ambiguous markers or failed assembly instead of replacing user data.

## Attribution

These are maintainer integrations, not wholesale adoption of the contributor branches. The four source PRs were subsequently closed as superseded, with individualized thanks and immutable merge/implementation citations:

| Area | Contributor input | Integration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact redaction spans | @aclansley, #2929 | Diagnosis and anchored-span approach; exact-original-span implementation and normalization/fail-closed controls |
| Destination-aware pre-push scans | @lubosxyz, #2935 | Diagnostic source; independent implementation, not cherry-picked |
| Hermetic credentials | @ntdatt812, #2636 | Adapted credential-suffix screening at the shared environment boundary |
| Agent lifecycle | @saltydoctor, #2931 | Ownership and confirmed-exit design input; no broad process sweep |

Related: #2930, #2912, #2927, #2894, #2830, #2907. Post-merge dispositions: #2930, #2927, #2830, and #2907 are completed; #2912 and #2894 remain open for their unaddressed scope. Contributor PRs #2929, #2935, #2636, and #2931 are closed as superseded, not merged. See the post-merge follow-up comment for individual citations.

## Test coverage and local acceptance

Fresh, isolated acceptance at **dc1614d**: `bun run build`, generated-output cleanliness, then `xvfb-run -a bun run test` through the strict shard runner. **25,090 passed, 61 skipped, 0 failed, 0 module/unhandled errors; 192,185 assertions across 1,000 files.** Both shard, inner, Docker, container, and evidence-copy exits were verified as zero. Fresh build/test receipts bind to the exact frozen tree.

The no-network acceptance container uses the pinned CI image with the previously verified local-only Python-venv prerequisite layer: Bun 1.4.0, Node 22.20.0, Python 3.12.3, Xvfb, lock-matched dependencies, isolated Git fixtures, and no model credentials. The build and suite completed in about 14 minutes.

```text
F1 normalization → original spans → CSO/CLI/telemetry: exact-output and refusal controls
F2 destination → scan windows → real installed hook: destination, seam, and no-remote-mutation controls
F3 environment policy → actual child launcher: credential denial and intentional admissions
F4 owner generation → replacement/publication/shutdown: process, uncertainty, and takeover controls
F5 exact filesystem IDs → lease lifecycle/recovery: portable boundaries and native NTFS gate
F6 canonical settings target → mutation/rollback: links, modes, races, and cleanup controls
F7 managed prefix + preserved suffix → atomic re-init: exact bytes and failure preservation
```

The Unicode repair added eight engine/CLI cases plus actual compiled-reader and installed-hook cases. They reproduce **eight failures before repair** and pass afterward; the BMP invariant covers all 65,536 input units. Focused and adjacent runs passed **429 tests** before full acceptance. No existing assertion, timeout, detector threshold, or model budget was weakened.

Coverage percentage is **unmeasured**, not 100%. Four direct behavioral gaps remain disclosed: POSIX CLI startup-timeout cleanup, repeated failed-start watchdog cutoff, same-path external settings replacement, and defensive CSO uint64/metadata rejection boundaries. These are not demonstrated production defects; the watchdog cutoff remains a partial planned proof item.

Changed-text scanning reports **0 HIGH, 26 reviewed MEDIUM advisories, no oversize input**; advisories are version/dead-PID/synthetic fixture data. Error-level ShellCheck, shell syntax, the exact CI-pinned actionlint container, diff hygiene, and online version-queue checks pass. Critical dependency audit checked 256 packages with no critical findings; three lower-severity advisories remain.

## Performance comparison

Bun 1.4.0, hash-pinned baseline/repaired code, 48 adapter/correctness controls and 90 fresh-process timed samples across nine workloads. Median pre-push scan time rises **8.6%** on 8 MiB clean text, **10.9%** on 8 MiB with findings, and **20.1%** on normalization-heavy text; those cases have matching findings. The extra work preserves neighboring normalized context.

Dense redaction with byte-identical output improves **1000.5 → 163.2 ms (6.1× faster)**; median whole-process peak RSS rises **84.3 → 93.1 MiB**. Observed scan calls stay below 1 MiB. Separately, a boundary fixture improves from zero to 16 expected findings; that is corrected detection, not equivalent-work speedup. These synthetic shared-machine measurements are not production percentiles, a latency target, or scanner-only allocation measurements.

## Pre-landing review

The final review found one P1 UTF-16 mapping defect and three stale documentation statements. All are repaired in `dc1614d`. A fresh full-branch native adversarial pass found no remaining concrete FIXABLE or INVESTIGATE production findings; unchanged-tree review receipts are current. Adversarial fixture review was summary-only; the parent inspected and executed the regression tests.

External Claude Code review was unavailable because its CLI was unauthenticated. No dual-model review is claimed. Greptile triage found no comments. No visual frontend change is included.

## Required CI on dc1614d

- [x] Linux free-test shards and aggregate, generated-content, quality, workflow, version, and build gates.
- [x] Native macOS: 7 startup tests and 166 lifecycle/concurrent-shutdown/linked-settings tests passed, 0 failed.
- [x] Native Windows: 19 startup/NTFS high-ID lifecycle tests passed, 0 failed. Curated Windows passed across 652 files; Windows setup also passed. The quiet curation log does not retain separate pass/skip totals.
- [x] Existing CSO Docker gate: 5 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed. The unselected staged-stack and Node-producer journeys receive no coverage credit.
- [x] Authenticated run [35816517616](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/35816517616), attempt 1: all six slices and 36 planned shards reconciled successfully. Collectors record **85 executed + 14 exact-input reused = 99 passed, 0 failed**, with 99 attempt records and $21.59 reported cost. Direct PTY outcomes are separately accounted by the shard reconciliation; the formerly provider-blocked plan-devex file passed in 136 seconds. No workflow retry was needed.

Selection remains **77 E2E case IDs and 25 judge IDs** in full-fallback mode. **119 behaviors remain scheduled/release coverage**, not PR-pass credit. Fourteen eligible unchanged judge results were reused; 11 uncached judges ran under the maintainer's explicit approval. The entirely skipped routing (10 cases) and judge-recommendation (1 case) shards are periodic-tier placeholders, not gate passes. The two workflow-level skips are qualification/staging jobs. Local report-only reconciliation also passed, and CI merge commit `73a5eba3` has the exact same tree as `dc1614d`.

## Plan completion and limits

title: fix(browse): validate canonical upload targets
body: ## The bug `browse upload` checked the safe-directory boundary only for absolute paths. A relative symlink inside the project could therefore point outside the allowed directories, and Chromium would receive that outside file. This requires an authorized local upload; it is not a remote upload bypass. ## The fix Resolve every requested file to its canonical target and apply the existing read-path allowlist before resolving the input or delivering any file. Pass those checked paths to Playwright, so mixed uploads fail together while ordinary project/temp files and safe symlinks still work. The regression fixture exercises both upload selector paths against real Chromium, including relative and directory symlinks and no-delivery controls. ## Validation - Current `main` (`06ed920a`): pinned build and headed Chromium preflight passed; 321 focused tests passed, including 38 real upload controls. - Complete free suite: **25,540 pass, 0 fail, 59 skip** across 1,010 files; both shard logs retained, source unchanged. - PR-profile live actors: `browse-basic`, `browse-snapshot`, and `diagram-triplet` executed and passed with zero skips. The passing `browse/SKILL.md reference` judge is reused from a prior run after comparing its complete 17,809-byte request, model, and rubric byte-for-byte; it was not resampled. - Complete staged diff: credential scan **0 high, 0 advisory**; independent pre-PR review found no actionable defect. Native macOS and Windows upload behavior is not claimed by these Linux checks. Like the existing file-read policy, validation does not defend against another local process replacing the canonical file after the check and before Playwright opens it.

title: fix(gbrain): classify structured PGLite busy response
body: ## The bug When PGLite is already owned by `gbrain serve`, the native CLI can return a structured `{"error":"pglite_busy"}` on stdout. The local-status detector only recognized legacy stderr/timeouts, so it could label a usable but temporarily locked local brain as broken and suppress brain-aware guidance. ## The fix Recognize the exact structured error on failed probes and classify it as `engine-locked` only for a configured PGLite engine. Existing remote-MCP fallback, malformed/unrelated responses, cache and `--is-ok` behavior remain intact. The regression drives the actual detector subprocess and isolated guidance renderer with busy and negative-control responses. ## Validation - Current `main` (`06ed920a`): pinned build and preflight passed; 128 focused tests passed, source unchanged. - Complete free suite: **25,517 pass, 0 fail, 59 skip** across 1,011 files; both shard logs copied and checksummed, source unchanged. - Staged diff: credential scan **0 high, 0 medium**; independent review found no actionable defect. The PR profile selects no live actor or judge for this two-file change. Two PGLite setup behaviors remain deferred periodic coverage, not passes. A real native `gbrain` lock emission was not exercised on this machine because the executable is unavailable. The test validates the detector’s handling of the documented structured CLI response, not the CLI’s emission or a model-driven workflow.

title: fix(browse): stop faking extension runtime messaging
body: ## The bug On pages without an installed extension, the stealth fallback invented callable `chrome.runtime.connect` and `sendMessage` functions. A site could mistake those stubs for a real extension and take an extension-only path that then throws. No specific SaaS login recovery is claimed from this synthetic reproduction. ## The fix Omit fabricated messaging methods from the fallback runtime while leaving a browser’s real existing extension APIs intact. The regressions compare stock Chromium with default stealth on a synthetic site and exercise an actual temporary MV3 extension to verify its native messaging functions survive. ## Validation - Current `main` (`06ed920a`): pinned build and headed Chromium preflight passed; 55 focused tests passed. - Complete free suite: **25,507 pass, 0 fail, 59 skip** across 1,010 files; both full shard logs copied and checksummed, source unchanged. - PR-profile live actors: `browse-basic`, `browse-snapshot`, and `diagram-triplet` executed and passed with zero skips. The selected `browse/SKILL.md reference` judge reuses a previously passing result after its complete 17,809-byte request, model, and rubric matched byte-for-byte; it was not resampled. - Complete staged diff: credential scan **0 high, 0 medium**; independent review found no actionable defect. The tests do not verify a production SaaS login, shipped gstack/GBrowser extension integration, or native macOS/Windows behavior. The dependent displayless-handoff repair will be a separate follow-up PR on this branch.

title: Fix displayless browser handoff ownership
body: ## The bug A headless browser started without `DISPLAY` could not open its headed handoff, and promotion did not reliably preserve the old browser or publish the new instance's display and headed state. An off-screen display is not a human-visible desktop; remote desktop access remains a separate requirement. ## The fix Allocate an owned Xvfb display lazily for headed launch or handoff, pass it to the headed Chromium process, and keep existing displays untouched. Serialize promotion, restore the previous browser on a failed launch or state restore, and close only owned browser/display resources on shutdown. Persist the promoted mode and display under the active instance's state lock; suppress parent-death shutdown after a successful promotion without disabling the tunnel orphan reaper. Tests exercise displayless and existing-display paths, rollback before and after launch, real Chromium handoff, instance-scoped state, and cleanup. This PR is the nine-file follow-up to #2953. The full validation source included that base's stealth fix; a standalone current-main run had one expected failure because it lacked the prerequisite. ## Validation - Frozen combined source on current `main` plus #2953: pinned build and headed Chromium preflight passed; **541 focused tests passed**, complete staged credential scan **0 high, 0 medium**; independent review cleared the final diff. - Complete free suite: **25,532 pass, 0 fail, 59 skip** across 1,010 files and 199,371 assertions. Both shard logs are retained and checksummed; source fingerprint `f5ddb80c` was unchanged and exactly matches this delivery branch's working tree. - Three selected live actors (`browse-basic`, `browse-snapshot`, `diagram-triplet`) executed and passed with zero skips. The selected browse reference judge reuses a previous passing result after its complete 17,809-byte model request and dependencies matched byte-for-byte; it was not resampled. No human-visible remote desktop, shipped extension or real SaaS login, native macOS/Windows/Wayland behavior, merge, or deployment is claimed.

title: fix(skills): preserve positional literals in installed workflows
body: ## The bug Claude Code expands bare numbered placeholders before an installed skill reaches the model, corrupting checksum extraction, upgrade snooze parsing, preview-port extraction, health diagnostics and instructions when invoked with arguments. On Windows, checksum output also escaped backslashes in the installer pathname and prefixed the digest, causing four native test failures. ## The fix Use equivalent shell/awk expressions without bare numbered placeholders and hash installer contents through stdin, so neither GNU sha256sum nor shasum formats the filename into the digest. Regenerate the three browser-skill consumers. The regression keeps the original raw paths and tests zero and ten arguments with ordinary and backslash-containing paths. On Windows, the fixture normalizes paths for Git Bash and tests the rendered `shasum -a 256` invocation through a checked shim backed by available `sha256sum`; Linux still executes both real checksum tools. ## Validation - Latest head `85082c7` has **39 passing CI checks, zero failures or pending**. The free gate accounted for all 1,011 files; `test/pty-output-wake.test.ts` failed one first attempt and passed its configured serial retry, which remains a recorded flake. - [Native Windows CI](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/36015568954) passed both curated shards (660 files). Git Bash on that runner has no native `shasum`; its fixture validates the rendered `shasum -a 256` invocation via an argument-checked shim backed by available `sha256sum`. Linux exercises both real checksum tools. The local focused/adjacent suite passed **559/559**. - The selected paid report reconciled **3/3 final results, 3 executed and 0 reused**; 26 broader behaviors remain deferred without PR-pass credit. The retained Windows evidence covers the curated Windows suite, not the complete test portfolio. Deployment fixtures simulate workflows; no real merge, deployment or rollback was performed. No merge or auto-merge is requested.

title: fix(design-detect): find impeccable installed as a Claude Code plugin
body:
## Why

`gstack-design-detect probe` only looks for impeccable under `~/.claude/skills/impeccable/`. Today the normal way to get impeccable is as a Claude Code plugin, which installs at `~/.claude/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/skills/impeccable/` instead — a path the probe never checks. So every plugin-installed user gets `IMPECCABLE_SKILL: absent`, never sees the `NOT_CACHED` run hint even though their own launcher is sitting right there, and the `/impeccable <cmd>` handoff in `/review`/`/ship`/`/design-review` never fires for them. This adds a plugin-cache walk alongside the existing one, sharing the same presence/launcher/repo-local-exclusion/sibling-engine logic so both paths behave identically.

## Live evidence

```
$ HOME=<fixture-home> IMPECCABLE_HOME=<fixture-home>/.impeccable-home \
  bun --no-env-file run bin/gstack-design-detect.ts probe

# before this fix (bin/gstack-design-detect.ts @ 06ed920a, same fixture):
IMPECCABLE_NOT_AVAILABLE
IMPECCABLE_SKILL: absent
IMPECCABLE_HOOK: absent
...

# after this fix:
IMPECCABLE_NOT_AVAILABLE
IMPECCABLE_SKILL: present
IMPECCABLE_HOOK: absent
...
```

Fixture: `<fixture-home>/.claude/plugins/cache/impeccable/impeccable/4.3.1/skills/impeccable/SKILL.md` — the exact layout from the issue's own repro.

```
$ bun test test/gstack-design-detect.test.ts -t "plugin-cache"
 4 pass
 0 fail
```

```
$ bun test test/gstack-design-detect.test.ts
 70 pass
 3 fail   # pre-existing on main, unrelated to this diff — confirmed via `git stash`
           # on 06ed920a before any changes: same 3 tests fail (macOS /var vs
           # /private/var realpath normalization + one timing-sensitive install test)
```

## Scope

- **Changed:** `bin/gstack-design-detect.ts` (plugin-cache walk + shared `checkSkillDir` extraction), `test/gstack-design-detect.test.ts` (4 new regression tests)
- **Verified live by:** running the compiled probe binary directly against a constructed plugin-cache fixture (before/after above), plus the full `gstack-design-detect.test.ts` suite
- **Did NOT test:** Windows (two of the four new tests are `skipIf(!POSIX)`, matching the file's existing pattern for launcher-execution tests); did not test against a real Claude Code plugin marketplace install, only the fixture layout the issue's reproduction documents

## Liveness proof (required for external contributors)

![liveness proof: GSTACK PR typed live into a terminal prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SomSamantray/gstack/356c33b178ba52990ab7e269a558495e0e8b6d86/.pr-assets/pr-2976-liveness.webp)

## Checklist

- [x] Liveness screenshot attached (`GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface) or PR author is @garrytan (owner exemption)
- [x] This is not a generated-file-only diff (I edited the source/template and regenerated)
- [x] No ETHOS.md edits, and no changes to voice / founder perspective / YC references
- [x] New public command / external service / host adapter has an accepted issue linked (or N/A) — N/A, no new command/service/adapter
- [x] Linked issue or reproduction: #2838

Fixes #2838

## Unapplied review findings

- [ ] P2 — `bin/gstack-design-detect.ts:39` — Plugin-cache walk picks an arbitrary (possibly stale) version, not the newest
  Suggested fix: in `pluginCacheImpeccableSkillDirs`, sort version entries with the same `semverKey` comparator `newestSemverDir` uses (or call `newestSemverDir(pluginDir)` and push only that version), so plugin-cache resolution gets the same newest-wins guarantee the rest of the file relies on.

title: /ship pre-landing review lacks /review's core shared-code pass and slop scan
body:
## Summary

`/ship`'s mandatory pre-landing review (Step 9) is missing two checks that standalone `/review` runs: the **core shared-code pass** and the **slop scan**. The shared-code gap also leaves `/ship`'s specialist prompts referring to a check that doesn't exist in `/ship`.

Because `/ship` does not treat a prior `/review` as a substitute ("This preflight snapshot does not replace Step 9's mandatory review", `ship/SKILL.md.tmpl`), a user who runs only `/ship` gets a review that covers less than `/review` in these two areas.

Verified against `main` at 2a113ae7 (v1.91.1.0).

## 1. Shared-code pass: `/ship` specialists are told to defer to a core check it doesn't have

- `/review` has a core "Shared-code opportunities" pass that runs on every diff, including small diffs and hosts without Review Army (`review/SKILL.md.tmpl:154`, `{{SHARED_LIBS_RUBRIC}}`).
- `/ship` has no equivalent. `ship/SKILL.md.tmpl` and `ship/sections/review-army.md.tmpl` do not include `{{SHARED_LIBS_RUBRIC}}` or a core shared-code step.
- But the `REVIEW_ARMY` resolver renders the same specialist instruction into both skills (`scripts/resolvers/review-army.ts:119`):

  > Optional extraction advice belongs to the core shared-code check; do not duplicate its proposals.

  It also refers to "core shared-code" at lines 179 and 215. In `/ship` (`ship/sections/review-army.md:305`, `:359`, `:395`), there is no core check, so specialists are told to hold back extraction proposals that nothing else produces.

As a result, `/ship` never produces new shared-code extraction advice. It still handles advisories correctly when they come from an earlier `/review`: Step 9.3 revalidates skipped ones through `sharedLibsFingerprint`, and `test/shared-libs-rendering.test.ts:68` pins that for `ship`. The v1.89.0.0 CHANGELOG limits the rubric to `/plan-eng-review` and `/review` ("Parent reviews using the shared-code rubric: 0 → 2"), so leaving `/ship` out may have been intentional. If so, the specialist prompt text is still wrong for `/ship`.

## 2. Slop scan runs only in `/review`

`/review` Step 3.5 runs `bun run slop:diff origin/<base>` as an advisory diagnostic (`review/SKILL.md.tmpl:112`). `/ship` has no equivalent step. The only "slop" text in `ship/` is the design-lite "AI Slop" line in the PR body template, which is about visual design.

This one is lower severity because the scan is advisory and never blocks.

## Checked and not a gap

To save triage time, these `/review`-only-looking steps are already covered elsewhere in `/ship`:

| `/review` step | Where `/ship` covers it |
|---|---|
| Scope drift | Step 8.2 (`ship/sections/plan-completion.md:309`) |
| TODOS cross-reference | Step 14 updates TODOS.md (marks completed items, adds approved deferrals) |
| Documentation staleness | Step 18 dispatches `/document-release` (updates docs rather than flagging) |
| Learnings search + log | Preamble and Steps 8, 9, and 11 (`gstack-learnings-search` / `gstack-learnings-log`) |

## Suggested fix

Move the core shared-code pass and the slop scan out of `review/SKILL.md.tmpl` into a shared section or resolver, and include it in both `/review` Step 4 and `/ship` Step 9. The `/ship` version should run before specialist dispatch, as `/review` does, so the resolver's "core shared-code check" text is accurate for both skills. A rendering test asserting that `ship` contains `### Shared-code evaluation rubric` (like the existing Codex `review` assertion) would stop this from drifting again.

If leaving `/ship` out is intentional, make the `REVIEW_ARMY` resolver render the "belongs to the core shared-code check" sentence only for skills that include the core pass.
